entry.title: 2024 Nicks Secret HBBS TL Barossa Shiraz
entry.summary:
From a producer renown for their blockbuster Barossa reds, this richly flavoured Shiraz has been made in an Amarone style whereby the grapes are rack dried to concentrate the fruit. The resulting wine was then matured in French oak for a period of 18 months. At over 50% off it delivers great value for those who like their Shiraz on the bigger side of town.

Rich, dense and concentrated with an opulent yet chewy mouth feel and power packed finish.

Magnificent colour density featuring a super saturated inky black heart along with an equally deep dark purple black hue. Peppery black cherry, black plum and liquorice scents infiltrate the olfactory senses followed by some fennel, scorched earth and spicy vanillin cedar notes. Rich, dense and concentrated, the full bodied palate is engulfed with lavish black cherry, liquorice and dark to black plum fruits. Opulent mouth feel with chewy, robust tannins providing structure. Spicy vanillin cedar, subtle scorched earth and peppered fennel characters extend across the back half. Power packed it finishes with great density, length and succulence.
Drink over the next 6 years.
Alc. 14.8%

Other Reviews....
A strikingly modern Barossa Shiraz that bursts from the glass with freshness, clarity and energy. Blueberry and dark berry fruits lead the way, vibrant and pure, before subtle notes of espresso bean, spice and crushed mineral detail add depth and sophistication.
The palate is bright, juicy and mouth-wateringly delicious, with beautifully handled fruit intensity balanced by a lively lift and fine savoury edge. There is a polished contemporary feel here, but still plenty of Barossa generosity, carried by excellent freshness and a long, moreish finish. A superb Shiraz with real style and precision.
96 Points
Vino Masters

Deep crimson. Attractive panforte, ripe plum, praline, liquorice aromas. Deeply concentrated yet lithe in structure with ample panforte/ Christmas cake, dark chocolate, liquorice, hint rum and raisin flavours, fine dense chalky tannins and underlying wax varnish notes. Finishes firm and crispy tight. Now2036.
95 points
The Vintage Journal Barossa Guide 2026

entry.title: 2006 Signatory Vintage Glenlivet 19 Year Old Cask Strength Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary: Knowing how good Glenlivet can be from Signatory, we've secured a little more of this than some of the other bottlings in the latest shipment. Also, we're back to a world where Signatory is a leader in both price and quality, so the confidence is high and the risk is low. Some of these au naturale Glenlivets are known to be clean and refreshing, others extremely complex with an old school vibe, especially when they're out of sherry, like this is. It could reasonably sell for more, but we're passing on the savings to move it fast. 522 bottles were drawn from a first-fill oloroso sherry butt. 58.7% Alc./Vol. Non-chill-filtered.

entry.title: 2023 Cape Mentelle Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Mid weighted with a gently creamed feel and long generously fleshed yet refined conclusion.

Wild fermented in French oak barriques then given a further 8 months maturation. Brilliant pale straw colour with glimmering green tinted edges and a watery hue. Aromas of nectarine, pear and biscuity oak mingle with citrus and gun flint notes. Rich nectarine, pear and dried honey fruits carry a gentle creamed feel across the mid weighted palate. Biscuity oak and infusions of gun flint extend across the back half. Fresh underlying acidity with a long generously fleshed yet refined conclusion.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.4%

Other Reviews..
Gee this is good. It's moreish and savoury, with plenty of flavour yet a certain level of restraint as well. The spicy oak lightly coats the lemon and grapefruit, there's some ginger tea, and lemon curd and clotted cream lees add texture across the palate. Fine acidity ensures a fresh finish and gets you ready for the next sip. Drink by 2033.
95 Points
Jane Faulkner - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: Boatrocker Four Grain Overproof Australian Whisky (500ml) - 50%
entry.summary:
A higher-ABV expression of the Melbourne-based distillery's bourbon-style whisk(e)y. Bottled at 50% ABV rather than the standard 40%, it maintains the 51% corn, 31% rye, 6% barley and 12% wheat mash bill with aging in high-char virgin American oak. Biscuity malt, light rye and Bourbon wood feature in the off-dry nose, the other grains granted a lesser showing; Medium bodied, cereal-forward flavours develop with a spicy edge; discreet, oily rye competes with rich oak in a chewy finish. Better balanced sweet'n'spicy Australian whisky would be hard to name. 50% Alc./Vol.

Notes from the producers... Expect bold yet balanced notes of vanillin and brown sugar, sweetness from the corn, gentle rye spice and a hint of mint on the nose. Great to drink neat with a drop of water, or as a base in spirit forward cocktails.

entry.title: 2024 Envinate Lousas Vinas de Aldea Mencia
entry.summary:
Lousas is the name Envintate has given to their wines from Ribeira Sacra, translating to slate and a nod to the rock that marks these wines. Each of their Lousas releases are predominantly Mencia, along with a smaller component of various indigenous varieties such as Merenzao, Caino, Garnacha Tintorerra, and Palomino among many others.

Vina de Aldea is a blend of several plots from the Amandi, Quiroga, and Ribeiras do Sil subregions of Ribeira Sacra. Doad meanwhile hails from different terroirs throughout the Galician town of Doade, is Mencia dominant with the remaining 15% a field blend of various varieties. Rosende is sourced from a single vineyard from a village of the same name, and the soils here are similar to the Northern Rhone with granite crystals flecked through the sand. Finally the single vinyard pair of Seoane and Camino Novo perched on the edge of the River Sil, each featuring vines over 80 years old. While similarly located these two are very different in style, Seoane being the more lifted, elegant and immediately attractive, whereas Camino Novo is more brooding and often one of the most profound Mencia in the area.

Other Reviews...
Herbal, bloody and ferrous, with dark and wild berries. The palate is medium-bodied with focused, nervy tannins and incisive acidity, showing a more mellow profile than the 2023, with a fluid, slightly more ethereal expression of fruit. From multiple plots in Amandi, Quiroga and the Mio area, each vinified separately with varying proportions of whole bunches. Aged mostly in barrique with a smaller proportion in cement. Drink or hold.
96 points
Jacobo Garca Andrade - JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2023 Donnhoff Oberhauser Brucke Riesling Auslese Goldkapsel (375ml)
entry.summary:
Donnhoff make the best wines in the Nahe region, and some of the finest anywhere in the world. While it was Helmut Donnhoff that launched this estate to worldwide attention, winemaking duties are now managed by his talented son, Cornelius. There's a deep understanding of the grand wines and grand vineyards that's been handed down through the generations. And given the enormous technical proficiency Cornelius has demonstrated so far, Donnhoff is sure to be at the top of the vinous hierarchy for years to come.

An exclusive monopole of the estate, the steep, slate-rich Oberhauser Brucke vineyard sits on a distinct river bend that yields some of Germany's most coveted Pradikat Rieslings. Its Spatlese and Auslese balance electrifying mineral acidity with lush fruit sweetness, delivering an effortless harmony of weightless power, purity, and decades-long cellaring potential.

Other Reviews...
Auslese might sound cuddly to some, but this is a very radical wine with gigantic concentration of cool tropical fruit and mineral acidity. Electric glide on the medium- to full-bodied palate. The finish is all blue and green in spite of the extraordinary yellow fruit on the nose and front palate. And with that, only the most basic characteristics of this extraordinary wine are adequately described. Drink or hold.
99 points
JamesSuckling.com

The 2023 Riesling Oberhuser Brcke Auslese is made from mostly highly ripe grapes with around 10-15% of botrytized fruit, all pressed in a basket press, slowly, over hours, drip by drip is extracted, without rupturing the grape skins. The tender nose is not obvious; it shows distant notions of iced Reine Claude compote with an overtone of passion fruit foliage; all is lemony and tender. The palate is sweet, bright and concentrated, but it has a slender, taut footprint. Extreme elegance is the name of the game, and the tenor is still of fresh lemon juice and zest. Restraint and elegance are exemplified here. Drink 2034-2070.
96 points
Anne Krebiehl MW - Vinous

entry.title: 2025 Kooyong Clonale Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Concentrated and gently creamy texturally, it shows great refinement across the long finish.

The Clonale Chardonnay is sourced from Kooyongs Tuerong and Balnarring vineyards and is matured in a mixture of French oak barriques and puncheons (14% new) for a period of 9 months.
Brilliant pale straw colour with green tinted edges and a watery hue. Delightful white peach, dried honey and nectarine aromas drift through the nostrils trailed by biscuity nougat, subtle cashew and spice notes. Refined in nature yet impressing with its richness and textural properties, delicious white peach, nectarine, dried honey, biscuity nougat, delicate cashew and spice flavours flow seamlessly across the mid weighted palate. Perfectly balanced acidity with a long gently creamed finish. A very impressive Chardonnay for the price.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13%

entry.title: 2024 Joh Jos Prum Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Auslese Goldkapsel
entry.summary:
The Wehlener Sonnenuhr vineyard has become intrinsically tied to the name of Joh. Jos. Prum. The estate owns seven hectares of this majestic site, which is largely planted with ungrafted vines and features very thin topsoil over Devonian slate (in some areas, the plants grow directly out of pure rock). Wehlener Sonnenuhr has the highest pure stone content of all the Prum vineyards and, along with neighbouring Zeltingen, is the steepest, boasting a dizzying 65 to 70 percent gradient. The forest resting above the vineyard also acts as a natural water regulator for the slope.

Other Reviews...
The 2024 Wehlener Sonnenuhr Auslese (Gold Capsule) offers a clear, deep and concentrated, remarkably complex and saline nose with intense fruit and even floral aromas. Light yet intense and with a certain phenolic grip, this is a tightly meshed, age-worthy and sustainably structured Riesling that will surely benefit from further bottle aging. 7.5% stated alcohol. Natural cork. Tasted at the domaine from AP 15 25 in March 2026. Drink 2031-2080.
98 points
Stephan Reinhardt - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2024 Riesling Wehlener Sonnenuhr Auslese Goldkapsel is alive with citrus foliage, zest and the sweetest fruit aromas. Its tanginess tingles on the nose and continues right on the palate. Vivid freshness and poise define pale white peach flesh on the palate, tempered by a gorgeous, tangy orange peel note that attains a subtle edge of candy. The 2024 is superbly fine, stony, linear and, of course, delicious. It is so poised and clean. Drink 2030-2065.
97 points
Anne Krebiehl MW - Vinous

This smells like an entire florists store, but theres nothing overpowering about it at all. Very concentrated and complete, with fantastic floral honey richness and great underlying freshness, this is a very great Mosel Auslese. Still only medium-bodied in spite of the generous unfermented grape sweetness, and so incredibly clean and pure in the super-long finish. Drink or hold.
97 points
JamesSuckling.com

The 2024 is superbly fine, stony, linear and, of course, delicious. It is so poised and clean. Drink 2030-2065.
97 points
Anne Krebiehl MW - Vinous

This smells like an entire florists store, but theres nothing overpowering about it at all. Very concentrated and complete, with fantastic floral honey richness and great underlying freshness, this is a very great Mosel Auslese. Still only medium-bodied in spite of the generous unfermented grape sweetness, and so incredibly clean and pure in the super-long finish. Drink or hold.
97 points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2024 Envinate Parcela Palo Blanco Las Molinas
entry.summary:
Migan and Palo Blanco are both very old vine wines from the Valle de la Orotava zone, although they dont bear the D.O. stamp. The old vines are trained in the Trezendo fashion: braiding new shoots over older ones until the vines begin to resemble old dreadlocks weaving over the landscape. The terrain is flatter than Tganan, more conducive to farming. 2023 Las Molinas is the second vintage of this single parcel wine from a centenarian plot of ungrafted, pre-phylloxera vines that had formerly been included in the Palo Blanco bottling. Fermented and aged in a single neutral oak foudre of 2500 liters.

Other Reviews...
The 2024 Palo Blanco Las Molinas comes from a year with a homogeneous and normal production and also homogeneous ripeness. The wine is healthy and clean, and it achieved very good ripeness and kept very good freshness. It matured in a 20-year-old Italian foudre where it went through full malolactic. It's still a baby, with a bright and pale color and a slightly reductive nose, which I guess is a bit dizzy from the recent bottling. It has notes of struck match and a core of dry herbs, spices and flowers. It comes in at 12% alcohol, with a pH of 3.2 and 7.32 grams of acidity. It is vibrant and pungent, with great depth and complexity. It is long, dry and tasty, with a strong mineral sensation in the finish that is crunchy and salty. This should age magnificently in bottle. 2,000 bottles produced, a little less than in 2023, but they used more of this for the regular Palo Blanco blend. This It was bottled in July 2025. Drink 2025-2034.
99 points
Luis Gutirrez - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This has a very unique nose, with a citric lime-like element, a subtle toasty note as well as a wet stone, austere-like note. The palate is vibrant and austere but with a touch of flesh, complemented by a saline, nervy note. Despite being austere, it is almost mouthwatering. Vibrant, saline and with a subtle, almost ethereal quality as well. This comes from a small parcel of centenary listan blanco in Los Realejos. Whole-cluster press, fermentation in concrete and aging in 2500 L foudre. Drink or hold.
96 points
Jacobo Garca Andrade - JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2025 Rising Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
A savoury red to dark fruited Yarra Valley Pinot that carries a supple feel.

Red to dark red colour with black toned edges and a red tinged hue. Amplified scents of violet, dark cherry and strawberry enchant the olfactory senses with some anise, dried herb, forest floor and spice notes also evident. Delicious red to dark cherry and strawberry fruits flow across the palate with a supple feel. Also chiming in are subtle rhubarb, spicy dried herb and forest floor characters. Polished tannins with ample power to the savoury finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 13.2%

entry.title: 2024 Grampians Estate Woolclasser’s GST
entry.summary:
Rich and succulent with velvety tannins and ample freshness.

A blend of 50% Grenache, 40% Shiraz and 10% Tempranillo. Deep dark red black tinged colour with a purple red hue. Fragrant dark raspberry, liquorice, dark cherry and red plum scents sail out of the glass trailed by some earthy incense and peppered herb notes. Rich and succulent, the mid weighted palate is doused with dark raspberry, liquorice and dark cherry fruits. Earthy incense infusions and delicate spicy pepper elements linger underneath. Velvet smooth tannins with good freshness carried across the long juicy finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14%

entry.title: 2022 Oliver’s Taranga Vineyards Shiraz - DAMAGED LABEL

Dense pitch black core with a very deep dark red black hue. Elevated ripe blackberry, dark plum and liquorice scents are trailed by vanillin oak, hints of mocha, earth and pepper. Drink over the next 5-6 years.

entry.title: 2025 Dog Point Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc
entry.summary:
Showing outstanding intensity and drive, this super scrumptious Sauvignon Blanc is one of New Zealands best.

Sourced from eight estate-owned vineyards within the Wairau Valley with vines on average 28 years old. The fruit is whole bunch pressed to tank for fermentation and matured on lees for 5 months before bottling.
Brilliant very pale straw almost water like core with green tinged surrounds. Pungent nose with aromas of passionfruit, gooseberry and kiwi fruit leaping out of the glass. Some herbaceous grassy, grapefruit and flinty mineral notes are also evident. Super scrumptious, the palate is lined with zesty passionfruit, gooseberry and kiwi fruit flavours with some subtle herbaceous characters, lime and mineral elements lying underneath. Showing outstanding intensity and drive it finishes with crisp acidity and a long lip-smacking finish.
Drink over the next 1-2 years.
Alc. 12.5%

Other Reviews.
A wine that catches you off guard with its familiar waft of candle wax and sparkler flint. Theres a wistful white floral aroma of frangipani and freesia drawing you in. As it opens, notes of pomelo, white pear and pineapple emerge. The wine then lights up like fireworks the soft, sparkling kind revealing hints of lemonade, yellow melon and a glittering acidity that is carefully bridled. Nuances of celery heart and fresh ginger follow, adding complexity. It is exquisite in its balance teetering tropical notes, the fragility of herbal suggestion and an utterly moreish finish. Drink by 2032.
97 Points
Shanteh Wale - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2025 Forest Hill Vineyard Chardonnay
entry.summary:
A fresh, well fleshed Chardonnay that displays good length.

Sourced from three sites on the Forest Hill Vineyard, Block 8 and Block 9 planted in 1985 and Highbury Fields with maturation taking place in French oak (20% new).
Brilliant pale straw colour with green toned edges and a watery hue. Uplifted nectarine, white peach and dried honey aromas fill the nostrils with whiffs of cashew, citrusy nougat and gun flint also chiming in. Mid weighted the palate is lined with white peach, nectarine and citrus fruits. Lively acidity with biscuity nougat, dried honey and spice elements extending across the back half. Fresh, well fleshed finish of good length.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 13%

entry.title: 2024 Samuel Billaud Chablis Les Grands Terroirs
entry.summary:
While the origins of this domaine date back to Charles-Louis-Noel Billaud in 1815, it's the current generation winemaker Samuel Billaud that has made waves with the exceptional quality of his wines produced since the creation of this project in 2009. Following the sale of the family business Domaine Billaud-Simon to Faiveley in 2014, Samuel received further prized parcels of land and now makes wines from five of the grand cru vineyards, and five of the top premier cru vineyards. The wines are vinified in a mixture of stainless steel and large old wood barrels, the latter mainly for the premier and grand cru wines.

Other Reviews...
The 2024 Chablis Grands Terroirs comes across as quite austere on the nose, with wet pavement and gunflint scents. The palate is fresh on the entry, with Granny Smith apple and lime, fine tension and a cohesive, persistent finish. Drink over five to ten years. Drink 2026-2033.
90 points
Neal Martin - Vinous

Pure, precise and driven, with mineral and crystalline aromas. Very clean, transparent and modern, with medium body and a slightly mineral and peachy finish. Tank sample. Some CO2 at this stage trims it down. Quite acid-driven finish with salinity. Will be bottled in June. Drink from 2027.
91-92 points
Zekun Shuai - JamesSuckling.com

Demonstrates a mastery of the difficult 2024 vintage with its charming aromas of citrus fruit and fresh white flowers, accented by chalky minerality. The texture balances fresh acidity with enough richness and concentration to satisfy Chablis lovers. The grapes are from both vineyards that Samuel Billaud owns and those he sources from left-bank sites including Pargues near Prhy and the cooler back of the Montmain slope in the lieux-dits of Fontenottes and Les Cartes, and grapes from lieu-dit Chapelot on the right bank. Drink 2026-2031.
91 points
Charles Curtis MW - Decanter

Made from the usual three locations. 25 hl/ha on average. A little bready yeast note on the nose along with its more classical components. Wonderful tension behind. The they dont make Chablis like they used to grumblers should be satisfied. Crisp citrus notes infuse the finish. Drink from 2027-2030.
90-92 points
Jasper Morris MW - Inside Burgundy

entry.title: 2023 Haan Estate Shiraz

Plush with rich blue to black fruit and a relatively refined finish.

Matured in a combination of new and old French oak barrels. Impenetrable inky black in colour with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Generous aromas of liquorice and dark plum sail through the nostrils followed by some gentle smoky vanillin cedar, fennel and peppered earth notes. Rich dark plum, liquorice and ripe blueberry fruits carry a plush feel across the medium to full bodied palate. Smoky fennel, vanillin cedar and peppered earth elements sit in the background. Polished tannins with a well fleshed yet relatively refined finish of good length.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 15%

entry.title: 2024 Blue Gables Jesse Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Fresh and elegant with a gently creamy yet tense finish.

Brilliant pale straw colour with green tinged edges and a watery hue. Aromas of nectarine and lemon butter intermingle with roasted almond and gun flint notes. Toasty flavours of nectarine and lemon butter line the palate with roasted almond, biscuit and gun flint accents also chiming in. Fresh acidity with an elegant, gently creamy yet tense finish.
Drink over the next 3-4 years.
Alc. 13.3%

Other Reviews
Jeez, Jesse has found its groove of late and this is another excellent one. Its flinty, with moreish sulphides (not too much, just the right amount). Its all citrusy, spicy and vivacious, with mouth-watering acidity. Next some appealing cedary oak and lemon curd lees fill the palate. This is quite a linear, tight style and so delicious as a result. Drink by 2032.
95 Points
Jane Faulkner - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2024 Sangreal By Farr Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Deeply concentrated and powerful this a highly seductive Sangreal.

Planted in 1994, Sangreal is By Farr's oldest vineyard, lying on a north-facing slope with bluestone and limestone soils streaked with red ironstone. Its unique northsouth orientation and long exposure to sunlight produce Pinot Noir of lift, perfume, and seamless elegance. Over the decades, the 114 and 115 clones have evolved into what the Farrs call the "Sangreal clone," giving this site its own microclimate identity. Sangreal is consistently made with 70 per cent whole bunch and aged in 70 percent new oak.

Deep dark red colour with black toned edges and a red tinged hue. Displaying a wonderful combination of potency and complexity, the nose is filled with violet, spicy red to dark cherry, wild strawberry, clove, forest floor, brambly earth and spicy cedar notes. Deeply concentrated and powerful, a tidal wave of spicy dark cherry, strawberry and more subtle brambly rhubarb like flavours are layered across the palate. Juicy and supple yet also fresh, earthy forest floor, clove and spicy cedar elements linger across the back half. Seamless tannin integration with an exceptionally long and expansive finish. A highly seductive Sangreal.
Drink over the next 8-10 years.
Alc. 14%
entry.g:title: 2024 Sangreal By Farr Pinot Noir
entry.g:description:
Deeply concentrated and powerful this a highly seductive Sangreal.

Planted in 1994, Sangreal is By Farr's oldest vineyard, lying on a north-facing slope with bluestone and limestone soils streaked with red ironstone. Its unique northsouth orientation and long exposure to sunlight produce Pinot Noir of lift, perfume, and seamless elegance. Over the decades, the 114 and 115 clones have evolved into what the Farrs call the "Sangreal clone," giving this site its own microclimate identity. Sangreal is consistently made with 70 per cent whole bunch and aged in 70 percent new oak.

Deep dark red colour with black toned edges and a red tinged hue. Displaying a wonderful combination of potency and complexity, the nose is filled with violet, spicy red to dark cherry, wild strawberry, clove, forest floor, brambly earth and spicy cedar notes. Deeply concentrated and powerful, a tidal wave of spicy dark cherry, strawberry and more subtle brambly rhubarb like flavours are layered across the palate. Juicy and supple yet also fresh, earthy forest floor, clove and spicy cedar elements linger across the back half. Seamless tannin integration with an exceptionally long and expansive finish. A highly seductive Sangreal.
Drink over the next 8-10 years.
Alc. 14%

entry.title: 2005 Signatory Vintage Orkney 20 (HP) Cask No: DRU 17/A63 #2 20 Year Old Cask Strength Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary:
"It grabbed me from the very first dram... an absolute no brainer." - whiskybase.com

At the price, there's absolutely no reason to hold back on this value Highland Park. All the Orcadian hallmarks will be here - warm honey canopied by rich oak, a drift of peat and soft sea breeze These natural strength bottlings can be amazingly concentrated yet graceful spirits. Signatory have opted for a little extra complexity and richness with elevage in a first-fill oloroso butt. 608 bottles were decanted at 55.2% Alc./Vol. Non chill filtered.

Other reviews... Beautiful aromas that successfully vary the familiar Orkney theme without to lose sight of it. It grabbed me from the very first dram. Floral honey on the nose then soft sherry on palate. Great balance between distillate and cask. - whiskybase.com

...A very pleasant surprise. Slightly smoky and full-bodied. Needs a few minutes in the glass. It opens up further with water, which I really liked. For [the price], it's an absolute no-brainer. - whiskybase.com

entry.title: 2024 Envinate Lousas Parcela Camino Novo Mencia
entry.summary:
Lousas is the name Envintate has given to their wines from Ribeira Sacra, translating to slate and a nod to the rock that marks these wines. Each of their Lousas releases are predominantly Mencia, along with a smaller component of various indigenous varieties such as Merenzao, Caino, Garnacha Tintorerra, and Palomino among many others.

Vina de Aldea is a blend of several plots from the Amandi, Quiroga, and Ribeiras do Sil subregions of Ribeira Sacra. Doad meanwhile hails from different terroirs throughout the Galician town of Doade, is Mencia dominant with the remaining 15% a field blend of various varieties. Rosende is sourced from a single vineyard from a village of the same name, and the soils here are similar to the Northern Rhone with granite crystals flecked through the sand. Finally the single vinyard pair of Seoane and Camino Novo perched on the edge of the River Sil, each featuring vines over 80 years old. While similarly located these two are very different in style, Seoane being the more lifted, elegant and immediately attractive, whereas Camino Novo is more brooding and often one of the most profound Mencia in the area.

Other Reviews...
Ferric, asphalt with wild berries and a pleasant herbal touch. The palate is medium-bodied, detailed, with subtle fruit, focused tannins and linear brightness to complement. This comes from a single vineyard planted on the banks of the Sil river in the upper part of Doade. Drink or hold.
98 points
Jacobo Garca Andrade - JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: Mery Melrose The Old Alliance Classic Single Malt French Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary: A single malt made from organic barley malted and kilned by La Malterie de l'Ouest, then distilled in a Charentais alembic traditionally used for cognac. Five years in oak was followed by a secondary maturation in the estate's own 10-year-old Pineau des Charentes casks. Mouth-filling, textural and beautifully rounded flavours conjure oatmeal biscuits and honey-drizzled bircher muesli, extended by a splash of sweet dried fruits and chocolate (no doubt from the finishing casks). Re-tasted after five minutes' air contact, it leaves the impression of a buxom young cognac. The name references the Auld Alliance, the 1295 treaty between France and Scotland, a nod to the estate's dual French-Scottish heritage. 46% Alc./Vol. Non-chill filtered. 30ml sample.

entry.title: 2024 Envinate La Santa de Ursula Tinto
entry.summary:
La Santa de Ursula is a new bottling from the northeast coast of Tenerife in an area called La Carujera, part of the Tacoronte-Acentejo appellation. Its a blend of three parcels of 100+ year old vines planted on sandy clay over red basalt bedrock, situated between 350m and 650m above sea level. The blend is 48% Negramoll, 50% Listn Negro, and 2% Listn Blanco, which are vinified partially with whole clusters in cement and aged in small neutral oak barrels. Bottling is without fining or filtration, and only a small addition of sulfur.

Other Reviews...
The 2024 La Santa de rsula has to be the finest vintage for this red from the zone of Tacoronte-Acentejo, and this year, it breaks down to 77% Listn Negro, 20% Negramoll and 3% Listn Blanco. There was a fire in the zone in 2023, and 2024 was dry and healthyit's a humid zone that's prone to illnesseswith a good yield (10% less than in 2023) and balance. The wine has a perfumed nose, with high aromatic intensity and the spiciness that is so classical here, with depth and complexity. It comes in at 12% alcohol, with a pH of 3.33 and 6.18 grams of acidity. It has a medium-bodied palate with fine tannins, and it is stony and serious, with more elegance and finesse, like an improved version of 2021. 5,700 bottles produced. It was bottled in July 2025. Drink 2026-2032.
97 points
Luis Gutirrez - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

This has a very attractive nose of pepper, burnt sesame seed and crunchy wild berries with a herbal touch. Medium-bodied with stimulating acidity, fresh and vibrant, with nervy tannins. Ethereal with a savory touch. A blend of 48% negramoll, 50% listan negro and 2% listan blanco. Drink now.
95 points
Jacobo Garca Andrade - JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2014 Edradour 200th Anniversary 11 Year Old PX Sherry Cask Small Batch Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary: A new 2026 batch of Edradour's PX Sherry Cask lands, one year older than the previous offering. Andrew Symington's signature flourish places impact before elegance in a whisky matured entirely in first-fill Pedro Ximnez (sweet) sherry butts to mark the distillery's bicentennial. Offering a decadent profile of molasses, jammy stewed fruits, earthy malt, and a warm baking spice kick at a price that's completely accessible, it will be your fireside companion, a fine dessert whisky or a preferred dram for whenever you feel like spoiling yourself. This style isn't for everyone, but it is a rallying call to fans of sherried malts longing for the bargains of yesteryear. 46% Alc./Vol. Non chill filtered and natural in colour.

entry.title: 2023 Escarpment NOIR Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
A fresh, elegant red fruited Pinot Noir.

Semi translucent red to dark red colour with a light red hue. Spicy red to dark cherry, strawberry and red liquorice aromas flow through the nostrils followed by some clove and forest floor notes. entry.title: 2025 Fighting Gully Road Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Light, fresh and elegant with a supple flow of red fruits.

This delicious Pinot Noir was made from two clones (114 and MV6) and comprises a whole bunch component, which was fermented separately using maceration carbonique. Each component was matured separately in new (40%) and seasoned Italian coopered French oak 500 litre puncheons for a period of 12 months.

Dark red core with black toned edges and a red to dark red hue. Perfumed like aromas of violet, dark cherry and wild strawberry mix with hints of anise, clove, bramble, cedar, forest floor and spice. Delicious dark cherry, strawberry and rhubarb fruits flow supplely across the palate with notions of brambly cedar, dried herbs, forest floor and spice lending further interest across the back half. Polished tannins finishing long, fresh and elegant.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13%

entry.title: 1960 The Last Drop Blended Scotch Whisky (700ml) - Plus 50ml bottle
entry.summary:
Note: Product has come from a private collection and as such has some minor scuffing/scratches/handling marks. Actual product pictured.

The Last Drop was founded by three industry veterans who set out to track down extraordinary old stocks in forgotten cellars in order to bring whiskies of both great age and exceptional quality to the market. What can only be described as an obsession, they've committed a significant amount of time and energy scouring Scotland for buried treasure.

Reportedly made from around 70 different malt and 12 different grain whiskies, many of which are from silent distilleries, the inaugural release from The Last Drop takes its namesake to the next level. With the youngest whisky in the blend being 48 years old, when bottled in 2008, this is a serious step into the past for any whisky enthusiast. Only 1347 bottles were produced, each with its own 50ml miniature for the ultimate drinker/collector experience. Very rare. 52% Alc./Vol.

Tasted prior to Australian release: Slightly dull, deep orange/sienna brown colour with a viscous appearance. The nose is profound - shellac top note, then surprisingly Bourbon-like with deep vanilla cream and brandy sauce aromas. The palate takes an unexpected turn from the nose, with a silky glycerous entry followed by an intense, slow explosion of dried apricots and prunes over old, slow-burning oak smoke. Fantastic balance. Pronounced warming spirit glow followed by a long, soft aftertaste of smoky oak, nougat & cloves. This is all about incredible depth that only whiskies of this venerable age seem to attain.

entry.title: 2022 Brini Blewitt Springs Single Vineyard Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich and sumptuous with blackberry, liquorice, dark plum and dark chocolate flavours carrying a plush feel.

Matured in French and American oak. Dense inky black in colour with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Elevated blackberry, liquorice and dark plum aromas are intermeshed with toasty vanillin oak, hints of earthy dark chocolate and peppered fennel notes. Rich, sumptuous blackberry, liquorice, dark plum and dark chocolate flavours carry a plush feel across the palate. Toasty vanillin oak, earth and peppered fennel elements line the back half. Polished yet sturdy tannin structure. Showing impressive depth and power it finishes long and opulent.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14.5%

entry.title: 2024 Joh Jos Prum Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Auslese (375ml)
entry.summary:
The Wehlener Sonnenuhr vineyard has become intrinsically tied to the name of Joh. Jos. Prum. The estate owns seven hectares of this majestic site, which is largely planted with ungrafted vines and features very thin topsoil over Devonian slate (in some areas, the plants grow directly out of pure rock). Wehlener Sonnenuhr has the highest pure stone content of all the Prum vineyards and, along with neighbouring Zeltingen, is the steepest, boasting a dizzying 65 to 70 percent gradient. The forest resting above the vineyard also acts as a natural water regulator for the slope.

Other Reviews...
The 2024 Wehlener Sonnenuhr Auslese offers a remarkably fine and sophisticated nose of crushed slate, salt, blackcurrant, peach and lemon rind. The wine is filigreed yet intense and persistently saline, dense, complex and very long. This is a fabulous, highly digestible Riesling Auslese from one of the Moselle's most famous crus. AP 12 25. 7.5% stated alcohol. Natural cork. Tasted at the domaine in March 2026. Drink 2026-2070.
96 points
Stephan Reinhardt - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2024 Riesling Wehlener Sonnenuhr Auslese, without any botrytis to speak of, flirts with peach bathed in orange zest with a gorgeous frisson of bergamot. It has a serene sweetness, delving deep into ripe, golden peach flesh. The 2024 is gorgeously framed with tangy citrus on a beautifully contoured body that is so racy, sleek and smooth. What a class act. Drink 2030-2065.
97 points
Anne Krebiehl MW - Vinous

The interplay of white peach and complex floral flavors with salty minerality makes this Auslese really stand out. Concentrated but also very vibrant on the medium-bodied palate. Extremely long, salty finish with great drive and raciness. Drinkable now, but best from 2027.
96 points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2024 Quealy Tussie Mussie Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Light, fresh and supple with an elegant red fruited finish.

Slightly cloudy red colour with a light red hue. Fragrant violet, red cherry and winter strawberry scents are trailed by some forest floor, rhubarb, dried herb and spice notes. Light, fresh and supple, red cherry, winter strawberry and rhubarb fruits are detailed across the palate. Forest floor, fresh herb and spice elements linger across the back half. Energetic acidity and refined tannins with a long, elegant red fruited finish that has a sense of vibrancy to it.
Drink over the next 3-4 years.
Alc. 13.8%

Other Reviews.
Such expressive aromas with pinot from the 24 vintage, although Tussie Mussie tends to be particularly pretty. Florals, autumn leaves, Angostura bitters, poached rhubarb and strawberry conserve with the requisite cherry accents. It feels light and bright, some grip to the tannins, while a smidge of green walnut on the finish detracts. Still, sweet fruit comes through, and acidity leads the charge. Drink by 2032.
94 Points
Jane Faulkner - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2021 Patrick of Coonawarra Home Block Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
Rich, concentrated and fleshy textured with a long, deeply fruited conclusion.

Matured for 2 years in a combination of French and American oak. Impenetrable inky black heart with a very deep dark red black hue. Intense aromas of blackcurrant and dark chocolate flood the olfactory senses with some mulberry, vanillin cedar, earth and subtle mint notes ensuing. Rich, concentrated and fleshy textured, the medium bodied palate has generous layers of black currant, dark cherry and dark chocolate flowing across it. Sitting in the background are spicy vanillin cedar, subtle earthy mocha and delicate tobacco elements. Fine grained tannins with a long, deeply fruited conclusion.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 13.8%

Other Reviews.
Sourced from 60-year-old vines. Two years in oak, followed by three years resting in the cool of their cellars. A pretty iteration of the Home Block this vintage, with lavender and blackberry buds, dried blueberries and dark cherries. The spice threads come from black soils, tree bark and fine-grained oak. There is a hazelnut cream delicacy on the mid-palate. It's youthful and deftly stitched. Drink by 2035.
95 Points
Shanteh Wale - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2024 Farrside By Farr Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Light and supple in its flow with a smoky, bramble like complexity and long, expansive finish.

Planted in 2001 on a northeast-facing slope of dark volcanic soils over limestone, the Farrside vineyard produces a more structured and brooding style of Pinot Noir compared to its Sangreal counterpart. Hand-picked and wild-fermented, the fruit sees partial whole bunch inclusion before maturing in 5060% new Allier oak.

Red to dark red in colour with black toned edges and a light red to darker red hue. Intense red cherry, violet and wild strawberry scents infused with dried clove sail out of the glass trailed by some complexing rhubarb, bramble, forest floor and spice notes. Light and supple in its flow, a power wave of red to dark cherry, strawberry, rhubarb, bramble and clove flavours fan out across the palate like a peacocks tail. Forest floor, smoked meat and spicy cedar elements lend further sophistication. Wonderful balance and freshness with seamlessly integrated, fine grained tannins and a long, expansive finish.
Drink over the next 8-10 years.
Alc. 14%

entry.title: 2024 Joh Jos Prum Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Kabinett Magnum (1500ml)
entry.summary:
The Wehlener Sonnenuhr vineyard has become intrinsically tied to the name of Joh. Jos. Prum. The estate owns seven hectares of this majestic site, which is largely planted with ungrafted vines and features very thin topsoil over Devonian slate (in some areas, the plants grow directly out of pure rock). Wehlener Sonnenuhr has the highest pure stone content of all the Prum vineyards and, along with neighbouring Zeltingen, is the steepest, boasting a dizzying 65 to 70 percent gradient. The forest resting above the vineyard also acts as a natural water regulator for the slope.

Other Reviews...
The 2024 Wehlener Sonnenuhr Kabinett displays lovely fruit intensity with subtle earthy notes, floral nuances and a hint of reduction. Full-bodied, juicy and piquantly racy on the palate, this is a fresh, elegant and ever-light-footed Kabinett yet with a sensual, juicy character. This is AP 05 25. 8.5% stated alcohol. Natural cork. Tasted at the domaine in March 2026. Drink 2026-2050.
92 points
Stephan Reinhardt - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2024 Riesling Wehlener Sonnenuhr Kabinett opens with subtle hints of creamy woodruff, candied angelica and wet slate. The palate is lightness itself, like a veil of scented fruit referencing green apple, supple, sweet but tart citrus, like juicy, pale pomelo, rounded out with a touch of white peach. It is wonderfully serene, cooling, elegant and precise. Drink 2025-2050.
94 points
Anne Krebiehl MW - Vinous

Wonderfully expressive nose of honeysuckle and fresh garden herbs. Juicy, light-bodied palate with creaminess, slatey minerality and very elegant acidity. Long, zesty finish with plenty of mandarin orange character. Drink or hold.
94 points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: Yalumba 30 Year Old Fine Aged Tawny (500ml)
entry.summary:
Aged for a minimum of 30 years and meticulously blended, this is a superb Tawny thats sweet, luscious and intense with a syrupy like mouth feel.

Deeper and darker in colour than the Yalumba 21 year old, it has a sienna brown black tinged core and an onion brown, olive green tinged hue. Powerful scents of toffee, honey, walnut and rancio waft through the olfactory senses followed by some dried raisin and spice notes. Sweet, luscious and intense with a syrupy like mouth feel counterpointed by superb spirit integration which provides a dryness across the finish. Honey, toffee, hazelnut and dried raisin flavours meld into a nutty old brandy and rancio back drop. Mouth coating, long and silky with a lingering honeyed nut, dried fig and marzipan aftertaste.
Alc. 21%

Other Reviews...
A bit drier than the 21-year-old version, the NV Fine Aged Tawny 30 Years Old boasts knockout aromas of maple syrup, walnuts, rancio and hints of dried fig, citrus and sherry-like notes. It's amazingly drinkable, not overly sweet and just a terrific effort that will age effortlessly.
96 points
Joe Czerwinski - Robert Parker's The Wine Advocate

entry.title: Boatrocker Alpha Beer 7 Year Old Australian Whisky (500ml)
entry.summary:
Back in 2019, Boatrocker distilled their flagship Alpha Queen American-hopped Pale Ale. After seven years in a first-fill Buffalo Trace cask, it was bottled at high strength to preserve the vibrant aromatics. The delightful fruity, hoppy pick-up on the nose carries through to the palate. You can almost sense the fizziness and bitter fruitiness of the pale ale through the piney finish, while the Bourbon barrel adds a light vanilla creaminess. No gimmick. Just one of the most engaging, refreshing and distinctively beer inspired whiskies you're ever likely to try.

Notes from the producers... On the nose: heady honeysuckle and ripe gooseberry with citrus zest and fresh green hops.  The palate is silky and balanced, waves of stone fruit and floral sweetness followed by a gentle peppery spice and herbal hop lift.  The finish brings classic whisky warmth with that bright, lingering hop bite beer lovers will adore. Perfect neat, with a large cube of ice, or in a premium cocktail.

entry.title: 2024 Joh Jos Prum Graacher Himmelreich Riesling Kabinett
entry.summary:
The wines of Graacher Himmelreich often challenge those from Wehlener Sonnenuhr, especially in hot, dry years. They feature racy acidity, a pronounced minerality, and distinct fruit aromas and flavours. They often become accessible slightly earlier than the Wehlener Sonnenuhr wines and are delightfully mouthwatering. The hill faces slightly more westerly and has deeper soils than Wehlener Sonnenuhr, which act as excellent water reservoirs. With a gradient of 45 to 65 percent, the soils, if they can even be called soils, consist of deeply weathered Devonian slate interspersed with parcels of blue slate.

Other Reviews...
The 2024 Graacher Himmelreich Kabinett displays very clear and delicate yet aromatic ripe fruit. Tender and delicate on the palate, this is a slender, filigreed Riesling with fine character and lovely elegance. The wine is a light-footed classic and refreshingly invigorating. This is AP 02 26. 8.5% stated alcohol. Natural cork. Tasted at the domaine in March 2026. Drink 2026-2050.
92 points
Stephan Reinhardt - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2024 Riesling Graacher Himmelreich Kabinett is still a little flinty but tender green apple shows through. The palate stays on this beautifully bright side where fruitiness is juicy and tart, but its freshness is absolutely subsumed and intertwined with ripeness. Its beautiful lightness is grounded in slaty stone like a scented breeze. The 2024 is gorgeous. Drink 2025-2050.
93 points
Anne Krebiehl MW - Vinous

Very fresh and animating, this light-bodied Mosel has delightful delicacy. I love the fresh apple, white peach and fresh herb aromas. Off-dry, with a well-integrated touch of natural grape sweetness. Long, crisp finish. Drink or hold.
93 points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2025 Madeleine Mediterranee Rose
entry.summary:
A moreish, gorgeously shaped Rose with a fresh, silky textured finish.

Crafted from a blend of 30% Grenache, 30% Cinsault, 30% Syrah and 10% Rolle this is a delicious Rose at a highly attractive price produced by Burgundian domaine Famille Paquet.

entry.title: Christian Drouin Pomme Prisoniere Pays d'Auge Calvados (1000ml)
entry.summary: Each spring in Normandy, the Alleaume family hangs thousands of empty glass carafes in their apple orchards near Gonneville-sur-Honfleur. Over the summer, a tiny apple grows inside each one. Timing is everything, as the fruit must be introduced at precisely the right moment to fit through the vessel's narrow neck. By September, the carafes are harvested, cleaned, and filled with Calvados. Even after 30+ years of practice, only 40% of carafes hung yield a bottle fit for sale. But as founder Christian Drouin says: "Our first year, the success rate was just 5%. It wasn't zero, so we decided to persevere." As the apple macerates, its character melds beautifully with the spirit, resulting in a juicy, fruit-forward expression. Compared to most other Calvados, there's significantly less oak influence, yet it remains a proper young brandy throughout - vibrant and warming more than mellow and sweet, bursting with baked apple and pear flavours at the finish. Once opened, you can continue to top up the bottle with Calvados. Doing so will keep the apple glossy and preserved indefinitely. 40% Alc./Vol.
entry.g:title: Christian Drouin Pomme Prisoniere Pays d'Auge Calvados (1000ml)
entry.g:description: Each spring in Normandy, the Alleaume family hangs thousands of empty glass carafes in their apple orchards near Gonneville-sur-Honfleur. Over the summer, a tiny apple grows inside each one. Timing is everything, as the fruit must be introduced at precisely the right moment to fit through the vessel's narrow neck. By September, the carafes are harvested, cleaned, and filled with Calvados. Even after 30+ years of practice, only 40% of carafes hung yield a bottle fit for sale. But as founder Christian Drouin says: "Our first year, the success rate was just 5%. It wasn't zero, so we decided to persevere." As the apple macerates, its character melds beautifully with the spirit, resulting in a juicy, fruit-forward expression. Compared to most other Calvados, there's significantly less oak influence, yet it remains a proper young brandy throughout - vibrant and warming more than mellow and sweet, bursting with baked apple and pear flavours at the finish. Once opened, you can continue to top up the bottle with Calvados. Doing so will keep the apple glossy and preserved indefinitely. 40% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2024 Lou Parais Alpes de Haut-Provence Rose
entry.summary:
A delicious, slippery textured Provence Rose with a dry tangy finish that shows some spice.

Made from a blend of 60% Grenache, 40% Syrah and 20% Cinsault. Pale salmon tinged colour. Lifted peach, raspberry and blood orange scents are trailed by some stony mineral notes. Delicious raspberry, strawberry and peach fruits carry a slippery textural feel across the palate with some blood orange and slatey mineral characters the undercard. Brisk acidity with a dry tangy finish that shows some spice.
Drink now.
Alc. 13.5%

Matured for 10 months in older French oak. Deep dark red core with black toned edges and a dark red hue. entry.title: 2021 Bekkers Syrah
entry.summary:
Powerful and rich with lush, concentrated fruit framed by a sturdily built tannin structure.

Fruit was sourced from the McLaren vale sub regions of Clarendon and Seaview with 28% whole bunches utilised in the fermentation process. Maturation took place in a mixture of new (47%) and older (53%) French oak puncheons (500L).
Impenetrable inky black in colour with a very deep dark red black hue. Pronounced pepper infused aromas of dark plum and liquorice emanate from the glass followed by some smoked meat, earth, dried herb and subtle fennel notes. Rich, concentrated dark plum, liquorice and blackberry fruits are lush and supple upon entry. Notions of scorched earth, fennel, dried meats and blackpepper lurk underneath. Outstanding power with a sturdily built tannin structure that shows great polish. Concludes very long and sumptuous with plenty of spice.
Drink over the next 8-10 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews.
Deep, bold, bright red-purple colour with essency aromas of black fruits, blackberry/blackcurrant, the flavours bold and primary, full-bodied, rich and generous, with traces of star anise and licorice, poised high on the ripeness scale but certainly gets away with it. Opulent and hedonistic, a full-bodied and plush shiraz that already drinks superbly and should have a long career.
97 Points
The Real Review

You cant do much Bekkers than this.
This is a full-bodied red wine with complexity served neat and structure planted firm. Its as commanding as it is beguiling. It tastes of blue and black berries, licorice, seaweed, smoked-liquid-cedar and toast, and while I think theres some positive reduction at play here too its difficult to tell; it may just be the way the smokiness of the oak has teamed with the seaweed-side of the fruit. No matter. The effect is mesmerising; the cups of flavour runneth into sheets of brilliant, mineral-strewn tannin, atmospheric smoke on the rise, all manner of goings on rumbling in the background. Its a wonderful wine. Drink 2025-2035+
96 Points
Campbell Mattinson The Wine Front

The 2021 Syrah is supple, dark and spicy, and gives me all the detail and presence I was hoping for from the excellent 2021 vintage. The tannins in the mouth emphasize the black fruit, and it pulls together as a seamless, cohesive whole, even at this very young/early stage in its life. This is much more open-weaved and approachable than the Clarendon Syrah tasted next to it. Perhaps this speaks more of attraction and seduction up front. The fruit is sourced from three parcels41% Clarendon (with one parcel at 194-242 meters above seal level) and 59% Seaview (with one parcel at 102-110 meters above seal level). You can see from the elevations that the Clarendon area is hilly and elevated (and beautiful!)this is obvious when you visit. There was around 30% whole bunches in the mix this year, and it had a wild ferment and matured in French oak puncheons (500 liters, 47% new) until bottling in December 2022. 14% alcohol, sealed under screw cap. Drink 2023-2043.
95+ Points
Erin Larkin Robert Parkers The Wine Advocate

entry.title: 2024 Joh Jos Prum Graacher Himmelreich Riesling Spatlese
entry.summary:
The wines of Graacher Himmelreich often challenge those from Wehlener Sonnenuhr, especially in hot, dry years. They feature racy acidity, a pronounced minerality, and distinct fruit aromas and flavours. They often become accessible slightly earlier than the Wehlener Sonnenuhr wines and are delightfully mouthwatering. The hill faces slightly more westerly and has deeper soils than Wehlener Sonnenuhr, which act as excellent water reservoirs. With a gradient of 45 to 65 percent, the soils, if they can even be called soils, consist of deeply weathered Devonian slate interspersed with parcels of blue slate.

Other Reviews...
The 2024 Graacher Himmelreich Sptlese offers an intense, refined and elegant bouquet of tropical fruits, weathered wet slate and greenish herbs and grass. Very elegant and refined but also lush and savory on the palate, this is another sophisticated Sptlese that combines the juiciness and fruit intensity of the Badstube with the saline and crystalline finesse of the Graacher Himmelreich. This is an excellent effort. 7.5% stated alcohol. Natural cork. Tasted at the domaine from AP 07 25 in March 2026. Drink 2026-2060.
94 points
Stephan Reinhardt - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2024 Riesling Graacher Himmelreich Sptlese offers a salty wet slate aroma with a savor reminiscent of lichen and citrus peel. All about it is precise, stony, linear, crystalline and bright. You almost forget that this is a Sptlese, as its sweetness and acidity seem to be bound absolutely to the sunken salty slate that makes the mouth water endlessly. The 2024 has brilliance, poise, absolute structure and very fine bones. The finish is full of lemon zest. Drink 2028-2055.
95 points
Anne Krebiehl MW - Vinous

Juicy and well structured with quite a firm core, this makes a bold statement. Theres a hint of bitterness interwoven with the pronounced acidity to give this a firm core. Serious minerality, but also plenty of grapefruit peel and pith flavors in the long, slightly austere finish. Drinkable now, but best from 2027.
94 points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2023 David Duband Morey-Saint-Denis Clos Sorbe Premier Cru - DAMAGED LABEL
entry.summary:
David Duband is regarded as one of the rising stars of Burgundy. He took over his family domaine at a very young age and now has more than 20 vintages of experience behind him. Starting out with small family holdings David, together with his business partner Francois Feuillet, have added to their portfolio of wines through the purchase of some exceptional old Grand cru vineyards throughout Gevrey Chambertin and Morey St Denis, including prime holdings of retiring vigneron Jacky Truchot.

Other Reviews....
A cool, airy and elegant nose present wafting aromas of the essence of red cherry nuanced by a broad range of pretty floral wisps. The succulent, seductive and detailed medium-bodied flavors possess a more refined mouthfeel while offering notably better complexity on the balanced and youthfully austere finale. This is lovely, understated and worth considering. Drink through 2031+.
90-93 points
Allen Meadows - Burghound

Pretty ruby purple, with a lifted nose, I can hardly see the whole bunches though they are part of it. Medium depth here, flowing nicely if softly across the palate. Drink from 2029-2035.
91-93 points
Jasper Morris MW - Inside Burgundy

Rich juicy dark to black fruits and gently chewy tannins.

Deep dark red black colour with a dark red hue. Aromas of dark to black raspberry and liquorice fill the nostrils followed by some ripe cherry, vanillin cedar, earth and spicy fresh herb notes. Rich juicy dark to black cherry and liquorice fruits overlay a dark raspberry, subtle earth and vanillin spice back drop. Gently chewy tannins with a generously fleshed mid length finish.
Drink over the next 3-4 years.
Alc. 14%

entry.title: 2023 Esilio Tooth & Nail Sangiovese
entry.summary:
Generous red fruits backed by sturdy tannins and energetic acidity with a quite rustic finish that shows plenty of spice.

Midnight black core with a dark red hue. Spicy red currant aromas show good lift out of the glass followed by some dried herb, earth and subtle tobacco notes. Generous red currant and red cherry fruits are backed by a sturdy tannin structure which imparts a chalky feel across the back palate. Some liquorice, earthy tobacco, dried herb and spice characters sit underneath. Energetic acidity with a long well fleshed yet quite rustic finish that shows plenty of spice.
Drink over the next 2-3 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews.
From the rolling hills north-east of Adelaide in whats known as the One Tree Hill district, we get a pretty ballsy Sangio with a decent whack of oak impact on first opening not surprising as a result of 15 months maturation in French and American barrels, new and seasoned, the latter source letting itself known in the bouquet. The fruit is quite jubey, crimson and black berried, finishing with timbery and grippy tannins. Will definitely satisfy those who like their oaked-style wines and will perform a treat with a serious cut of beef.
92 Points
Tony Love WinePilot.com

entry.title: 2025 Bellvale Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Rich yet refined with a long, fresh, generously shaped finish.

Recently purchased by the owners of Kooyong Estate and Port Phillip Estate, the new releases from Bellvale feature a smart packaging refresh and have taken a significant leap in quality. Matured on lees for a period of 11 months in French oak barriques (15% new).
Brilliant pale straw colour with green highlighted edges and a watery hue. Attractive white peach, nectarine, dried honey and cashew aromas drift from the glass with some biscuity nougat and spice notes also evident. Rich and creamy yet refined in its feel, mouth filling flavours of white peach, nectarine and dried honey are layered across the palate. Biscuity nougat, subtle spicy cashew and delicate struck match stick overtones unfold across the back half. Finishes fresh, long and generously shaped.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 13%

Other Reviews..
We have a winner here. This is crisp and elegant and textural and long, and throughout it just simply tastes good. Its as good or better than any Bellvale Chardonnay Ive had previous. It tastes of pears, nectarines, oyster shells and grapefruit, with hay, cedar and toast notes layered over the top the latter in the most subtle way possible. If this is a sign of things to come from the Bellvale vineyard, under new ownership, then we have a lot to look forward to. Drink 2026-2031+
94 Points
Campbell Mattinson The Wine Front

entry.title: 2024 Shiraz By Farr
entry.summary:
Rich, savoury and smoky Northern Rhone styled Shiraz.

Planted in 1994, the original By Farr vineyard is the source of this Shiraz. Set on a north-facing slope with red volcanic soil over limestone and deep sandstone, it delivers fruit of concentration and poise. All grapes are hand-picked from VSP trellising, with a portion of whole bunches included to bring added spice and structure. In most vintages, 2-4% Viognier is co-fermented, depending on timing, adding aromatic lift and a subtle textural edge.

Pitch black heart with a dark red black tinged hue. Intense clove and smoked meat infused aromas of red plum and liquorice sail through the nostrils trailed by some fennel and peppered earth notes. The rich, impressively fleshed, mid weighted palate is flooded with red plum and liquorice fruit which is complexed by notions of smoky vanillin cedar, clove and peppered dried meats. Supple mid palate feel with relatively polished yet underlyingly structured tannins. Excellent depth and power with a long savoury finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14%

entry.title: 2021 Produttori del Barbaresco Montefico Riserva Barbaresco
entry.summary:
From a not widely known vineyard, Montefico sits half way between Ovello and Montestefano and it is often compared to the latter because of their similar soil (high calcium) and their close proximity. Its warm - full south - exposure is mitigated by the cooler northern wind that occasionally funnels into the narrow valley between the villages of Barbaresco and Neive. First released in 1970, it produces classic Barbaresco wines that could be seen as austere when young but with incredible complexity behind the tannins.

Other Reviews...
The Produttori del Barbaresco 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Montefico is another large-scale Nebbiolo in this ladder of Riserva intensity. The wine shows notable texture and depth with flavors of dark fruit, blackcurrant and dried cherry that unfold steadily across the palate. Subtle notes of spice, cinnamon, licorice and camphor build in the background, adding complexity and dimension. Sourced from 3.9 hectares of vines on calcareous clay soils, Montefico consistently delivers a more structured and powerful expression of Barbaresco, and the 2021 vintage amplifies those qualities. Fermented in stainless steel and aged in large oak botti, this release totals 16,600 bottles. Drink 2027-2052.
97 points
Monica Larner - Rober Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Montefico is a tense, vibrant wine. Whereas in most vintages the Montefico can be a touch austere, the 2021 has plenty of energy, but also the textural depth to pull it all together. In that sense, the Montefico is a terrific example of the vintage here. Its concentration and persistence are the stuff dreams are made of. Hints of sage, graphite, chalk and mint explode on the back end. Drink 2027-2041.
97 points
Antonio Galloni - Vinous

Spicy and aromatic, this is full of wild herbs and strawberries, licorice and mint. Fully focused on freshness yet restrained, showing balsamic and figs. Full-bodied, silky to velvety on the palate due to superripe tannins, with crisp acidity and a tight yet chiseled structure in the finish. Long and warming. March 2026 release. Drink or hold.
96 points
Aldo Fiordelli - JamesSuckling.com

The 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Montefico pours a slightly deeper red color than the Ovello and opens with inviting aromas of sweet cedar, cherry liqueur, toasted spice, and polished leather. Medium-bodied, it delivers vibrant acidity, velvety tannins, and a bit more depth and structure on the palate. The finish is long and persistent. Roughly 16,348 bottles and 1,826 magnums were produced. Drink 2028-2050.
97 points
Audrey Frick - JebDunnuck.com

From a not widely known vineyard, Montefico sits half way between Ovello and Montestefano and it is often compared to the latter because of their similar soil (high calcium) and their close proximity. Its warm - full south - exposure is mitigated by the cooler northern wind that occasionally funnels into the narrow valley between the villages of Barbaresco and Neive. First released in 1970, it produces classic Barbaresco wines that could be seen as austere when young but with incredible complexity behind the tannins.

Other Reviews...
The Produttori del Barbaresco 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Montefico is another large-scale Nebbiolo in this ladder of Riserva intensity. The wine shows notable texture and depth with flavors of dark fruit, blackcurrant and dried cherry that unfold steadily across the palate. Subtle notes of spice, cinnamon, licorice and camphor build in the background, adding complexity and dimension. Sourced from 3.9 hectares of vines on calcareous clay soils, Montefico consistently delivers a more structured and powerful expression of Barbaresco, and the 2021 vintage amplifies those qualities. Fermented in stainless steel and aged in large oak botti, this release totals 16,600 bottles. Drink 2027-2052.
97 points
Monica Larner - Rober Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Montefico is a tense, vibrant wine. Whereas in most vintages the Montefico can be a touch austere, the 2021 has plenty of energy, but also the textural depth to pull it all together. In that sense, the Montefico is a terrific example of the vintage here. Its concentration and persistence are the stuff dreams are made of. Hints of sage, graphite, chalk and mint explode on the back end. Drink 2027-2041.
97 points
Antonio Galloni - Vinous

Spicy and aromatic, this is full of wild herbs and strawberries, licorice and mint. Fully focused on freshness yet restrained, showing balsamic and figs. Full-bodied, silky to velvety on the palate due to superripe tannins, with crisp acidity and a tight yet chiseled structure in the finish. Long and warming. March 2026 release. Drink or hold.
96 points
Aldo Fiordelli - JamesSuckling.com

The 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Montefico pours a slightly deeper red color than the Ovello and opens with inviting aromas of sweet cedar, cherry liqueur, toasted spice, and polished leather. Medium-bodied, it delivers vibrant acidity, velvety tannins, and a bit more depth and structure on the palate. The finish is long and persistent. Roughly 16,348 bottles and 1,826 magnums were produced. Drink 2028-2050.
97 points
Audrey Frick - JebDunnuck.com
entry.g:product_type: Red Wines > Imported Red Wines > Italy

entry.title: 2022 Richard Hamilton Lot 148 Merlot
entry.summary:
An elegant mid weighted Merlot that has a long savoury red fruited finish.

Deep black dark red core with a dark red hue. Elevated mulberry and red currant aromas are intermeshed with cedar, tobacco, earth, dried herb and spice notes. Generous red currant and mulberry fruits are elegantly layered across the mid weighted palate with dusty earth, cedary tobacco and spicy dried herb elements lending further complexity across the back half. Fine grained tannins provide ample structure across the long savoury red fruited finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews
Lot 148 was the familys first vineyard way back in the day. From what was a very good year, this is a Merlot of some style. The nose captures the reds of fruits of raspberry and mulberry augmented with a slightly earthy ironstone character. It works well. The palate is medium-bodied but concentrated, revealing expressive fruits sprinkled with spices. Its a vibrant and lively wine with the fine chalky tannins directing through to the sustained finish. Drink 2025-2033.
92 Points
Ray Jordan WinePilot.com

entry.title: 2021 Produttori del Barbaresco Ovello Riserva Barbaresco
entry.summary:
Ovello is the northernmost vineyard in the village of Barbaresco and among the first 5 single-vineyards produced back in 1967. Soils are calcareous and rich in clay: these characterics combined with the cooler microclimate shape its exuberant fruit profile and its fuller body. Due to its powerful structure, some years of bottle ageing are usually required to balance that out.

Other Reviews...
The Produttori del Barbaresco 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Ovello shows greater richness and structure on the mid-palate, with ripe and supple flavors of red and purple fruit that give the wine an especially generous personality. This is a concentrated expression of Nebbiolo, yet it remains direct, sharp and beautifully focused, fully living up to the reputation of this highly collectible vintage. The added depth of fruit is balanced by freshness, creating a wine that is both powerful and elegantly composed. Fermented in stainless steel and aged in large oak botti, the 2021 Ovello was produced in 19,400 bottles and 2,000 magnums. Drink 2027-2052.
96 points
Monica Larner - Rober Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Ovello sizzles with tension right out of the gate. Orange peel, mint, chalk, white pepper and crushed rocks are all finely sketched. Bright and sinewy to the core, the 2021 captures the purest essence of Ovello. It's another stellar wine in this range. The Ovello will appeal most to readers who like tense wines. Drink 2027-2041.
96 points
Antonio Galloni - Vinous

Restrained if not austere, showing dark fruit, earthy tones and cherries with almost wild blackberries and a whiff of blood oranges. Full-bodied. The attack is dense and velvety with thick, firm tannins that are dusty yet ripe. Powerful but well-balanced at the end, with a mouth-coating texture. March 2026 release, but will need another year or two to be ready to drink.
95 points
Aldo Fiordelli - JamesSuckling.com

Displaying a saturated medium red hue, the 2021 Barbaresco Riserva Ovello offers notes of dusty cedar, red cherries, raspberries, and crushed stones, although the wood tones will need time to fully integrate. Medium-bodied, the palate has beautiful brightness, with hints of apricot and stone fruit along with a more linear, elegant structure. For me, this wine holds a very special place in the range and quietly stopped me in my tracks during the tasting. Roughly 16,666 bottles were produced. Drink 2026-2056.
98 points
Audrey Frick - JebDunnuck.com

entry.title: 2021 Haan Estate Prestige Shiraz
entry.summary:
A rich, plush Barossa Shiraz seductively draped with dark chocolate, dark plum, toasty vanillin oak and liquorice flavours.

Impenetrable inky black in colour with a very deep dark red black hue. Potent aromas of dark plum, dark chocolate, liquorice and toasty vanillin oak fill the nostrils complimented by earthy mocha and spice notes. Rich and plush, the full bodied palate is seductively draped with dark chocolate, dark plum, toasty vanillin oak and liquorice flavours. Concentrated, powerful and possessing velvet smooth tannins, it has earthy mocha, subtle leather and spice characters lingering across the long opulently textured finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 15.5%

entry.title: 2021 Whistling Eagle Vineyard Eagles Blood Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich, dense and bold, this is a classic example of Heathcote Shiraz.

Renown as one of Heathcotes leading growers and viticulturalists, Ian Rathjen also produces small parcels of wine under his own label, Whistling Eagle. Matured in French oak (25% new) for a period of 18 months, the Eagles Blood Shiraz is his ultimate expression of the Cambrian terroir displaying spectacular colour, depth and power.
Impenetrable inky black heart with a very deep dark red black hue. Heady aromas of ripe blackberry and liquorice waft through the nostrils trailed by some ripe black cherry, subtle dark chocolate, spicy vanillin cedar, fennel and pepper notes. Rich, plush and concentrated, the palate is greeted by a dense wave of blackberry, liquorice and dark plum fruits. Lurking in the background are notions of spicy fennel, vanillin cedar and peppered earth. Opulently textured it has a velvety yet solidly built tannin structure, outstanding power and a long, sumptuous finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews..
An exceptional vintage shows Heathcote shiraz at its best. As ever, Eagles Blood delivers a wine with a strong sense of place, of Aussie bush scents, acacia, briar, bracken and mineral red earthiness against a core of sturdy, ripe black fruits, chocolate and spice. In the fuller-bodied style, but it carries it well with tannins laid out evenly. There is the kind of balance in place that encourages drinking now which I would do but with the potential for further ageing which I would also do. Drink by 2039.
96 Points
Jeni Port - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2014 Signatory Vintage Bunnahabhain Staoisha 10 Year Old 100 Proof Edition #61 Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary:
"Doesn't hold back at all... Rich sherry, rich smoke, nice strengthit just works". / "...a superb example of excellent value for money." - whiskybase.com

Notwithstanding recent pricing on Edradour's Ballechin and several Ardbegs, this is easily one of the most exciting peated whiskies we currently have on offer. At Bunnahabhain they refer to the style as Moine. Independents aren't permitted to use that title, so they reference nearby Loch Staoisha instead. The undeniably rare 40ppm output is usually reserved for blenders, yet more than holds its own against Islay compatriots. Wide, tall stills synergise dense smoke with Bunnahs naturally briny character, creating a spirit that's both coastal and deeply peated. The complexity and divergence can be significant between bottlings. The smoke is strong, often of the cured meat variety, but generally not as maritime as that of Islay's south coast. At close to natural strength and with added input from first and second fill Oloroso casks, you can expect a diverse and immensely tasty rush of flavour. Find out why this 'new' Islay classic is gaining popularity so fast. 57.1% Alc./Vol. Non chill filtered.

Other reviews... "Very decent peated Bunna for the age and the price. Not a huge fan of the nose but the palate delivers. Some great bbq, dark fruit, spicy menthol peat and a very enjoyable finish."

"Very powerful. Strong peat and heavy barrel influence. Doesn't hold back at all. For the style, it doesn't taste too young. Relentless. Salted liquorice is the main note on the palate. Candy. It's not my favorite style, but I can enjoy it for what it is, and it's a really fun drink. Very well done and a great price. - whiskybase.com

entry.title: 2023 Donnhoff Oberhauser Brucke Riesling Spatlese
entry.summary:
Donnhoff make the best wines in the Nahe region, and some of the finest anywhere in the world. While it was Helmut Donnhoff that launched this estate to worldwide attention, winemaking duties are now managed by his talented son, Cornelius. There's a deep understanding of the grand wines and grand vineyards that's been handed down through the generations. And given the enormous technical proficiency Cornelius has demonstrated so far, Donnhoff is sure to be at the top of the vinous hierarchy for years to come.

An exclusive monopole of the estate, the steep, slate-rich Oberhauser Brucke vineyard sits on a distinct river bend that yields some of Germany's most coveted Pradikat Rieslings. Its Spatlese and Auslese balance electrifying mineral acidity with lush fruit sweetness, delivering an effortless harmony of weightless power, purity, and decades-long cellaring potential.

Other Reviews...
When worlds colide. The tension between the cool, dark side (think Darth Vader) and the enormous brightness of the stone fruit (think Luke Skywalker) makes this astonishing riesling Spatlese extremely compelling. The most beautiful pineapple and grapefruit aromas. Fabulous freshness at the stunningly straight and pure finish. Drink or hold.
98 points
JamesSuckling.com

The 2023 Riesling Oberhuser Brcke Sptlese is from a geologically complex site that has loess, loam, shale, weathered sandstone and volcanic formations, the moderating influence of the river also means that botrytis is possible. Sptlese and Auslese are harvested together but selected in the vineyard. Golden and gently botrytised fruit goes into Sptlese. This charms with a touch of crushed blackcurrant foliage and ripest, juiciest Reine Claude plum, all edged with citrus. Beautifully taut, vividly concentrated, yet no heaviness, just light-footed, dancing, playful and oh so balanced. Drink 2034-2070.
96 points
Anne Krebiehl MW - Vinous

entry.title: 1995 Signatory Vintage Fettercairn 29 Year Old Symington's Choice Cask Strength Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary: Fettercairn eludes many a malt buff, not only in physical form, but in its taste profile which tends to elicit varied and polarising reactions. This sounds like a good example, with comments on whiskybase.com ranging from "a decent whisky with a fairly broad palette of derivatives," to "Delightfully fruity" and "menthol-like". A conversation starter, no doubt, and reported to show its best with water. Symington's 2025 bottling was drawn from a single hogshead yielding 211 bottles. 59.8% Alc./Vol. Non chill filtered.

entry.title: Tiki Lovers Coffee Rum (700ml)
entry.summary: Created from rums sourced from Jamaica, Barbados, Trinidad and Guyana, paired with roasted coffee beans. If the rums are lost amid the fabulous notes of chocolate-flavoured jelly babies, milk-coffee, vanilla and cocoa, this still makes a positive addition to the coffee-flavoured segment. It's also drier than many liqueur equivalents while boasting a significantly higher ABV. Enjoy in a Kingston Negroni, Black Voodoo, with cola or simply by itself. 43% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: Compagnie des Indes Great White Original White Rum (700ml)
entry.summary: Compagnie des Indes "Great White" series started out showcasing unique terroirs and distilleries globally. Two expressions from the Dominican Republic have landed, produced from pure sugarcane juice and bottled in France without chill filtration. The "Original" has an entry-level ABV and a bouquet resembling agricole or Clairin, less the pungent intensity; Grassy, caney, waxy, white-pepper-laced notes are echoed on the palate, finishing warm, vibrant, dry, vaguely briney and grappa-like. Use this unsweetened, pure and very natural rum for classic serves such as the Mojito, Daiquiri or rum and soda. 40% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2018 Oakridge Vineyard Series Blanc de Blancs
entry.summary:
Refined and airy yet racy, this is a beautifully proportioned Yarra Valley Sparkling.

Made from 100% Chardonnay grapes and aged on yeast lees for 5 years and 8 months. Pours with an exuberant mousse that slowly fades to reveal a pale straw coloured base thats finely threaded by a very nimble bead. Elevated aromas of yeast lees, citrus and baked bread are trailed by hints of cashew, dried honey and subtle chalky notes. Refined and airy yet racy, the beautifully proportioned palate is detailed with baked bread, citrus, yeast lees and brioche flavours which are complimented by delicate cashew and dried honey characters across the back half. Gentle creamy texture with crisp acidity and a long dry, chalk tinged finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 12.5%

Other Reviews..
Just over five years on lees before being disgorged and with six months on cork before being released. 4.5g/L dosage. A very bright green gold. A complex amalgam of stone fruits, baked apples and brioche. Fine boned and very even on the palate. Already a delight to drink, this will still be looking good five years from now. Drink by 2030.
96 Points
Philip Rich - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion
