entry.title: 2023 Yering Station Shiraz Viognier
entry.summary:
Beautifully fleshed and deeply fruited with a long, refined finish.

Possibly their best yet release, the 2023 vintage is a blend of 98% Shiraz and 2% Viognier. Dense pitch black heart with a dark red hue. Showing impressive aromatic lift, the nose is led by blackberry, liquorice and dark plum scents followed by subtle smoky cedar, peppered fennel and apricot notes. The beautifully fleshed, mid weighted palate is generously detailed with blackberry and liquorice fruits over a spicy dark plum, vanillin cedar and peppered earth back drop. Polished, almost velvet like tannin structure with a long, deeply fruited yet refined finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.4%

Other Reviews....
Co-fermented with 2% viognier; matured in 18% new French barriques. A vibrant, plummy red. There was no reserve in '23, and the fruit mainly went into this. The result is a nicely perfumed wine with red and black fruits, freshly crushed peppercorns and a little anise. The palate is medium bodied and gently plush, with gently chewy, persistent tannins rounding out a delicious wine to drink over the next four to six years. Outstanding value. Drink by 2034.
95+ Points
Philip Rich - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2023 Woodstock Deep Sands Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich, lush and full bodied with a long opulent conclusion.

Pitch black in colour with a dark red hue. Elevated ripe dark plum and liquorice scents mix with vanillin spice, black cherry and subtle peppered earth notes. Rich and lush, the full bodied palate is swamped with dark plum, liquorice and black cherry fruits. Vanillin spice, scorched earth and blackpepper elements lurk beneath. Ripe, gently chewy tannins with a long opulent conclusion.
Drink over the next 2-3 years.
Alc. 14.9%

entry.title: 2020 Greenock Creek Roennfeldt Road Shiraz
entry.summary:
An ultra rich, monumentally sized Barossa Shiraz.

Super dense inky black heart with a very deep dark red black hue. Potent aromas of dark plum, liquorice and dark chocolate waft through the nostrils followed by vanillin oak, mocha, subtle earth and spice notes. Ultra rich, thick and voluptuous, the monumentally sized palate is coated with dark plum, liquorice, dark chocolate and vanillin oak flavours. Exceptional concentration, density and power with earthy mocha, faint leather and spice elements the undercard. Sturdy in their structure yet velvet like in their feel, the tannins are seamlessly interwoven through the long decadent yet slightly chewy finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 16%

Other Reviews
An incredibly proportioned shiraz sourced from 120-year-old vines on the Greenock Creek estate in western Barossa. I'm always amazed at the balance Greenock Creek achieve in these wines. Now, this is full-bodied to be sure, but the line and flow shows a distinct elegance and grace, tannins fine and chewy, the fruit pure and a mix of red and dark tones studded with spice, floral facets and roasting meats. Jeez Louise ... very nicely done. Drink by 2044.
97 Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: Starward Two-fold Australian Whisky (700ml) - Older Bottling
entry.summary:
Note: Product has come from a private collection and as such has some minor scuffing/scratches/handling marks. Actual product pictured.

The first general release from Starward in years. Like some previous editions, this was matured in Australian red wine barrels (Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir). The difference here is Two-fold incorporates a 35% wheat component with the barley. The lighter, softer wheat spirit allows a little more of the barrel character to shine through. 6000 bottles are initially on offer (with a large volume destined for the US) - that's double the number of bottles of the inaugural Solera single malt Starward. The distillery's own allocation appears to have sold out online, and Proprietor David Vitale is already starting to wonder whether he's made enough... The hope is this will last through till Christmas!

Tasting note: Brilliant copper. Reminiscent of the standard issue Starward, only softer and slightly sweeter with notes of banana cake, toffee, vanilla-wafer biscuit and light cocoa. The sweetness is tempered by spices and delicate tannins in the mouth, with hints of dried banana, vanilla and a touch of creamy soda to finish, the distillery's characteristic notes retained. Eminently drinkable, this rolls out like a good Canadian blend. 40% Alc./Vol.

Other reviews... The temptation, when tasting a spirit for the first time, is to scrabble through your flavour memory banks looking for comparisons with spirits you've tasted in the past. With this new whisky, that proved to be a fruitless exercise because it really doesn't taste quite like any other I've tried before. It ticks the general whisky boxes of flavour and style expectation without evoking bourbon or scotch. And while it has unmistakably grain-based spirit characters on the nose and the palate, there are some quite distinctive, unexpected characters in there too: aromas of fresh toast, some dried fig, a hint of ripe banana, then a soft, pretty, creamy vanilla texture on the tongue, finishing with a little tannic grip and savoury complexity. As I say, a very good whisky, especially at this price.
- Max Allen, The Financial Review

entry.title: Naud 10 Year Old Anejo Colombian Rum (700ml)
entry.summary: While rooted in traditional cognac-making, Naud sources sugarcane from South America to create bespoke rums, this time partnering with Casa Santana. The column-distilled ten year old is matured in ex-Bourbon barrels, before further benefiting from a six month finishing period in French oak in the cellars of Maison Naud. 40% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2021 Brand’s Laira Blockers Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich and plush with a long amply concentrated finish.

Dense inky black heart with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Plummy liquorice like aromas mix with blackberry, vanillin confectionary, subtle earth and spice. Rich liquorice and blackberry fruits carry a plush feel across the medium to full bodied palate. Notions of dark plum, vanillin cedar and subtle peppered earth linger across the back half. Velvet smooth tannins with a long deeply fleshed and amply concentrated finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 14.5%

entry.title: 2020 Domaine Clos Rougeard Saumur-Champigny Les Poyeux
entry.summary:
Other Reviews...
The 2020 Les Poyeux elegantly fills the mouth like an arch. It's not a big wine despite the warmth of the year, nor is it warm. This is serious and not overdone. Its supple, ripe and gentle with some savory earthiness joining the cedary, tobacco-like oak. A few rains before harvest have ensured that it didn't become too concentrated. The 2020 is rounded and ripe, and its tannins offer the finest of grains. This is gentle, satisfying and balanced. Drink 2026-2036.
94 points
Rebecca Gibb MW - Vinous

entry.title: 2024 Samuel Billaud Sechet Vieilles Vignes Chablis Premier Cru
entry.summary:
While the origins of this domaine date back to Charles-Louis-Noel Billaud in 1815, it's the current generation winemaker Samuel Billaud that has made waves with the exceptional quality of his wines produced since the creation of this project in 2009. Following the sale of the family business Domaine Billaud-Simon to Faiveley in 2014, Samuel received further prized parcels of land and now makes wines from five of the grand cru vineyards, and five of the top premier cru vineyards. The wines are vinified in a mixture of stainless steel and large old wood barrels, the latter mainly for the premier and grand cru wines.

Other Reviews...
The vines that produce Billaud's Schet Vieilles Vignes are the oldest that he owns, planted almost a century ago in the heart of the lieu-dit. The yields were tiny in 2024 no more than 10 hl/ha but produced a wine with exotic aromas of passion fruit, gooseberry and hazelnut. The texture is silky, concentrated and long. Fermentation was carried out entirely in glass wine globes to preserve the fruit's intense purity. This thrilling Chablis will age for decades to come. Drink 2030-2060.
94 points
Charles Curtis MW - Decanter

Cool, pure, layered and airy aromas focused mostly on citrus confit, lemongrass and oyster shell. There is seriously good concentration to the powerful and palate staining medium weight flavors that display equally good depth and persistence on a mildly rustic finale. This is old school Chablis, a bit rough and tumble but packed with potential. Drink through 2034+.
92-94 points
Allen Meadows - Burghound

From vines planted in the 1920s and 1930s, the 2024 Chablis 1er Cru Schet Vieilles Vignes produced only 10 hectoliters per hectare this year and, given the tiny volume, was vinified in a glass wine globe. It soars from the glass with a bouquet of Granny Smith apple, lemon oil, sage, oyster liquor and spring flowers. On the palate, it is chiseled, displaying exemplary purity, bracing acidity and a strikingly sapid, mouthwatering finish. It is particularly incisive this year, a quality only amplified by the character of the vintage.
92-94 points
Kristaps Karklins - Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

The 2024 Chablis Les Schets 1er Cru marks the first year that Billaud used 200-litre WineGlobes for vinification, before transferring the wine into stainless steel barrels after one year. It is very steely and austere on the nose, old-school Chablis, with green apple and a touch of grapefruit, but missing the bandwidth of the other Premier Crus. The palate is well balanced with a tangy opening, quite sharp acidity, moderate depth and admirable length, with hints of orange zest and lime on the finish. Very fine. Drink 2027-2042.
91 points
Neal Martin - Vinous

10 hl/ha translates into three wine-globes and one barrel. A light lemon tint to the colour. The bouquet is very classy, all on those dry stones, with a fantastic precision. Very direct, very linear, almost a tannic touch since the fruit is always so dry here. Good persistence. Makes one salivate! Drink from 2029-2035.
92-95 points
Jasper Morris MW - Inside Burgundy
entry.g:title: 2024 Samuel Billaud Sechet Vieilles Vignes Chablis Premier Cru
entry.g:description:
While the origins of this domaine date back to Charles-Louis-Noel Billaud in 1815, it's the current generation winemaker Samuel Billaud that has made waves with the exceptional quality of his wines produced since the creation of this project in 2009. Following the sale of the family business Domaine Billaud-Simon to Faiveley in 2014, Samuel received further prized parcels of land and now makes wines from five of the grand cru vineyards, and five of the top premier cru vineyards. The wines are vinified in a mixture of stainless steel and large old wood barrels, the latter mainly for the premier and grand cru wines.

Other Reviews...
The vines that produce Billaud's Schet Vieilles Vignes are the oldest that he owns, planted almost a century ago in the heart of the lieu-dit. The yields were tiny in 2024 no more than 10 hl/ha but produced a wine with exotic aromas of passion fruit, gooseberry and hazelnut. The texture is silky, concentrated and long. Fermentation was carried out entirely in glass wine globes to preserve the fruit's intense purity. This thrilling Chablis will age for decades to come. Drink 2030-2060.
94 points
Charles Curtis MW - Decanter

Cool, pure, layered and airy aromas focused mostly on citrus confit, lemongrass and oyster shell. There is seriously good concentration to the powerful and palate staining medium weight flavors that display equally good depth and persistence on a mildly rustic finale. This is old school Chablis, a bit rough and tumble but packed with potential. Drink through 2034+.
92-94 points
Allen Meadows - Burghound

From vines planted in the 1920s and 1930s, the 2024 Chablis 1er Cru Schet Vieilles Vignes produced only 10 hectoliters per hectare this year and, given the tiny volume, was vinified in a glass wine globe. It soars from the glass with a bouquet of Granny Smith apple, lemon oil, sage, oyster liquor and spring flowers. On the palate, it is chiseled, displaying exemplary purity, bracing acidity and a strikingly sapid, mouthwatering finish. It is particularly incisive this year, a quality only amplified by the character of the vintage.

entry.title: 2024 Morris Rutherglen Bin No. 158 Durif
entry.summary:
Rich and opulent with firm, chewy tannins.

Impenetrable inky black in colour with a very deep dark red black hue. Heady dark plum, liquorice and dark chocolate aromas mix with vanillin oak, earthy mocha and spice notes. Rich opulent dark plum, liquorice and dark chocolate flavours flood the weighty palate with vanillin oak and earthy mocha elements then moving across the back half. Drink over the next 5-6 years.

entry.title: Clase Azul Reposado Tequila (1750ml)
entry.summary:
Produced from organically grown agaves. Deep bright gold. The bouquet yields up superbly pure, sultry notes of suggesting baked capsicum, pickled onion and grilled pineapple followed by more peppery, icing sugar and orange cake-like scents in the subsequent passes. Entry is likewise impeccably pure in its beeswax and butterscotch-driven mid palate; Sprinklings of cinnamon, white pepper and vanilla round off what is a sweet, though deliciously different Reposado experience. One to savour at the end of the night. 40% Alc./Vol.

Other reviews... This is mellowed in deep char oak for at least 8 months, which gives this tequila more character, but it retains that funky sweetness that the Plata is imbued with. Here the sweetness veers into a vanilla character, more like a creme brulee than the candy bar of the Plata. That offers more nuance to play with the slight pepper notes, but not much: The sugary notes remain overwhelming and I am normally a huge fan of sweeter tequilas again leaving you with a finish that coats the mouth, making you reach for the salty bar mix. - drinkhacker.com

...Not to be outdone by the beautiful imagery on the outside, the tequila on the inside smells equally amazing. Upon opening, you get a punch in the face of floral and sweetness. A little hint of vanilla creeps into the nose as well.  By now youre thinking, Ok this thing cost 5 times as much as Jose, it comes in this huge designer bottle, and it smells AMAZING, so when will I be let down To put it simply, this one delivers. For tequila lovers this is like a party in your mouth and for tequila squealers this one will turn you into a believer. (My wife The Novice Drinker was quite impressed. Her exact words being Its good and that says ALOT). Dont worry, it will still mix just fine in your Margaritas, Palomas, and Tequila Sunrise cocktails but I HIGHLY recommend you sip this one and enjoy its flavor. They manage to bring together a fully flavored tequila with a smooth finish that will have you wanting more (I sure did). - intoxicology.net

entry.title: 2018 Barossa Boy Lifeblood Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich, full in body and opulently textured with a long, sumptuous yet gently chewy conclusion.

Aged for 22 months in French oak hogsheads. Dense pitch black heart with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Potent dark plum, liquorice and dark chocolate aromas waft out of the glass complimented by some vanillin oak, earthy mocha and spice notes. Rich, full in body and opulently textured, the palate is drenched in a tidal wave of plush dark plum, blackberry, dark chocolate and liquorice fruits. Earthy mocha, spicy vanillin oak and subtle leather elements sit in the background. Velvety yet sturdy tannin structure with a long, sumptuous yet gently chewy conclusion.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14.5%

entry.title: 2024 Quealy Halarah Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Supple on entry with delicious red fruits finishing long, savoury and spicy.

Matured for 12 months in French oak hogsheads. Semi translucent, slightly cloudy red colour with a light red hue. Fragrant violet, red cherry and strawberry scents blossom out of the glass followed by some gentle clove, forest floor, rhubarb and spice notes. Delicious red cherry and strawberry fruits make a supple entrance with notions of rhubarb, forest floor, clove, brambly cedar and spice complexing the back half. Excellent power wave with refined tannins and good underlying freshness. Finishes long, savoury and spicy.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.2%

Other Reviews..
Given a second day chance, as it was bothering me. Still peculiar. Lots of savoury, slightly vegetal tones, wet forest, moss on stones, fresh woody spice, pine needle resin, dark amaro bitterness; this can be a difficult wine, edgy, moody, quinine-driven. But now, its intriguing, compelling. Has a character and made me stop; this must count for something in the AI era. Maybe needed time. Who doesnt. Drink 2027-2030+
92 Points
Kasia Sobiesiak The Wine Front

entry.title: 2022 Kilikanoon Walton 1946 Grenache
entry.summary:
Juicy, energetic and intensely flavoured.

From vines planted in 1946 with 5% whole bunch inclusion and maturation in seasoned French oak puncheons for 16 months.
Dark red core with black shaded edges and a red tinged hue. Fragrant red to dark raspberry, red liquorice and red cherry scents drift through the nostrils followed by some crushed rock, gentle vanillin spice and peppered earth notes. Juicy, energetic and intensely flavoured, the mid weighted palate is awash with red to dark raspberry, cherry and red liquorice fruits. Extending across the back half are notions of crushed rock, vanillin spice and pepper. Slightly muscular tannins together with fresh underlying acidity provide great structure. The long, sumptuous finish showing good tension.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews
This Grenache, from vines planted in 1946 on the hills of Leasingham, remains one of my favourite examples of this variety. Its been made with very light winemaking influence and is really designed to capture both that sense of place and variety from this vineyard. Medium-bodied, with floral, subtle damp turned earth characters and a hint of ironstone gravel. A little leafy lift adds further to the nose, and that slightly dry savoury finish provides further appeal. An excellent wine for current drinking, but with cellaring potential, as you might expect. Drink 2026-2036.
96 Points
Ray Jordan WinePilot.com

Layer after layer after layer, Walton delivers an intriguing and astonishing level of Grenache flavour. Is it the old vines, the winemaking, the vintage? Maybe its all three, and a little bit extra. From the first sniff, its wonderfully complex earth, leather, a touch of tar, dark berries, dark spices, black liquorice. Brings a concentration of flavour on the middle palate where those layers come into effect; a layering of savoury, earth, tar, leather and charcuterie melding into layers of dark fruits, spice, hints of fig and a splash of citrus peel. Tannins do a great job of producing a freshness, especially on the finish where bright tannins, red fruits and orange peel close what is an undoubted stunner of a Grenache with fabulous length. Drink 2026-2040.
96 Points
Jeni Port WinePilot.com

entry.title: Ardbeg Corryvreckan Cask Strength Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml) - Older Bottling
entry.summary:
Note: Product has come from a private collection and as such has some minor scuffing/scratches/handling marks. Actual product pictured.

A replacement for the discontinued Airigh Nam Beist, 'Cauldron of the speckled sea' (aka Corryvreckan) is a whirlpool located between the Isles of Islay and Jura, and now the name of a whisky. It's base is Ardbeg 10 combined with spirit exclusively matured in French Limousin Virgin oak. We tasted an early batch back in 2011. Dull gold colour with a pale straw hue, it presents an unusual nose for an Ardbeg: Rich chocolate, vanilla, lemon butter and spice above a smoky salty layer, the only evidence that it's Ardbeg is the end note of terracotta/clay/wet charcoal. With time in the glass, fresh smoky characteristics emerge, but do not dominate. The intense palate is initially rich and creamy, quite heavily peated, rich chocolatey flavours mingle harmoniously with the lemon butter before the unusually overt oak grips dry and the peat explodes - softly! The back palate is dry, firm, overtly oaky, and extremely spicy. Excellent balance at cask strength. Warm, tingly, spicy finish. Lemon, dry cocoa, strong spice and gentle smoke dominate the lengthy aftertaste. Unusually dry for Ardbeg, otherwise an utterly brilliant, unique expression of Islay. 57.1% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2024 Teusner Joshua Grenache Mataro Shiraz
entry.summary:
Fleshy and plush with a long, sumptuous finish.

An unoaked blend of Grenache, Mataro and Shiraz. The Grenache and Mataro fruit is sourced from old vines at Ebenezer, Williamstown, Seppeltsfield and Tanunda with the Shiraz coming from 20 year old vines.
Deep dark red black tinged core with a dark red hue. Dark raspberry, plum and liquorice scents sail through the nostrils followed by some vanillin spice, dried herb and peppered earth notes. Juicy dark raspberry, liquorice and dark plum fruits overlay an earthy dark chocolate, vanillin spice and subtle peppered dried herb back drop. Fleshy and plush it has velvety tannins and a long, sumptuous finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews..
The much-loved and freakishly consistent Joshua a grenache, shiraz and mataro blend is again on form in the excellent '24 vintage. Juicy with plum, cranberry and raspberry fruits and layered with exotic spice and hints of dried citrus rind, blossom, dried meats and earth. Pure and plummy with a gentle slide into savoury on the finish, it's built for effortless consumption and it is at that which it excels. Drink by 2040.
95 Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2024 Elderton Ashmead Single Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
Rich and sumptuous yet underlyingly robust with a powerful and generously endowed finish.

Matured in French oak for 18 months. Pitch black dark red core with a dark red black tinged hue. Elevated blackcurrant and liquorice aromas mix with cigar box, black olive, earth and spice notes. Rich and sumptuous yet possessing an underlyingly robust structure, the medium to full bodied palate is flooded with blackcurrant and liquorice fruits. Subtlety smoked vanillin cedar, tobacco, earth and spicy mint elements sit in the background. Sturdy tannins impart mild grip across the powerful and generously endowed finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews
An elegant, fruit-pure, single-vineyard cabernet sauvignon from the Elderton estate in Nuriootpa, matured for 18 months in new and seasoned French oak. Deep crimson with aromas of blackberry, black cherry, boysenberry and blackcurrant over hints of five-spice, some distant blackcurrant pastille, cedar, dark chocolate, dried tobacco, vanillin oak, licorice, crushed herbs and roasting meats. Full bodied yet finely structured with wonderfully pure, slender black fruits, fine-grained tannins and a long draw of flavour on the finish. No problem tucking this one away in the cellar for an extended period. Drink by 2046.
95+ Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

Estate-grown at the Nuriootpa vineyard, the fruit is sourced from a single block planted around 1944. Deep alluvial silt over red and brown earth and limestone near the banks of the North Para River allows the vines to develop deep roots, so they need minimal irrigation. As a later-ripening variety, Cabernet Sauvignon often avoids the challenging weather conditions that can affect earlier varieties during budburst and flowering. In 2024, the 80-year-old vines produced a balanced crop, naturally moderated by their low vigor. Mild seasonal conditions required careful management throughout ripening, though significant rainfall did not arrive until after harvest. After hand-picking, the destemmed fruit spent one week in open fermenters with gentle cap management prior to pressing. The wine was then matured in new French oak hogsheads from trusted coopers, selected to support fruit expression and build structure while keeping oak influence restrained.
The 2024 Ashmead Single Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon leads with bay leaf, cassis and sweet pouch tobacco. There are notes too of shaved fennel, star anise and licorice, with gently minty, menthol-like notes that contribute freshness to the wine. The tannins are structural and silky, offering a supple framework to the fruit, which is balanced and long on the finish. The oak leaves a tiny pinch through the finish, but given this wine's capacity for graceful aging, one would expect it to soften in time. This is an excellent wine from a marvelous vintage. 14% alcohol, sealed under screw cap. Drink 2026-2044.
95 Points
Erin Larkin Robert Parkers The Wine Advocate

Another brilliant wine from the outstanding 2024 Barossa vintage. This is a stylish and expressive Cabernet Sauvignon that shows how well the variety can perform in excellent years. It comes from very old vines in fact, the oldest Cabernet Sauvignon vines on the estate. The aromatics are a classic blackcurrant and blackberry blend, with a faint leafy bay leaf character and a touch of black olive. The palate is seamlessly woven, with fine tannins and oak framing what is quite sumptuous fruit. The oak integration is spot on, and while it will clearly age well, it is already drinking beautifully. Drink 2026-2046.
96 points
Ray Jordan WinePilot.com
entry.g:title: 2024 Elderton Ashmead Single Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.g:description:
Rich and sumptuous yet underlyingly robust with a powerful and generously endowed finish.

Matured in French oak for 18 months. Pitch black dark red core with a dark red black tinged hue. Elevated blackcurrant and liquorice aromas mix with cigar box, black olive, earth and spice notes. Rich and sumptuous yet possessing an underlyingly robust structure, the medium to full bodied palate is flooded with blackcurrant and liquorice fruits. Subtlety smoked vanillin cedar, tobacco, earth and spicy mint elements sit in the background. Sturdy tannins impart mild grip across the powerful and generously endowed finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews
An elegant, fruit-pure, single-vineyard cabernet sauvignon from the Elderton estate in Nuriootpa, matured for 18 months in new and seasoned French oak. Deep crimson with aromas of blackberry, black cherry, boysenberry and blackcurrant over hints of five-spice, some distant blackcurrant pastille, cedar, dark chocolate, dried tobacco, vanillin oak, licorice, crushed herbs and roasting meats. Full bodied yet finely structured with wonderfully pure, slender black fruits, fine-grained tannins and a long draw of flavour on the finish. No problem tucking this one away in the cellar for an extended period. Drink by 2046.
95+ Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

Estate-grown at the Nuriootpa vineyard, the fruit is sourced from a single block planted around 1944. Deep alluvial silt over red and brown earth and limestone near the banks of the North Para River allows the vines to develop deep roots, so they need minimal irrigation. As a later-ripening variety, Cabernet Sauvignon often avoids the challenging weather conditions that can affect earlier varieties during budburst and flowering. In 2024, the 80-year-old vines produced a balanced crop, naturally moderated by their low vigor. Mild seasonal conditions required careful management throughout ripening, though significant rainfall did not arrive until after harvest. After hand-picking, the destemmed fruit spent one week in open fermenters with gentle cap management prior to pressing. The wine was then matured in new French oak hogsheads from trusted coopers, selected to support fruit expression and build structure while keeping oak influence restrained.
The 2024 Ashmead Single Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon leads with bay leaf, cassis and sweet pouch tobacco. There are notes too of shaved fennel, star anise and licorice, with gently minty, menthol-like notes that contribute freshness to the wine. The tannins are structural and silky, offering a supple framework to the fruit, which is balanced and long on the finish. The oak leaves a tiny pinch through the finish, but given this wine's capacity for graceful aging, one would expect it to soften in time. This is an excellent wine from a marvelous vintage. 14% alcohol, sealed under screw cap. Drink 2026-2044.
95 Points
Erin Larkin Robert Parkers The Wine Advocate

entry.title: 2024 Chateau Tanunda Grand Barossa Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich and seductively plush Barossa Shiraz.

Matured for 18 months in a combination of new and seasoned French and American oak barrels. Dense pitch black colour with a deep dark red black hue. Leaping from the glass are ripe blackberry, liquorice and black cherry aromas which intermingle with vanillin cedar and peppered fennel notes. Rich, opulent and concentrated, the palate is awash with lush black cherry, liquorice and blackberry fruits. Spicy vanillin cedar, fennel and blackpepper elements line the back half. Showing ample power and depth it has velvet smooth tannins and a long, seductively plush finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews..
A definite contender for best value of the year, this is compelling evidence that one can drink extremely well, wines chock full of flavour, without breaking the bank. Maturation is usually for around fifteen months in a mix of new and older French and American oak. Opaque maroon in colour, on the nose we have notes of plums and mulberries, soy, tobacco leaves, coffee grinds, sarsaparilla and blackcurrants. There is a sleek texture through to the satiny tannins and the wine has excellent length. Seamless and finely balanced, this is delicious drinking now and will surely remain so for at least ten to fifteen years, if you can keep your hands off it that long. Cracking value. Drink 2026-2041.
94 Points
Ken Gargett WinePilot.com

entry.title: Sullivans Cove Single Cask TD0392 French Oak Second Fill Single Malt Australian Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary: The distillery's French Oak Second-Fill casks have a history as rich as their flavour. Initially serving as first-fill ex-Tawny casks for an earlier batch of single malt, the best casks are then selected for a second round of maturation, hence the title "Second Fill" or "Re-fill". Because their impact on the flavour profile is muted, refill casks make a good canvas for showing off distillate character. In fact, they're a staff favourite at the distillery for that very reason. French Oak Second Fill TD0392 was distilled in February of 2013 and decanted in October of 2025. The outturn was 471 bottles at 49% Alc./Vol. Non-chill filtered.

entry.title: 2022 Matias Riccitelli Viejos Vinedos en Pie Franco Malbec
entry.summary:
Founded in 2009 in Las Compuertas, Mendoza, Matas Riccitelli produces site-focused wines from high-altitude, ungrafted old vineyards across Mendoza and Patagonia. Winemaking centers on low intervention, using native yeasts, concrete eggs, and neutral oak to highlight freshness, natural texture, and vineyard character over heavy oak or over-extraction. The portfolio spans nuanced single-vineyard Malbecs alongside revived heritage varieties like Criolla Chica, Torronts, and old-vine Smillon.

Crafted from unrooted vines planted as early as 1908 in Las Compuertas and Vistalba, this wine showcases the depth of historic, agroecologically managed vineyards. Native fermentation in concrete vats and 16 months in French oak deliver a nuanced, deeply structured Malbec.

Other Reviews...
Fresh blackberries, spiced dark fruit, oranges, hazelnut chocolate and a touch of waffles. More of a classic style but so expressive and well made, with superfine tannins and a very long finish. Drink or hold.
96 points
Zekun Shuai - JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: G.E. Massenez Creme de Cacao (Cocoa) Liqueur (500ml) - DAMAGED LABEL
entry.summary:
Crme de Cacao or chocolate liqueur is manufactured by maceration or percolation of cacao (cocoa)beans followed by distillation and sweetening. As with coffee, the best results are obtained by blending beans from different areas. It is available as either a colourless or brown liquid, the brown version often containing vanilla.

The history of cocoa and chocolate is well known to date back to the Aztecs of South America. The plumed serpent is said to have bought it back from the Lost Paradise. By consuming it one attained universal knowledge and wisdom. It came into vogue in Europe as a liqueur from the seventeenth century on, often being drunk through a thick layer of cream floating on the surface.

Uncompromising on quality, G.E. Massenez is today universally acclaimed for his 'eaux de vie' (fruit brandies) as well as his crme liqueurs. The company has won many awards at international exhibitions. 25% alc/vol

entry.title: 2024 Greenock Creek Grenache Blanc
entry.summary:
Glossy textured pear and red apple fruits with a refreshing mineral edged finish.

Brilliant pale straw to straw colour with a subtle glimmer of green to the edges and a watery hue. Aromas of pear and red apple drift from the glass with hints of lime, quince and spice also evident. Delicious pear and red apple fruits are to the fore carrying with them a glossy textural feel. Delicate lime, quince and wet stone elements line the back half. Nicely integrated acidity lends a brisk feel to the refreshing mineral edged finish.
Drink over the next 1-2 years.
Alc. 13.5%

Other Reviews
An impressive new wine in the Greenock Creek line-up; a single-vineyard grenache blanc from the edge of Marananga, made with extended skin contact in the press and fermented/matured in equal parts clay amphora and stainless steel. Pale straw with bright grapefruit, pear and citrus characters with hints of meadow flowers, crme frache, a light dusting of ginger spice, crushed stone and lime zest. That pithy textural aspect is dialled in beautifully here; the wine leans dry and savoury on the back end with a minerally cadence. Super stuff! Drink by 2031.
93+ Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: Matsui Mizunara Cask Single Malt Japanese Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary:
Produced at the Kurayoshi Distillery in Tottori Prefecture, the Matsui range was introduced around 2018 to critical acclaim. This is a lower ABV version of the original award winning whisky which was bottled at 48%. For some of the talk dismissing Japan's Mizunara oak as just another marketing gimmick, there is something quite sensuous about the overall delivery here that is almost unlike any other. The spirit caresses the tongue, the malt has a light, vanilla-wafer-biscuit touch; dried coconut and purring spices unfurl with hints of cigar box, followed by a burst of crisp apple, fading on an exotic wood note. Though not particularly long, this is exquisite form for what must be predominantly young malt (Kurayoshi only started distilling their own whisky in 2017). The export label features Katsushika Hokusais Thirty Six Views of Mount Fuji with a fly-by of red-crowned cranes, native to Japan. Tasted from a 20ml sample.

Other reviews... slightly less bold and challenging than previous years, this is still an absorbing single malt, though perhaps now with a preponderance of toffee. However to say that it is anything less than delightful and an absolute treat would be both churlish and inaccurate. 91.5 points - Jim Murray's Whisky Bible 2025-26

entry.title: 2022 Craiglee Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich yet savoury and elegant with a long, peppery finish.

Midnight black heart with a dark red black tinged hue. Pronounced blackberry and liquorice aromas infused with a mix of blackpepper, smoked meats, toasty vanillin cedar, black olive and clove stream through the nostrils with ample volume. Richly fruited yet simultaneously elegant and highly finessed in its flow across the mid weighted palate. Blackberry, liquorice and blackpepper flavours meld into a smoky vanillin cedar, scorched earth, black olive and spicy clove back drop. Slightly grainy in its feel with well integrated tannins and fresh underlying acidity providing great structure for longer term cellaring. Concludes long savoury and peppery.
Drink over the next 10-12 years,
Alc. 13.5%

Other Reviews..
Glorious Craiglee shiraz. Nothing like it. This is incredibly fresh and lively, with wonderful aromas of florals and spice, especially black pepper, with dark fruit to the fore. Its savoury and mid-weighted with textural tannins and lithe acidity. Quite delicious now, but as is the way with this producer, built for the long haul. Drink by 2038.
96 Points
Jane Faulkner James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

Proper stuff. Done the Craiglee way.
Moody, brooding, rich and grippy. A proper Craiglee release with all the mettle of a wine destined for dusty cellaring and a slow reveal of its potential. Chewy tannin laced with slate, smoky spice, dark cherry and stewed plum characters, black olive, choc-mint, clove, new leather and game meat all in abundance and yet controlled and flowing in a sumptuous slip. Flavour plus and coolness through the finish a boon. Big glasses, watch the evolution, hold tight to the six pack. Fantastic wine. Drink 2026-2040+
96 Points
Mike Bennie The Wine Front

Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 14%

entry.title: 2024 Solitude Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Rich, powerful and silky yet light on its feet.

Red to dark red colour with a light red hue. Pretty violet, red to dark cherry and strawberry aromas drift through the olfactory senses with good intensity followed by some clove, forest floor and spicy bramble notes. Rich, powerful and silky yet light on its feet, the palate features delicious dark cherry and strawberry fruits over a subtle anise, dried herb, forest floor and spicy cedar back drop. Polished tannins with a long, supple finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13%

entry.title: 2024 Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
A richly fruited Margaret River Cabernet that shows impressive weight, flesh and concentration yet has a refined finish.

Established in 1967, Vasse Felix is one of Margaret Rivers founding estates. Known as the son of Vasse Felix Cabernet Sauvignon the Filius Cabernet Sauvignon is made in a more fruit forward style designed for earlier drinking. The 2023 vintage is a blend of 85% Cabernet Sauvignon, 12% Malbec and 3% Merlot matured in a combination of 1-7 year old French oak barriques for a period of 10-12 months.
Midnight black heart with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Aromas of blackcurrant, ripe mulberry and liquorice engulf the nostrils mixing with some earthy black olive, gentle tobacco and spicy cedar notes. Rich blackcurrant and ripe mulberry fruits carry impressive weight, flesh and concentration across the palate. Youthfully inky yet juicy feel with liquorice, cedary tobacco, earthy dried herb and spicy black olive elements lending further nuance. Fine grained tannins impose a sense of sturdiness across the long generous yet refined finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews..
Let this breathe to coax out the varietal flavours. The 12% malbec in the mix is strong and lovely all plums and leather with a whiff of formic acid/crushed-ant character. But cabernet rules with its leafy freshness, mulberries, spice and menthol. The mid-weighted palate is supple thanks to neatly shaped tannins, and it feels plush throughout. Drink by 2034.
92 Points
Jane Faulkner - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2025 Holm Oak Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Light, supple and fresh with juicy red fruits and an elegant finish.

Semi translucent red to dark red colour with black toned edges and a light red hue. Fragrant red cherry, subtle violet and strawberry scents are trailed by fresh herb, subtle forest floor and spice notes. Light, supple and fresh, juicy red cherry and strawberry fruits are featured over a brambly forest floor, rhubarb and spicy dried herb back drop. Polished tannins with an elegant red fruited finish of good length.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13%

Other Reviews..
Theres a real brightness and energy about this wine, with its burst of dark cherry and strawberry, with a little raspberry character. The palate has such vibrant fruit intensity balanced with some nice subtle oak and a necessary crunchy acidity that gives it life and energy through to the finish. That complexity and textural feel have come from the wild ferments and regular hand plunging four times a day. Lovely wine of great vibrancy. Drink 2026-2032.
94 Points
Ray Jordan WinePilot.com

entry.title: 2024 Rob Hall Full Moon Vineyard Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Light, savoury and elegant.

Semi translucent red to dark red colour with black toned edges and a light red to brick red tinged hue. Spicy red to dark cherry and rhubarb aromas intermix with bramble, dried herb, forest floor and dried meat notes. Light and savoury, the palate is elegantly detailed with dark cherry, rhubarb and strawberry fruits. Lying beneath are dried herb, brambly cedar, forest floor and spice elements. Fine grained tannins with a savoury complexity to the medium to long conclusion.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 13.5%

Other Reviews..
From the Full Moon vineyard in Gladysdale, and a new wine for Rob Hall; 10% whole bunches and matured in seasoned puncheons. Bright garnet. A little closed initially before revealing aromas of red and blue fruits together with some spice and savoury notes. There's good depth on the nicely structured, medium-bodied palate and I can see this only getting better over the next four to six years at least. Drink by 2031.
94 Points
Philip Rich - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2025 Jasper Hill Georgia's Paddock Shiraz
entry.summary:
Other Reviews...
Year after year this wine delivers, and the 2025 is no exception. Theres lovely depth and concentration cut with freshness and purity, giving classic Heathcote shiraz notes of blackberry, mulberry, dried herbs, red brick, bitter chocolate and a spicy earthy undertone. The palate is firmly framed yet layered with silky tannins and class, leading to a long, decadent yet restrained finish. Excellent now but will reward with cellaring. Drink or hold.
99 points
Ryan Montgomery - JamesSuckling.com

Black fruit, dark chocolate, dried herb, aniseed, dried flowers, a distinct steely note. Its full-bodied, blackberry, a deep ferrous grip to tannin, fresh berry acidity pops through it, iron and liquorice richness, with ripe sooty tannin closing out a finish of excellent length. This is a wine of substance and impact. Its quite something. Superb. Drink 2028 - 2045+.
96 points
Gary Walsh - The Wine Front

entry.title: 2026 Forest Hill Vineyard Riesling
entry.summary:
Long and zesty with terrific drive and concentration.

A blend of sites across Forest Hill Vineyard, including the first harvest from two new plantings, an extension to Block 1 and a site planted with cuttings from another of the regions best vineyards.
Brilliant very pale straw colour with green tinted edges and a watery hue. Aromas of lime, citrus and green apple leap out of the glass with great intensity trailed by some talc and chalky mineral notes. Scrumptious lime, citrus, green apple and orange rind fruits engulf the mouth underscored by racy acidity. Chalky talc and steely mineral elements line the back half. Boasting terrific drive and concentration it finishes long and zesty.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 12.5%

entry.title: 2004 Penfolds Bin 60A Magnum (1500ml)
entry.summary:
Other Reviews.
The release of the 2004 Bin 60A following the epic 1962 Bin 60A is old news now, but the wine was looking very fine indeed when I tasted it so I thought Id add a note. Blended of 56% Coonawarra Cabernet from Block 20 and 44% Barossa Shiraz from Koonunga Hill Block 56G and Kalimna Blocks 4 and 14, the wine was matured in 100% new American oak hogsheads for 13 months. Very deep purple-black in color, it offers restrained notes of game, smoked meat, earth, blackberry and black currant liqueurs, yeast, marmite-toast plus whiffs of dried lavender, cedar and bark. Very crisp, very tight and very firm, this taut medium-bodied wine is still all structure at this stage, going very long and earthy in the finish. Give it time and consider broaching it from 2014. It should drink well into the 2030s if not beyond.

With a lot of changes happening around the Fosters Group, it is business as usual at Penfoldswhich seems to operate within its own world. But this is no small world. The vineyard holdings here are vast and the connections with growers go back generations. Chief winemaker Peter Gago is the very well spoken front-man for the production team backed-up Kym Schroeter in charge of the whites and Steve Lienert crafting some very fine, consistent and sometimes inspired reds. If Champagne is all about the art of blending, then Penfolds is the Champagne of Australian wine. Those that think large companies producing wines that emphasize blending cant make great wines need to think about the Champagne model or simply try some of Penfolds top wines to become believers. That said check out their recent single vineyard release: the very special 2004 Block 42 Kalimna Cabernet Sauvignon, the first release of a wine made purely from this 100+ year old single block (perhaps the oldest block of Cabernet in the world?) since 1996. Drink 2014 - 2030.

99+ points
Lisa Perrotti-Brown Robert Parkers The Wine Advocate

entry.title: Jacopo Poli Po' Elegant Pinot Grappa (700ml) - DAMAGED GIFT BOX
entry.summary:
The highly regarded Jacopo Poli distillery is an artisan operation solely owned by the Poli family, founded in 1898 in Schiavon, near Bassano del Grappa, in the hearth of Veneto, the most typical region for grappa production.

Tasting note: Produced from Pinot grapes. Clear, silvery appearance. Opening aromas are slightly soapy, with notes of pine and lavender. After several minutes they become more fresh grape like and herbal. Soft entry leads into a semi sweet, light to medium bodied profile that includes spicy dried fruit and nut flavours and fresh herbal notes. Very gently warming spirit. Subtle dried fruit aftertaste. Concludes minerally and dry. 40% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2025 Domaine Christian Moreau Chablis
entry.summary:
Domaine Christian Moreau is one of the most respected names in Chablis blessed with magnificent vineyard holdings in the best areas of Chablis. The highlights are undoubtedly the amazing range of Grand cru vineyards including one single holding of approximately 3 hectares in Les Clos as well as 0.41 hectares of Clos des Hospices dans Les Clos plus slightly smaller holdings in Valmur, Blanchots and Vaudesir. The wines are gaining in even clearer expression with the vineyards having been certified organic since 2013 and together with some new tanks and other investments the results are showing clearly in the wines with each vintage. These are wines of precision, crystal clear typicity, and elegance that will age classically while enabling tremendous enjoyment throughout their lives.

Other Reviews...
The 2025 Chablis Village, which comes from purchased fruit, has a well-defined nose with citrus peel and subtle leesy scents, a touch of sea spray in the background. The palate has commendable weight, a little spicier than expected, with hints of mango and apricot furnishing the finish. This has an easy-going quality to it. Drink 2027-2032.
87-89 points
Neal Martin - Vinous

entry.title: 2024 Novum Riverbrook Vineyard Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Rich, full and texturally enveloping feel yet underlyingly fresh.

From a family who have been managing vineyards in Marlborough since the 1970's, after a significant stint at Fromm winery, ending as General Manager, Will Hoare and his wife Rachel decided to venture out on their own to produce wine from the incredible vineyards they had access to. For this wine fruit was sourced from a block in the central Wairau plains of Marlborough planted entirely with the Mendoza clone around the mid 1980s. Originally a riverbed, this block is naturally warm during the day, as well as at night, thanks to the radiating effect of the exposed greywacke rock lying beneath the vines. The rock radiates heat up into the canopy, making this vineyard an ideal site for ripening Chardonnay.
Brilliant pale straw colour with a watery hue. Intense peach, honeycomb and crme brulee scents are married to hints of bacon fat, nougat, cashew and spice. Rich, full and texturally enveloping, the palate is engulfed with ripe peach, honeycomb and pear flavours which meld into a citrusy crme brulee, nougat, subtle cashew and flint back drop. Creamy in its feel yet underlyingly fresh, it finishes long and expansive.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews
There is real powdered spice to this wine. Powder ginger, turmeric and cumin. A backbone of yellow peach flesh and golden baked apples. Fruit is ripe, with a twitch of fruit nectar rounding out a full palate. Oak spice is savoury and suits the tones of orchard fruit. A very memorable wine for its shape and grandeur. A touch of white pepper warmth on the finish. Drink by 2032.
95 Points
Shanteh Wale - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

This is very fresh and alluring with precise fruit and lovely ground spice notes melding beautifully. White peach, grapefruit, pear, ground cinnamon, nutmeg, nectarine pulp, powdery peach skin, flint. It deepens with air to reveal apricot kernel, nougat, tangerine, water chestnut and a mineral element the amalgam of which makes for a very interesting and complex perfume. The palate is at once intense and fresh with stone fruit and spice in the lead again with notes largely akin to the nose, along with a sweet essence of lemon curd and tangerine adding a sense of completeness. Theres some powdery phenolics and a good wash of orange-citrus acidity through a finish of crystalline length. This is very impressive complex, charming, long and utterly moreish. Brilliant.
95 Points
Tom Kline WinePilot.com

The 2024 Chardonnay is excellent. It's toasty and spicy, lean and nutty, with green apple acidity and attractive waxy phenolics that shape the mid-palate and finish. This is a beautiful wine, made as a result of thoughtful farming and endeavour. It has personality and charm, alongside length of flavor and complexity to boot. It's leaner and less obviously "worked" than many Chardonnays I see coming out of Marlborough. This is super and comes recommended. 14% alcohol, sealed Diam and wax.
94+ Points
Erin Larkin Robert Parkers The Wine Advocate

entry.title: 2025 Paralian Marmont Vineyard Blewitt Springs Grenache
entry.summary:
Tense yet powerful with muscular tannins and a long, succulent yet chiselled finish.

Dark red core with black tinged edges and a vibrant red to dark red hue. Pronounced dark raspberry, liquorice and black cherry scents jump out of the glass trailed by some ripe blueberry, earth and peppered herb notes. Juicy dark raspberry, liquorice and blueberry fruits are underpinned by bright acidity which imparts a fresh feel. Vanillin spice, scorched earth and pepper elements are scattered across the back half. Tense yet powerful, it has muscular tannins and a long succulent yet chiselled finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews..
From 1960s vines in Blewitt Springs planted to Holocene sand; 20% whole bunch, about 21 days on skins, then 10 months in an old 2500L foudre. Theres a compactness to this, a quietness on opening, fruit enmeshed presently, but theres concentration, balance and prettiness within. Cranberry, ripe raspberry, damson plum, marasca cherry, some darker cherry, too. Hints of dusky rose, ground cinnamon, white pepper, brown cardamom, bitter herbs, the palate buoyant yet intense, the fine-boned tannins and enlivening acidity invigorating. Theres a lot yet to unfurl, but its all there. Drink by 2037.
96 Points
Marcus Ellis - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: Hellyers Road Distillery American Oak 10 Year Old Single Malt Australian Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary: Other reviews... Being matured exclusively in ex-bourbon casks means the character of the spirit itself and the grains it was distilled from should shine here, uncomplicated by fortified wine or aggressive oak. Here, the oak is pretty dominant in a saw-dusty, sappy sort of way, and it still smells incredibly fresh for having spent so long in the cask with plenty of fresh peach goodness. At 46.2% its pretty hard on the palate without a lot of the creaminess or complexity youd expect from a whisky of this age, but there are some nice grain and vanilla notes through the finish. 84 points - winecompanion.com.au

entry.summary:
A grippy, mid weighted Chianti with a dry, rustic finish.

Sourced from the estates oldest vineyards with ageing taking place in small oak barrels for a period of 24 months. Very deep black dark red colour with a dark red hue. Uplifted aromas of blackcurrant, liquorice and earth are intermeshed with tobacco, dusty cedar, dried herbs and spicy leather. Mid weighted, blackcurrant and dark cherry fruits are framed by a sturdy tannin structure. Notions of earth, leather, old cedar, tobacco and spice extend across the back half. Grippy feel with a dry, rustic finish.
Drink over the next 3-4 years.
Alc. 14%

entry.title: 2024 Provenance Golden Plains Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Light and savoury with an elegant mid length conclusion.

Dark red in colour with black shaded edges and a red to dark red hue. Aromas of dark cherry and strawberry infused with spicy clove emanate from the glass trailed by some earthy graphite and smoked meat like notes. Light and savoury the palate features red cherry and rhubarb fruits which meld into a clove, forest floor, smoked meat and spice back drop. Fine grained tannins with an elegant mid length conclusion.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.4%

Other Reviews
Fruit is 60/30/10% Geelong/Henty/Ballarat. A medium, bright crimson red. Brightly fruited with its aromas of red and black fruits, some whole-bunch-derived green peppercorn notes and a little dried rose. Medium bodied, and like the other '24 Provenance pinots, this will need six months or so for the tannins to soften. A well-priced pinot to drink now and over the next three to four years. Drink by 2030.
93 Points
Philip Rich - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: Bruichladdich Octomore 14.2 Cask Strength Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml) - DAMAGED GIFT TUBE
entry.summary:
Other reviews... A robust puff of smoke and tobacco leaf are met marvelously by sweeter, softer notes lemon pound cake, cinnamon-sugar toast, red berries, and pomegranate. Theres tremendous char on the palate, but its balanced by a beautiful sweetness thats akin to mint tea and campfire smoke. The finish has a hint of meatiness, plenty of pepper, coffee beans, and iodine, and it all comes together exceedingly well. 93 points - whiskyadvocate.com

...The same 128.9 ppm malting and also 5 years old, but here the aging is all European, completed in 40% oloroso sherry hogsheads, 16% first-fill Amarone casks, and 44% second-fill Amarone casks. That explains the delightful pink color on this whisky, one of the prettiest Ive encountered in a while. Much lighter and fruit-driven on the nose than 14.1, this whisky melds red fruits and berries with black pepper and mixed spice notes, leaning toward tobacco over time. The palate isnt nearly as burly as the 14.1 is, though a drop or two of water is still a good idea to temper the hefty proof just a bit. Fresh biscuits and almond cookies kick things off on the tongue, more red fruit here closer to strawberry coming along in short order. While coming across as far less peaty than 14.1, the palate still has plenty of bonfire smoke and salty sea spray on offer, tempered again by strawberry cream, then a nougat note. Such a lively journey to go on. My favorite whisky in this lineup. 115.4 proof. - drinkhacker.com

entry.title: Hellyer's Road Distillery Coffee Whisky Cream Liqueur (700ml)

entry.title: 2025 Home Hill Estate Landslide Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Home Hill is one of your classic Australian vineyard retreats that functions as both a serious winery and a charming getaway with restaurant included. The focus here is primarily on Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sylvaner and Sparkling wine, but their track record really shines with Pinot. Over the years they have clearly established themselves as one of Tasmanias best and most consistent producers of the varietal, culminating in their 2014 Home Hill Reserve Pinot Noir taking out the Jimmy Watson Trophy.

Rich, silky and powerful yet light on its feet this a super seductive Tassie Pinot.

The Landslide Pinot Noir is sourced from newer plantings and is fermented and raised in mostly old French barriques for 8 months. Dark red in colour with black toned edges and a vibrant crimson red hue. Perfumed like aromatics of violet, red to dark cherry, strawberry and anise flood the olfactory senses followed by some fresh herb, forest floor, subtle brambly cedar and spice notes. Rich, silky and powerful yet light on its feet, moreish red to dark cherry, strawberry and anise flavours meld into a fresh herb infused back drop of forest floor, bramble and spicy cedar. Seamlessly integrated, velvet smooth tannins. Long and expansive, the finish is one of exceptional fruit purity that exudes freshness.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.8%

entry.title: 2025 Domaine Christian Moreau Petit Chablis
entry.summary:
Domaine Christian Moreau is one of the most respected names in Chablis blessed with magnificent vineyard holdings in the best areas of Chablis. The highlights are undoubtedly the amazing range of Grand cru vineyards including one single holding of approximately 3 hectares in Les Clos as well as 0.41 hectares of Clos des Hospices dans Les Clos plus slightly smaller holdings in Valmur, Blanchots and Vaudesir. The wines are gaining in even clearer expression with the vineyards having been certified organic since 2013 and together with some new tanks and other investments the results are showing clearly in the wines with each vintage. These are wines of precision, crystal clear typicity, and elegance that will age classically while enabling tremendous enjoyment throughout their lives.

The Petit Chablis vines are located at the top of the hill of Grand Crus only metres from the Grand cru Valmur, with another very small 0.4 hectare planting also at the crest of the hill of Grand Crus (just above Vaudesir) that the Moreau family have planted more recently.

Other Reviews...
The 2025 Petit Chablis had been bottled three weeks before my visit in June. This has a fragrant nose with lime and citrus fruit, with just a touch of nectarine. The palate is well balanced with a tangy entry, a fine thread of acidity and a lively, lychee-tinged finish. It will be difficult to resist, so why bother? Drink 2026-2030.
88 points
Neal Martin - Vinous

entry.title: 2023 Paul Conti Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
Concentrated, deeply fruited and grippy.

Impenetrable inky black heart with a very deep dark red black hue. Lifted blackcurrant, mulberry and liquorice aromas are interwoven with cedary tobacco, black olive and spice notes. Rich, concentrated blackcurrant and liquorice fruits are framed by firm tannins. Vanillin cedar, tobacco, minty earth and spice elements form the underbelly. Concludes long, deeply fruited and grippy.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews..
No mistaking this is cabernet, and cabernet from the heart of Margaret River, not far from Cowaramup. A small amount of malbec, that often-unheralded blending partner, adds to the palates depth. The result is quite soft but still structured, with deep fruit characters. A touch of bay leaf and olive tapenade adds complexity. It will handle medium-term cellaring but is ideal for early drinking.
92 Points
RayJordanWine.com.au

entry.title: Suntory Ao Limited Irish Edition World Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary: Suntory released its inaugural World Whisky, the Suntory Ao, in 2019, made using whiskies that the Suntory Group owns across the five major whisky producing regions of Scotland, US, Canada, Japan and Ireland. In mid 2026, building on the success of the original, Suntory released Ao Irish Edition, which, as the name suggests, places Irish whiskey at the heart of the blend. Liquid is sourced from Beam Suntory's Cooley Distillery for a fruitier, lighter, and more approachable profile than the standard Ao release. There's also none of the smokiness. It's the first in a new World Travel Collection series aiming to highlight the unique characteristics of each of the world's five major whisk(e)y categories. 43% Alc./Vol.

entry.summary: Compiled from a distinctive blend of casks that previously held Australian Pinot Noir, Bourbon and Fondillon wine. The profile offers lush pineapple up front, warm oak and dried fruit underneath and a finish that feels like late afternoon sun in White Bay. 38% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2024 Turkey Flat Butcher’s Block Grenache Shiraz Mataro
entry.summary:
Rich and juicy with a long, generously fruited finish.

Matured for 12 months in French oak hogsheads and puncheons. Deep dark red black tinged core with a red to dark red hue. Dark raspberry, ripe dark cherry and liquorice scents jump out of the glass followed by some vanillin spice notes. Rich and juicy, the mid weighted palate features dark raspberry, cherry, liquorice and dark plum fruits over a subtle earth and vanillin spice back drop. Nicely fleshed it has polished tannins and ample underlying freshness. Long, generously fruited finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews
This is a hit. This is a buy. This is $27 well spent.
Raspberries and rust, florals and aromatic herbs, a slip of chocolate and dives into deeper, darker berry flavours. This is lively, pretty and solid at once; it has a bit of a negroni-Campari-orange aspect to it; its easy-going but it has substance. Drink 2026-2030+
92 Points
Campbell Mattinson The Wine Front

entry.title: 2023 Eric Bordelet Poire Granit Pear Cider (Perry)
entry.summary:
Eric Bordelet approaches Cider-making with the same intensity as a passionate oenologist brings to winemaking. Bordelet worked as sommelier in the leading 3 star Parisian restaurant, Arpege where he became deeply familiar with the top winemakers and wineries of France. In 1992 he took over the tiny patch of family farmed orchards in Charchign, in the heart of Normandys premium Cider producing area. Since then he has set about rescuing the ancient heirloom varieties of pears and apples that produce tiny quantities and amazing flavour.

Working organically, the fruit is dry-farmed, as Bordelet prefers to work with tiny very flavoursome apples and pears. The fruit we work with looks quite different from what you'll find in the grocery store. I know what each apple variety brings to the cider. says Eric, explaining that some Ciders can have about 20 different varieties used. And he adds, I use about 40% of sweet apples, 40% bitter apples and 20% of acidic apples to get the right balance.

His ciders are deliberately made in a very gently sparkling petillant style and do not have the same level of effervescence as many other ciders. This is a conscious decision on Bordelet's part, I want it this way because it shows off the fruit character better.

Produced from pear trees estimated to be about 300 years old. Poir Granit has 25-80 grams of sugar per liter, yet it doesn't taste particularly sweet. This is due to the tannin and acidity, which Bordelet says is twice as high as the apple. Stunning as aperitif or with cheese or desserts, the low alcohol also means this can be enjoyed any time. Cider simply doesn't get better than this!

entry.title: Puss & Mew Distillery Distichon Port Barrel Release Australian Single Malt Whisky (500ml)
entry.summary: Named after Hordeum distichon (the scientific name for 2-row barley), this whisky spent time in first-fill casks from Portugal. Port pick-up is well-defined on the nose, sweet yet savoury, yielding mixed ripe berries over a deep vanilla backdrop. Slightly tense on entry, relaxing into a superb, port-soaked plum pudding delivery with hints of cinnamon and pepper. An undercurrent of dark chocolate carries the residual fortified fruitiness, coating the mouth. Fine tannins and oak spices bring structure to the whole. Excellent new Australian whisky. 44% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2024 Fromm Chenin Blanc
entry.summary:
Juicy pear, green to red apple and lime fruits with fresh acidity lending an energetic feel.

Certified organic. Brilliant pale straw colour with green tinged edges and a watery hue. Pronounced ripe pear and baked apple aromas intermingle with honeysuckle, quince and subtle cinnamon spice notes. Juicy pear, green to red apple and lime fruits are underscored by a vein of fresh acidity which lends an energetic feel. Subtle quince and stony mineral elements linger across the refreshing finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.5%

Other Reviews..
Plenty of dried apple, white peach and stone aromas that follow through to a medium body with layers of fruit and a stony finish. Lots of citrus. Crisp and round at the same time. Tangy at the end. Drink now.
93 Points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2024 Dalrymple Estate Vineyard Pipers River Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Light yet powerful and expansive with a long, savoury red to dark fruited finish.

Deep dark red core with black toned edges and a red to dark red hue. Aromas of violet, dark cherry, strawberry and rhubarb are delivered with a perfumed like intensity followed by anise, brambly cedar, dried herb and spice notes. Dark cherry, strawberry and red plum fruits are light in body but powerful and expansive in their flow across the palate. Subtle anise, spicy cedar, forest floor and fresh herb elements line the back half. Possessing an underlying freshness it has fine grained tannins and a long savoury red to dark fruited finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 13.5%

Other Reviews
Tasmania's fifth appearance in our Best In Show selection is also its third Pinot Noir in as many years; two additional whites (a Riesling and a Chardonnay) were featured back in the 2017 and 2019 DWWA editions respectively. This wine is relatively deep in colour, with ample soft red fruit aromatic sweetness (cherries and strawberries); there are rose-petal floral notes, too, as well as cedar and graphite notes from fine-coopered oak. The 2024 vintage was mild and settled, with a generous ripening window, and the harmony and limpidity of flavour that comes from a season of that sort are much in evidence here. The Tasmanian difference, perhaps, is evident in a tightening towards the end of the palate as some sour cherry acidity creeps in to bring the flavour sweep towards a focused finish. A Pinot of style and verve.
97 points
Best in Show Decanter World Wine Awards 2026

A single-vineyard pinot noir from Pipers River, looking very good indeed in the strong '24 vintage. Characters of wild strawberry, dark cherry and plum fruits with a curl of struck-flint reduction and hints of exotic spice, Chinese barbecue shop, mountain herbs, citrus blossom, pomegranate, subtle leaf litter tones, dried meats and turned earth. Silky and beautifully weighted with a lovely saline mineral cadence and a sweep of sour cherry and spice on the exit. Drink by 2041.
95 points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2024 Barwon Ridge Marsanne
entry.summary:
A rich and texturally viscous Marsanne.

Brilliant straw colour with green flashed edges and a watery hue. Wafting from the glass are ripe peach, apricot and honeycomb scents which are complimented by some toast and ginger spice notes. Rich and texturally viscous, the palate is loaded with luscious peach, apricot and honeycomb fruits which meld into a bacon fat, nougat and ginger spice back drop. Balancing acidity counterpoints what is a long, full and creamy conclusion.
Drink over the next 2-3 years.
Alc. 13.5%

entry.title: 2025 Sons of Eden Pumpa Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
Rich, deeply fruited and sturdily built.

A blend of 87% Cabernet Sauvignon, 12% Shiraz and 1% Cabernet Franc sourced from vines aged between 37-48 years old with maturation taking place in a mix of new and seasoned oak hogsheads.
Impenetrable inky black in colour with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Intense blackcurrant, tobacco and dried herb aromas jump out of the glass followed by some cedar, black olive and spicy earth notes. Rich fleshy blackcurrant, mulberry and more subtle liquorice fruits are framed by a sturdy tannin structure. Cedary tobacco, dried herb, earthy black olive and spice elements unfold across the back half. Concludes with a deeply fruited yet refined finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.5%

entry.title: 2025 Credaro Kinship Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Mid weighted and nicely fleshed with an energetically flinty finish.

Matured for 9 months in French oak, 25% new, with regular lees stirring. Brilliant pale straw colour with green highlighted edges and a watery hue. Lifted aromas of nectarine and grapefruit are trailed by some citrus, faint biscuity oak and gun flint. Nicely fleshed, the mid weighted palate features concentrated nectarine, pear and grapefruit flavours over a delicate biscuity oak and gun flint infused back drop. Fresh acidity lending an energetic feel across the flinty, mid length finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 13%

Other Reviews..
Beautifully captures the allure of Margaret River Chardonnay: the luscious fruit drive and oyster-like salinity that brings with it a beachy Margs vibe. And then there are the savoury nutty overtones. But first to the aromas, lively and deep, in yellow peach, nectarine, citrus, creme brle with a flurry of almond meal. Its a richer style of Chardonnay that comes with a distinctive savouriness in preserved lemon, almond skin, nuts and grippy citrus peel and pith. Theres plenty of flavour here, nicely concentrated, and it just goes and goes. A grippy, pithy tartness mixes with a lemony saline character working the tastebuds, while the nutty lees add extra depth. Oak features as a seasoning only allowing the fruit free rein. Drink 2026-2033.
94 Points
Jeni Port WinePilot.com

entry.title: Bruichladdich The Classic Laddie 10 Year Old Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary:
First offered as a Tenner back in 2011, but at a lower ABV, the distillery's signature bottling returns, now bottled at 50%. Its predecessor was a favourite entry-level Islayer , dangerously drinkable and not particularly expensive. Expect the same here. Showcasing the classic, floral and elegant Bruichladdich house style, it's made from 100% Scottish barley, trickle distilled, non-chill filtered and colouring free. 

Other reviews... Nose: Its fresh and bright with waxy orchard fruits of apples and pears in abundance along with peach, honey, floral meadows, dry grass and light oak. Palate: Its those orchard fruits again, but more sweet juicy red apples this time and theres lemon citrus bringing the sour too. Theres a peppery spice, but its never too assertive and is joined by honey, creamy vanilla and salt. The finish is creamy, with oak and green apple skins. The green apple note lingers for an age on the palate...This is undoubtedly good, spirit-forward whisky with plenty of flavour. Theres a really nice light and fruity profile and I love that we get 50% ABV here rather than the integrity base of 46%.  - dramface.com

entry.title: 2023 Greenock Creek Cornerstone Grenache
entry.summary:
A ripe, generously fruited Grenache that has an underlying freshness to it.

Deep dark red core with black tinged edges and a dark red hue. Pronounced black raspberry, liquorice and dark cherry scents engulf the nostrils trailed by some scorched earth, vanillin spice and subtle pepper notes. Rich, juicy black raspberry, liquorice and dark cherry fruits are intermeshed with scorched earth, vanillin spice and pepper characters. Refined velvet like tannins with a ripe, generously fruited finish that has an underlying freshness to it.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews..
Old bush-vine grenache from Marananga, bright crimson in the glass and packed with characters of raspberry, red plum and cranberry fruits along with hints of ginger cake, exotic spice, orange blossom, dried citrus peel and earth. Bright, compact, fresh and delicious, with fine, powdery tannin, abundant energy and a real ease of drinking.
93 Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2020 Greenock Creek Roennfeldt Road Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
Rich, concentrated and thick with firmly built tannins and a long potent finish.

Impenetrable inky black heart with a very deep dark red black hue. Intense ripe blackcurrant, liquorice and black cherry scents combine with vanillin cedar, tobacco, earthy dark chocolate, leather and spice notes. Rich, concentrated and thick in its flow, lavish blackcurrant, liquorice and black cherry fruits saturate the heavy weight palate. Earthy dark chocolate, vanillin cedar, leather and mint characters lurk underneath. Firmly built tannins have a burly feel imparting a sense of chewiness across the long potent finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 15.5%

Other Reviews
Super saturated purple/crimson in the glass with notes of blackberry jam, blackcurrant pastille and brandied fruits cut with hints of cedar, tobacco lead, licorice, dark chocolate, crushed rock, blackforest cake, dried herbs, purple flowers and earth. There's a lovely flow here ... elegant despite all its inherent horsepower and concentration, finishing long, strong and true with distinct western Barossa roots. Drink by 2038.
96 Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2024 Rainoldi Alpi Retiche IGT Nebbiolo
entry.summary:
Light, fresh and gently chewy with an elegant red fruited conclusion.

Semi translucent red colour with black toned edges and a light red hue. Aromas of red currant, subtle rose petal and red liquorice are intertwined with earth, dried herbs and spicy tobacco notes. Light, fresh and gently chewy, the palate is lined with red currant and red liquorice fruits which meld into earthy crushed rock like characters, dried herbs and faint spicy tobacco accents. Slightly muscular tannins and bright acidity with an elegant and savoury conclusion.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 12.5%

entry.title: Arran 14 Year Old Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary:
Matured primarily in Bourbon barrels and complemented by a proportion of Palo Cortado Sherry casks, Arran 14 makes a comeback in this newly presented edition. The bourbon casks bring vibrant notes of vanilla, orchard fruit and citrus, while the Palo Cortado casks add layers of dried fruit, toasted nuts and subtle spice. As with all Arrans, the whisky comes at a decent strength and bottled without chill filtration. 46% Alc./Vol.

Other reviews... A lovely, honest Arran though with a label color I'd prefer for the garden. Good thing it doesn't taste like lavender ;) - whiskybase.com

entry.title: 2025 Saracco Moscato d’Asti (750ml)
entry.summary:
Lusciously fruited and spritzy with a light, airy feel.

Described by Vinous Media wine critic Ian D'Agata as the 'DRC of Moscato d'Asti', this is a captivating example of Moscato.
Pours with a delicate fizzy mousse. A gentle spritz flows through the very pale coloured base. Freshly squeezed grape juice, mango, pineapple and subtle floral musk like notes fill the nostrils. Light, refreshingly sweet and frisky, the palate is decorated with flavours of grape juice, tropical fruits, mango and musk. Finishes long, fruity and effervescent.
Drink over the next 2-3 years.
Alc. 5.5%

Other Reviews
White peaches kissed with fresh mint flowing through jasmine petals and wild thyme, each aromatic layer floating like summer memories. The palate dances with perfect balance, where ripe nectarines and elegant sweetness ride waves of vibrant acidity. This is Moscato d'Asti showing its truest self, where delicate bubbles and pristine fruit linger. Pour it with spicy Vietnamese spring rolls now, save some for fresh peach tart later, this wine knows no boundaries.
95 Points
Wine Enthusiast

Theres a lot of terrible Moscato about, especially some of the gross sickly local examples, but when Moscato is good, its very much a refreshing treat.
Juicy white peach, mint, perfume. Theres a tickle of fine bubbles, acidity balances sweetness, and that tussle between those two things is the hallmark of good Moscato. Theres a feathering of grip and the finish is juicy and long. Bloody yum. This is a banger. Drink 2026-2027.
94 Points
Gary Walsh The Wine Front

entry.title: Kinglake Distillery The Wight Single Malt Australian Whisky (500ml) - Limited Release
entry.summary: A genuine limited edition with an outturn of just 165 bottles, 'The Wight' was aged for five years, starting life in a freshly emptied 30-gallon x-Bourbon cask before finishing in a Port barrel. The sweetness and warmth of the bourbon cask arrives wrapped in the richness and depth of the Port cask two very different influences coming together to make something far more indulgent than either alone. Two years was sufficient to extract just the right amount of sweetness from the American oak before a final stint in European wood. Specifically, a gorgeous French oak barrique that had previously held rich Port, re-coopered into a 100-litre cask for Kinglake by Murray River Coopers. Colour-wise, it appears to be one of the darker whiskies the distillery has released. Expect a flavour bomb! 53% Alc./Vol.
