entry.title: 2022 Catena Zapata Nicasia Vineyard Malbec
entry.summary:
Rich, concentrated and polished, this is a wonderfully finessed and powerful Malbec.

Nicola Catena planted his first Malbec vineyard in Mendoza in 1902 and today the estate is run by Nichols Catena and his daughter Laura. Malbec continues to be the estate's focus and the winery's pristine vineyards lie at the base of the Andes on soils of sand, lime and stone at altitudes between 920 and 1120 metres above sea level. Over the last 20 years, the fastidious vineyard work of Nicholas and Laura has paid dividends and Catena Zapata is now one of Argentina's most famous estates.
2022 was an exceptional year at Catena Zapata from every possible qualitative standpoint. Alejandro Vigil, Catena Zapatas Head Winemaker says: This is the best year that I have lived through.
Magnificent depth of colour featuring a super saturated inky black heart along with a dark purple black tinged hue. Perfumed aromas of violet, red to black currant, blueberry and liquorice stream through the nostrils complimented by some vanillin cedar, subtle tobacco, earth and spicy dried herb notes. Rich and concentrated yet gorgeously refined, the mid weighted palate has a deep coating of blackcurrant, blueberry, dark cherry and liquorice fruits flowing across it. Compact, grainy tannin structure with notions of vanillin cedar, earthy dark chocolate, subtle infusions of fresh herbs and delicate spicy tobacco elements outlined across the back half. Polished and fresh with a slightly dusty feel, its wonderfully finessed and powerful. Finishes long, juicy and expansive.
Drink over the next 8-10 years.
Alc. 13.5%

Other Reviews..
The 2022 Malbec Nicasia Vineyard was sourced from Paraje Altamira and aged for up to 21 months in oak barrels. Aromas of violets and lavender blend with cassis and intense blue fruit notes. Delicate yet juicy with a plush texture, it shows fine oak integration. It's precise in its fruit expression, finishing long with refined structure and a polished impression. The fresh, dry 2022 vintage lends additional nuance to this delicious wine. Compared to Catena Zapatas single-vineyard wines, Nicasia typically receives less attention, but this is a distinctive, captivating Malbec in and of itself. Drink 2025-2045.
97 points
Joaqun Hidalgo Vinous

This is concentrated, with dense dark fruit. The nose shows blue fruit, tar and tapenade. The palate is juicy and medium- to full-bodied, with delineated concentration, dark fruit flavors and voluminous presence balanced by precise tannins. Drink now.
96 points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: Red Mill Original Rum (700ml)
entry.summary:
First bottled in 1933, Red Mill Rum is now entirely new again thanks to the founders great-grandson. The brand was trademarked by George "Bunny" Fesq and originally sourced casked rums from the CSR refinery and distillery in Pyrmont. David Fesq's contemporary expressions started offsite using borrowed equipment. Considered a great success, these were barreled in the Spring of 2021. Fesq now produces rums in Sydney. Red Mill has a special approach to elevage: Alongside a traditional bourbon barrel program are more exotic casks that previously held some of the worlds great wines and spirits, including Sauternes, Cognac, various Whiskies, Madeira, Sherries, plus dry red & white wines. There are barrels ranging from 125L to 1600L in size, their contents blended into regular bottlings and rare special expressions. The distillery's primary ingredient, molasses, is sourced from the Harwood Mill in the Northern Rivers of NSW, with the rums distilled in both pot & column stills.

Red Mill's 'Original' is an ode to the history of both Red Mill and Sydney Harbour as a rum capital. Though not intended as a replica, Fesq has used the historic original as a reference point. His version has the stronger, punchier flavours of white oak cask rums, but with the refinement and elegance of all of the Red Mill spirits. The rum is batch blended from 75% ex-Bourbon and 25% ex-Scotch Whisky barrels (American oak), before resting for three months in a 1000L French oak foudre. The resulting rum remains on the savoury-dry side, so its a bit more elegant than most. The presentation is a modern interpretation of the bottles that existed in the 1960s, replete with a retro gold square label. 45% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2023 Peter Lehmann The Bond Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
Rich and sturdy with ample flesh and weight.

Dense inky black colour with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Nosing offers up aromas of blackcurrant, liquorice and mulberry which are complimented by vanillin cedar, tobacco and spicy mint notes. Rich blackcurrant, liquorice and mulberry fruits carry ample weight and flesh over a cedary tobacco, dried herb and spicy black olive back drop. A sturdy tannin structure imparts some gentle grip across the generous finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 14%

entry.title: 2023 Matias Riccitelli Malbec
entry.summary:
Founded in 2009 in Las Compuertas, Mendoza, Matas Riccitelli produces site-focused wines from high-altitude, ungrafted old vineyards across Mendoza and Patagonia. Winemaking centers on low intervention, using native yeasts, concrete eggs, and neutral oak to highlight freshness, natural texture, and vineyard character over heavy oak or over-extraction. The portfolio spans nuanced single-vineyard Malbecs alongside revived heritage varieties like Criolla Chica, Torronts, and old-vine Smillon.

Sourced from high-altitude, calcareous soils at 1,400 meters in Gualtallary, this agroecologically farmed Malbec is fermented in concrete vats using native yeasts. Gentle extraction and aging in French oak yield a focused, mineral-driven expression of the Uco Valley.

entry.title: 2024 Elanto Vineyard Basalt Lieu-Dit Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Elanto Vineyard is fast becoming one of the most compelling projects on the Mornington Peninsula. Established in 2018 by Elizabeth and Tony Todaro with Sandro Mosele at the helm, the 10.6-hectare Balnarring site is planted at an extraordinary density over 11,000 vines per hectare, four times the regional norm. Yields are kept to just 300-500g per vine, resulting in small, concentrated bunches that carry the depth and power Sandro has long championed. Volcanic red soils, southeast exposure, and the cooling influence of Western Port Bay provide the setting, while meticulous organic farming and uncompromising vineyard detail push the wines into rare territory.

The five Pinot Noir vineyards, Vertex, Ironstone, Chicory, Kilnside, and Basalt, span 6.7 hectares on the upper slopes with basalt-rich soils. The red volcanic soils transition to shallower, stonier terrain mid-slope, producing lower yields, concentrated flavors, and a distinct tannin profile. Each vineyard was harvested and vinified separately, with chilled, destemmed fruit (3-5% whole bunches) undergoing cold soak and natural fermentation in concrete vats. After 25-30 days on skins, the wine was pressed and aged in a mix of new and older French oak barriques for 11 months before blending and bottling.

Savoury and structural with a slightly meaty feel and an elegant if not a touch restrained finish.

Dark red core with black toned edges and a red to brick red tinged hue. Captivating aromas of dark cherry, violet and wild strawberry are complexed by brambly cedar, subtle clove, rhubarb, forest floor and spice notes. Supple and expansive, dark cherry, strawberry and rhubarb fruits are interwoven with bramble, earth, dried herb and spicy cedar characters. Savoury with a slightly meaty feel, it has polished yet structural tannins and ample freshness. Impressive torque with a long, elegant if not a touch restrained finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews...
Since planting Australias most ambitious high-density pinot noir vineyard in 18, Sandro Mosele has already identified unique parcels, this mid-slope and off the east side of the vineyard where basalt is closer to the surface. Such an individual imprint: incredible perfume of wild strawberries and black cherries with forest floor, Middle Eastern spices, menthol and orange zest with more savoury nuances coming through. Complex and detailed. There's a little pinch of green walnut, but mostly sweet fruit coats the mid-weighted palate, as do abundant supple tannins, before the cleansing acidity does its job. Drink 2026-2035.
97 points
Jane Faulkner - James Halliday's Wine Companion

This is the equal of the Ironstone release and the Ironstone was fantastic.
This is firm and complex but mostly its a celebration of pinot noir. Its an archetype in the best of ways. Cherries, strawberries, sweet spices, red roses and undergrowth notes come threaded with stern-but-silty tannin. Again were in masterclass territory. Theres so much perfume and life to this wine and yet for structure and length its A-Plus. Drink 2026-2031+.
96 points
Campbell Mattinson - The Wine Front

entry.title: 2025 Jasper Hill Georgia's Paddock Shiraz Magnum (1500ml)
entry.summary:
Other Reviews...
Year after year this wine delivers, and the 2025 is no exception. Theres lovely depth and concentration cut with freshness and purity, giving classic Heathcote shiraz notes of blackberry, mulberry, dried herbs, red brick, bitter chocolate and a spicy earthy undertone. The palate is firmly framed yet layered with silky tannins and class, leading to a long, decadent yet restrained finish. Excellent now but will reward with cellaring. Drink or hold.
99 points
Ryan Montgomery - JamesSuckling.com

Black fruit, dark chocolate, dried herb, aniseed, dried flowers, a distinct steely note. Its full-bodied, blackberry, a deep ferrous grip to tannin, fresh berry acidity pops through it, iron and liquorice richness, with ripe sooty tannin closing out a finish of excellent length. This is a wine of substance and impact. Its quite something. Superb. Drink 2028 - 2045+.
96 points
Gary Walsh - The Wine Front

entry.title: Williams & Humbert Don Zoilo 15 Year Old Palo Cortado en Rama Sherry
entry.summary: Notes from the producers... Wine the colour of old gold. Very sharp, intense aroma, complex with hints of dried fruits and hazelnut. Mouthfeel is dry, silky, has very balanced acidity, is full-bodied, has a very elegant character, has a persistent mouthfeel, and has tremendously expressive retronasal olfaction. Ideal for sipping slowly (meditation wine). Drink with dried fruits, mature cheeses, and at the table, consomms, stews, and gelatinous meats (oxtail, pork cheeks, etc.). 20% Alc./Vol.

Supple and juicy with medium length to the ripe, fleshy conclusion.

entry.title: 2026 Warrabilla Small Batch Fiano
entry.summary:
A thirst-quenching Fiano with good mid palate shape.

Brilliant pale straw colour with green tinged edges and a watery hue. Drifting through the nostrils are aromas of pear, red apple and subtle honeysuckle which are trailed by whiffs of guava and fresh herbs. Vibrant pear, lime, green apple and guava fruits are underscored by infusions of fresh herbs. Good mid palate shape with zingy mineral infused acidity that generates an energized feel across the thirst-quenching finish.
Drink over the next year.
Alc. 12.5%

entry.g:description:
Dry, savoury and energetic.

Made from Sangiovese. Salmon pink tinged colour. Spicy cherry, raspberry and blood orange scents are trailed by citrusy wet slate and mineral notes. Delicious cherry, raspberry and blood orange fruits are both shapely and tangy in their flow across the palate. Lively acidity with citrus and slatey mineral elements extending across the dry, savoury and energetic finish.
Drink over the next 1-2 years.
Alc. 12%

entry.title: Red Mill Spiced Rum (700ml)
entry.summary: Made by blending a base rum from ex-wine casks (Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Bordeaux, Sherry) with a smaller proportion from ex-Whiskey casks, Red Mill then top it off with a 4/1 ratio of their house Coconut Rum. The final blend undergoes a gentle maceration of tasty elements, including Cinnamon, All Spice, Pineapple, Cacao, Vanilla and Hibiscus. An exemplar of purity and restraint for the Spiced category, this take a leaf out of the distillery's 'Classic'. Supple and never too sweet, unfolding with suggestions of banana cake and dried pineapple, laced with vanilla and ginger; there's also hints of Bounty bar, a flash of muscat, with cinnamon and gingerbread warming up the lengthy finish. Carefully crafted, super-easy drinking and just plain delicious. 38% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2025 Pasqua 11 Minutes Rose
entry.summary:
A delicious, slippery textured Rose.

Made from a blend of 50% Corvina, 25% Trebbiano, 15% Syrah and 10% Carmenre. Pale damask pink tinged colour. Fragrant aromas of raspberry, white peach and musk stream out of the glass with some pomegranate and subtle wet stone notes also evident. Delicious peach, raspberry and musk flavours overlay a wet stone back drop. Slippery textured it has brisk acidity and a long supple finish.
Drink over the next 1-2 years.
Alc. 12.5%

entry.title: The Glenturret 2024 Release 10 Year Old Peat Smoked Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary:
2024 saw Glenturret near the end of its peated stocks, so if you're a fan of this style, it's essential to buy up now as the peated whiskies are discontinued as of 2026. Managing Director, Jennie Baernreuther says the decision to ditch peat was largely influenced by marketing challenges abroad. Some drinkers outside of Europe and the U.S. were confused by the distillerys peated expressions. When they like peat, they tend to go straight to Islay and they dont really know about Highland peat, she explains. Its very difficult for people to understand what it is, let alone be likely to choose Glenturrets peated [whiskies].  The decision to stop using peat also aligns with Glenturrets ongoing sustainability efforts to reduce carbon emissions. 48.4% Alc./Vol.

Other reviews... Overall, I may even prefer this whisky to the already superb 2024 release of The Glenturret 15. For my palate, peat seems to elevate the distillerys naturally earthy and wood-heavy character. I feel it gives their expressions a greater complexity and depth. - whiskybase.com

Bought this whisky because of friends suggestion of 2022 edition and I'm glad I did. Beautiful stuff. Sweet, smokey, gentle but fun. Very well crafted. - whiskybase.com

entry.title: 2025 Tiefenbrunner Merus Pinot Grigio
entry.summary:
Nicely shaped with lively acidity and a long spice laden finish.

Founded in 1848 Tiefenbrunner is considered to be a benchmark producer in the Alto-Adige region. Fermentation takes place in stainless steel tanks followed by four months ageing on lees in concrete vats.
Brilliant pale straw colour with green flecked edges and a watery hue. Citrus, pear and green apple skin aromas are trailed by some stony mineral notes. Delicious pear, red apple skin and citrus flavours carry a shapely feel across the palate with notions of subtle dried honey, quince and spice extending across the back half. Excellent concentration with lively acidity and a long spice laden finish.
Drink over the next 2-3 years.
Alc. 13.5%

entry.title: 2025 Domaine Christian Moreau Chablis Vaillon Premier Cru
entry.summary:
Domaine Christian Moreau is one of the most respected names in Chablis blessed with magnificent vineyard holdings in the best areas of Chablis. The highlights are undoubtedly the amazing range of Grand cru vineyards including one single holding of approximately 3 hectares in Les Clos as well as 0.41 hectares of Clos des Hospices dans Les Clos plus slightly smaller holdings in Valmur, Blanchots and Vaudesir. The wines are gaining in even clearer expression with the vineyards having been certified organic since 2013 and together with some new tanks and other investments the results are showing clearly in the wines with each vintage. These are wines of precision, crystal clear typicity, and elegance that will age classically while enabling tremendous enjoyment throughout their lives.

Other Reviews...
The 2025 Chablis Vaillon 1er Cru has a strict nose with touches of yellow fruit mixed with crushed stone and green apple. It gradually unfurls but keeps its foot on the brakes. The palate is well-balanced with a peachy opening. In fact, I would mistake this for a Cte de Beaune (Chassagne?) if I were served this blind. Very harmonious on the finish, this should drink well for several years. Drink 2027-2036.
90-92 points
Neal Martin - Vinous

entry.title: 2021 Domaine du Bel Air Bourgueil Grand Mont
entry.summary:
Domaine du Bel is comprised of 18 hectares of vineyards located in the village of Benais, just east of Bourgeuil. This certified organic estate is run by Pierre Guathier and his son Rodolphe, and produce deep, age-worthy single parcel wines which are incredible discoveries for Cabernet Franc devotees and Loire Valley wine lovers.

Grand Mont sits on a high chalky clay and limestone plateau, and average vine age here is around 70 years. All bunches are 100% destemmed, sorted and then after a cold maceration they are fermented by indigenous yeasts, before maturing in 600 litre third or fourth-fill barrels for up to 24 months.

Other Reviews...
The 2021 Grand Mont is savory and serious. There's richness and intensity of fruit despite a clear freshness that keeps this light on its feet. This is not a big, ripe Grand Mont like the 2018, but it has tenderness and finesse with a chalky, powdery texture on the palate. The 2021 is precise, balanced and full of sinew on the finish. Drink 2026-2040.
94 points
Rebecca Gibb MW - Vinous

entry.title: 2018 Taittinger Vintage Champagne
entry.summary:
Refined, stylish and sophisticated Champagne.

The Taittinger Vintage Brut is produced exclusively from first press wines, blended from 50% Chardonnay and 50% Pinot Noir. Grands Cru vineyards make up a significant proportion of the blend at 70%, while the other selected villages are all classified as Premiers Crus. Aged on lees for over 5 years.
Pours with a satiny mousse that slowly fades into a pale straw to pale gold coloured base which is threaded by a very fine and extremely persistent bead. Elevated pear and citrus aromas are accompanied by yeast lees, faint quince, chalk and delicate cashew notes. Refined, stylish and sophisticated, the airy palate is detailed with pear, baked bread, yeast lees and subtle oily cashew flavours. Some citrus and delicate brioche characters linger across the back half. Pillowy textural feel with crisp, chalk tinged acidity and a long, gorgeously finessed finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 12.5%

Other Reviews
A layered and lively wine with aromas of strawberries and hints of currant bush, lemons, earth, chalk and white pepper. Medium-bodied with structure and freshness. Lively and energetic. Half chardonnnay and half pinot noir. Disgorged February 2025. 9 g/L dosage. Released March 2026. Drink or hold.
94 points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: Experimental de Christian Drouin Planteray Clarendon Cask Finish 16 Year Old Calvados (700ml)
entry.summary: Continuing their exploration of rum terroirs, Drouin's Calvados Experiment #13 makes a stop in Jamaica. Finished for five months in casks that previously held high-ester Clarendon rum, it's a limited edition of 1788 bottles. The result is a brandy with notes of ripe apple, pear compote, tropical fruits, honey, toffee, and the funky, pungent molasses character typical of Clarendon. 47.5% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2024 Vanguardist Grenache
entry.summary:
Tense and sculptured with juicy red fruits.

Semi translucent red to dark red colour with black toned edges and a light red hue. Fragrant red raspberry, red liquorice and red cherry scents show excellent intensity complimented by some crushed rock, fresh herb and pepper notes. Rich and juicy yet light on its feet with sculptured tannins providing a gentle muscular feel. Succulent red raspberry and red liquorice fruits drive the palate with some crushed rock, red cherry, subtle graphite and pepper elements also chiming in. Tense and focused it finishes long, fresh and juicy.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14.1%

Other Reviews..
The Vanguardist calling card, the defining wine. Deeply savoury and intense, layered, detailed, chiselled, seriously complex. The vintage conditions were a little easier in '24 than '23, with a little more warmth, but this continues the Vanguardist upward trajectory with a theme of transparency, elegance and refined detail. Dehydrated cranberry and goji, barberry, amaro herbs and spicing, dried citrus peel, rye, caraway, pumpernickel, sun-warmed terracotta, pressed wildflowers. A sour-fruited tension to flavour and structure runs through it. Its a wine that is so captivating on the nose, so intense and layered, that it is almost enough as is. But the palate, the chewy, pithy, silty, sandy tannins, the tamarind acidity, the haunting persistence Another beautifully beguiling world-class grenache from Mr Corbett. Bravo. Drink by 2039.
97+ Points
Marcus Ellis - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

I just had winemaker Michael Corbett in the house to run through his new releases (available April 1). Hes a very passionate man, and his attention to detail in the vineyard and winemaking process is almost obsessive. I suggested he might like to taste this wine from a Conterno Sensory glass and he thought that was a very good idea (to paraphrase). This is matured in two 22HL Slavonian foudre, which are now seven years old. Two thirds whole bunch. From the Rende Vineyard in Blewitt Springs, which is now over 55 years old. This is a lighter, more frisky expression of Vanguardist Grenache, in the way of 2023, though with a bit more oomph, but less richness, tannin and stuffing than, say, 2019 and 2021. Not a comment on quality, more a guide to style.
Raspberry, cherry, almond, spice, slight liquorice richness, dried roses. Medium-bodied, spicy, cherry and raspberry, savoury and gently earthy, a fine grainy richness to tannin, a cranberry freshness to acidity, with a nutty strawberry and spice finish of excellent length. Wonderful finesse and perfume here. Give it a couple more years to come up. Drink 2027 - 2036+
96 Points
Gary Walsh The Wine Front

The 2024 Grenache is perfumed and aromatic, leading with saturated rose petals, pomegranate, raspberry and licorice, alongside cracked timut peppercorns (in the way that timut pepper leads with pink grapefruit, it is fresh, with black tea, sage, resin and is delicate, singular).
The tannins are silky and fine; they build over the course of drinking, through the middle palate, the crescendo and the finish. This is more powerful than I expected, despite what I know of the (in the end, magnificent) 2024 vintage, though the tannins are not as prominent as I expectedno bad thing. This is all about the tannins, as all great Grenache is, and it is the last impression on the palate once the wine is gone. The fruit was handpicked over three different days (10 days apart), with reduced yields from the 2023 vintage. It was made with around two-thirds whole bunches, with a long and slow fermentation over five weeks and matured for 17 months in two 2,200-liter Slavonian oak foudres (seven years old). This is a satiating, layered rendition of Vanguardist Grenache, and the highlight is the tannins. 14.1% alcohol, sealed under Diam Origine. Drink 2026-2039.
97 Points
Erin Larkin Robert Parkers The Wine Advocate

entry.title: 2024 Bass River 1835 Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Pear and tangy lemon flavours underscored by lively acidity with tertiary flavours lingering across the brisk, linear finish.

Fermented in oak puncheons (8% new), then matured on fine lees for 10 months. Bright yellow straw colour with a watery hue. Aromas of ripe peach and pear intermix with honeycomb, lemon butter, roasted almond and spice notes. Pear and tangy lemon flavours are underscored by lively acidity. Buttered almond, subtle toasty kerosene and spice characters lie underneath. Brisk, linear finish.
Drink over the next 3-4 years.
Alc. 12.5%

entry.title: 2020 Domaine Clos Rougeard Saumur-Champigny Clos
entry.summary:
Other Reviews...
The 2020 Saumur Champigny is super succulent and already welcoming despite its release date being almost a year away from tasting. What's good about this is its elegance and balance despite the warmth of the vintage, leaving you wanting more. Alongside pure fruit, smoky bacon and black tea, this is starting to show some subtle signs of savoriness and tobacco. The nature of the fine tannins is all-encompassing. While it may not be the longest wine in the world, the 2020 retains a sense of finesse and poise. Drink 2025-2036.
92 points
Rebecca Gibb MW - Vinous

entry.title: 2024 Elanto Vineyard Ironstone Lieu-Dit Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Elanto Vineyard is fast becoming one of the most compelling projects on the Mornington Peninsula. Established in 2018 by Elizabeth and Tony Todaro with Sandro Mosele at the helm, the 10.6-hectare Balnarring site is planted at an extraordinary density over 11,000 vines per hectare, four times the regional norm. Yields are kept to just 300-500g per vine, resulting in small, concentrated bunches that carry the depth and power Sandro has long championed. Volcanic red soils, southeast exposure, and the cooling influence of Western Port Bay provide the setting, while meticulous organic farming and uncompromising vineyard detail push the wines into rare territory.

The five Pinot Noir vineyards, Vertex, Ironstone, Chicory, Kilnside, and Basalt, span 6.7 hectares on the upper slopes with basalt-rich soils. The red volcanic soils transition to shallower, stonier terrain mid-slope, producing lower yields, concentrated flavors, and a distinct tannin profile. Each vineyard was harvested and vinified separately, with chilled, destemmed fruit (3-5% whole bunches) undergoing cold soak and natural fermentation in concrete vats. After 25-30 days on skins, the wine was pressed and aged in a mix of new and older French oak barriques for 11 months before blending and bottling.

Powerful, expansive and generous yet refined.

Totally opaque dark red black tinged core with a dark red hue. Pronounced dark cherry and rhubarb aromas are interwoven with dried herb, bramble forest floor and subtle spicy cedar notes. Showing more richness, density and power than the Basalt, the enveloping palate is layered with fleshy dark cherry, rhubarb and strawberry fruits. Supple mouth feel with notions of brambly cedar, forest floor, dried herbs and spice lending further complexity. Polished, velvety tannin structure finishing long, expansive and generous yet refined.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews...
Two Lieux-Dits wines released this vintage, Basalt and Ironstone; fascinating to try them side-by-side. So different. Of course, thats the point. To date, this is the lowest yielding site; its mid-slope, west side and next to Basalt. This needed a bit more coaxing so a decent decant is worth the effort, plus it has more structure and power than its sibling. Its not just word association either as this has strong ferrous aromas, pomegranate, wormwood, a touch of wintergreen and warm earth akin to freshly tilled soil. Beautiful aromatics. Intensely flavoured, the palate fuller bodied, with supple tannins and bright acidity. Incredible to consider such quality comes off young vines. Drink 2026-2038.
97 points
Jane Faulkner - James Halliday's Wine Companion

What a sensational pinot noir. Its firm, complex, effortless and forceful all at once. This isnt a pinot noir for wine children, thats for sure. Walnuts, rich black cherries, sweet spice notes, alpine herb characters, ferrous notes, smoked cedar. It suggests at fruit sweetness and then dives into earth and iron. It remains juicy to, and through, the end, but its also massaged quite exquisitely with integrated, nutty tannin. Its electric drinking, right now, but it will certain cellar. Drink 2026-2033+.
96 points
Campbell Mattinson - The Wine Front

entry.title: 2022 San Giusto a Rentennano Percarlo
entry.summary:
San Giusto a Rentennano, originally a monastery fortified in 1204 by the Florentines as their boundary with Siena, today uses the underground vaults built as part of the fortification as their cellars. For centuries it was owned by the Ricasoli family of neighbouring Brolio, passing to the Martini di Cigala family in 1957. This beautiful 160 hectare estate, with 30 of vineyards, is run by brothers and sister team of Francesco, Luca and Elisabetta. The vineyards enjoy exceptional exposure with considerable day and night temperature differences and the terrain is composed of various soils rich in minerals. San Giustos wines are renowned for their elegance, balancing rich fruit and beautiful aromatics with superb freshness.

Other Reviews...
The 2022 Percarlo is seriously impressive. I can't wait to see how it ages. Sumptuous and packed to the core, the 2022 flows with the essence of dark red fruit, spice, cedar, new leather, pomegranate and blood orange. I would not dream of touching a bottle any time soon. Hints of rose petal, cinnamon and dried herbs linger on the substantial finish. The 2022 spent 22 months in oak, mostly 30hl casks with some 500-liter tonneaux. Drink 2030-2052.
97 points
Antonio Galloni - Vinous

entry.title: Glen Scotia Campbeltown Malts Festival Limited Edition 9 Year Old Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary:
One of a series of special bottlings for the Campbeltown Malts Festival, each subject to a different maturation. This edition saw unpeated spirit finished in Fino sherry casks for a minimum of six months. The result is a vibrant and youthful whisky, brimming with notes of lemon citrus, orchard fruits and oak spice. The bottle also features a QR code with a short multimedia story ("Sound of Glen Scotia") designed to bring the atmosphere of the distillery and the festival to life. 56.2% Alc./Vol. Non-chill filtered.

Other reviews... Class act again from GS for the festival release real quality taste and texture as with other years! The improvement from disco cows era has to be recognised! Nose- sweet, honey, vanilla, subtle citrus and salinity. Hand rub malt smell is very warming. Taste- surprisingly light for 56.2%, citrus comes through more. Raisins there along with pleasant spice. No water required, not feeling any burn. GS have a great ability to demonstrate quality in both peated and unpeated spirit. Personally go for peated whisky as preference but this is a beautiful drinking whisky and Im glad I have 2 bottles! - whiskybase.com

...Youll say it was high time we gave this one a proper go, at least before the Campbeltown Malts Festival 2025! Colour: white wine. Nose: clearly in the same ballpark as the Maclean, though a little less defined and cheerful, showing more paraffin, modelling clay and leafy greenery. Could that be the fino influence? With water: bread dough, fresh sawdust, bakers yeast. Mouth (neat): same general remarks, the casks do make themselves known, but the fruitiness persists. Plenty of apples and a slight earthy, twiggy side. With water: it takes water well, bringing out liquorice and lemon zest. Very nice bitterness too (liquorice wood, ginseng). Finish: fairly long, youthful, with the sherry rounding off the whole ensemble. Comments: very pleasant indeed, just lacking the Macleans sense of clear line. 84 points - whiskyfun.com

entry.title: Puss & Mew Distillery Australian Dry Gin (700ml)
entry.summary: Made with Australian outback botanicals including Finger Lime, Peppermint Gum, Wattleseed and Cinnamon Myrtle.  Appealingly dry and herbaceous on the nose, the palate crisp and lively with a savoury edge to the sharper citrus notes; piney-juniper and lime peel more salient through the lengthy pepper-laced finish. Drier-styled gin that's tautly structured. 44% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2025 La P’tite Pierre Rose
entry.summary:
Supple and flavoursome entry level French Rose.

Pale salmon pink tinged colour. Peach, raspberry and musk aromas are trailed by some strawberry and wet stone notes. The slippery textured palate features raspberry, strawberry, pomegranate and musk flavours over a stony mineral back drop. Brisk acidity, finishing supple and flavoursome.
Drink over the next 1-2 years.
Alc. 11%

entry.title: 2024 Gapsted Estate High Country Albarino
entry.summary:
Vibrant guava, lime and green apple fruits underscored by crisp mineral laced acidity.

Brilliant pale straw colour with gleaming green tinged edges and a watery hue. Nosing reveals aromas of guava, pear and lime followed by faint honeysuckle and wet slate notes. Vibrant guava, lime and green apple fruits line the palate underscored by crisp mineral laced acidity. Dry invigorating finish with some wet slate characters lingering across it.
Drink over the next 1-2 years.
Alc. 13.5%

entry.title: 2023 Juxtaposed Wait Vineyard Old Vine Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich and plush with blueberry like freshness.

Dense midnight black colour with a dark red black tinged hue. Aromas of liquorice, blackberry, blueberry and dark plum fill the nostrils followed by spicy vanillin cedar, fennel and gentle peppered earth notes. Rich fleshy blackberry, liquorice and dark plum fruits flow across the mid weighted palate with a refined feel. Ensuing are notions of spicy vanillin cedar, earthy fennel and pepper. Showing a blueberry like freshness, it has polished tannins and a plush medium to long conclusion.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.8%

Other Reviews..
From the Sandy Corner block of Blewitt Springs Wait vineyard. Theres a charming blue fruit and floral engagement to this, so perfumed and expressive. Violet, iris, blueberry and boysenberry, black tea, iodine and iron, graphite and cigar ash. Such a nice wine, medium-ish in weight, but kind of weightless. A wine of place, intense, easy, but with import, too. Oh, and fine value. Drink by 2031.
93 Points
Marcus Ellis - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

The detail on these Juxtaposed labels are wine nerd heaven. From an unirrigated site, this Old Vine Shiraz blew my mind as it continued to get better and better over a few days of tasting. It deserves the 95 beside its name.
From the Sandy Corner Block of the Wait Vineyard, the 55 year old vines stretch their feet into the soils of the ancient Maslin Sands.
Dark plums and a basket of red and blue fruit greet you alongside a fistful of mulberries. There is a ribbon of caramel that is consistent with the Old Vine Grenache 2023 - both wines come off the Wait Vineyard. Let it breathe and it opens its arms with a welcoming embrace. A touch of minerality peers through, as do some iron filing notes. Fruit bun and Christmas cake spices keep a neat tempo with dusty and fine tannins having the last word. Sunday roasts and char grills are right in its line of sight. An excellent drink for $33.
95 Points
QwineReviews.com

entry.title: 2021 Peter Lehmann Mentor Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
Rich, succulent and fleshy textured with a sense of refinement carried through the finish.

Dense pitch black heart with a dark red black tinged hue. Dark plum, liquorice and blackcurrant aromas stream through the nostrils with ample intensity intermingling with some spicy vanillin cedar, tobacco, earth and bay leaf notes along the way. Rich, succulent dark plum and blackcurrant fruits carry a fleshy texture with notions of liquorice, vanillin cedar, subtle tobacco and mint extending across the back half. Fine grained tannins have an underlyingly sturdy feel. The long, deeply fruited finish carrying a sense of refinement.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14%

Other Reviews..
Deep crimson with aromas of blackberry, black cherry and blackberry pastille fruit tones alongside hints of fine spice, tobacco, cedar, dried herbs, licorice, choc-mint, espresso and earth. Full bodied and flush with ripe black fruits, tensing with ample fine-grained tannin before releasing with opulent black fruits and a nice energetic line as it slowly fades. Drink by 2040.
95 Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

Old PL, as he was known to all and sundry, was a mentor to so many Barossa winemakers. He was simply one of the great men of the Barossa. This is a wine demonstrating that the region is not all about Shiraz. In good years you get a wine like this balanced, poised and powerful, with style. Loads of blackcurrant and dark chocolate with a thread of steely oyster shell adding to the tannin profile. Love it. Drink 2024-2039.
96 Points
Ray Jordan WinePilot.com

entry.title: 2023 Jim Barry The Armagh Shiraz
entry.summary:
2027 Best Shiraz of the Year - James Halliday's Australian Wine Companion Awards

Other Reviews...
2027 Shiraz of the Year. Score awarded by the Halliday tasting panel at the annual Awards judging. MB writes: The '23 harvest has produced perhaps one of the most restrained and fine Armagh releases of all. This is a sublime wine of control, levity and sense of freshness, but it doesn't miss the trick of concentration. There are ripples of dark forest berries, dark chocolate and cola, with new leather, graphite minerality, green olive herbal lift and a lick of spicy oak seasoning like a cherry on top. Tannins are silky, the wine beautifully and evocatively perfumed. The quieter voice and elegance here is beautiful. A striking wine. Drink 2025-2040.
99 points
James Halliday's Australian Wine Companion

Dark fruited with blackberry, blackcurrant, licorice, dark chocolate, spice, cedar, earth, crushed blueberries and violets, showing the depth and complexity that comes from old vines planted in 1968. The palate is seamlessly integrated with melting tannins, bright acidity and a long, lush finish where fresh fruit, earthy nuance and spice come together with a touch of freshness from the cooler vintage. Another knockout bottling from this exceptional Clare Valley vineyard. Drink or hold. Screw cap.
98 points
Ryan Montgomery - JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2023 Elderton Command Single Vineyard Shiraz
entry.summary:
Gorgeously rich, seductive and plush yet refined and stylish.

Since the inaugural 1984 vintage Elderton Command Shiraz has established a formidable international reputation. Planted in 1894 the Command vineyard is located on the southern edge of the Nuriootpa township and planted on deep alluvial silt over red and brown earth and limestone. The majority of the rows are orientated east-west (as opposed to the more common orientation of north-south). This enables cooling breezes from the Barossa Ranges to flow through the rows of vines rather than against them. Maturation takes place in a combination of new French and American oak puncheons for 24 months, the wine is then given a further 12 months bottle age before being released.
Dense pitch black dark red colour with a dark red hue. Wafting from the glass are decadent scents of dark plum, liquorice, vanillin oak and mocha trailed by some scorched earth, fennel and pepper notes. Gorgeously rich, seductive and plush, the opulent palate is engulfed with dark plum, liquorice, vanillin oak and fennel flavours. Scorched earth, spice, mocha and pepper elements trail off into the distance. Velvet smooth yet structured tannin framework with a slightly more finessed feel to the long, sumptuous finish. A more refined, stylish expression of Command.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14.9%

The 2023 Command Single Vineyard Shiraz is from a cool, wet vintage, as the note below will attest, not dissimilar to the 2017 vintage. Here, the fruit is sweet and nuanced, with licorice, cocoa and pomegranate. Having tasted these wines today going back to 1985, it is abundantly clear that these wines look so good with some bottle age. While their youth is attractive, nothing beats the complexity gained in time. It's over to you to decide when you choose to drink your wine, but I personally would like to see this wine with around seven years from harvest. 14.9% alcohol, sealed under screw cap. Drink 2026-2053.
96 Points
Erin Larkin Robert Parkers The Wine Advocate

One of the most iconic Shiraz from the Barossa Valley, the first vintage was 1984. The release of this wine is always eagerly awaited. From a Nuriootpa Vineyard, the vines are now 132 years of age. Maturation was in a mix of new French and American oak puncheons for twenty-three months. Opaque maroon with a dark crimson rim, it offers a most evocative nose. Seriously impressive oak integration, we have aromas of chocolate, blackberries, mocha, cocoa powder, bay leaves, vanilla, coffee beans, charcuterie, cloves and a flick of gum leaf. Exhibiting a supple and seductive texture through to satiny tannins, this is beautifully balanced with great length. A wonderful Barossa Shiraz for enjoying over the next twenty to twenty-five years. At the moment, I have it scored at the same level as the stunning 2022 vintage of this wine, however, if pushed I would probably go for the older wine by a whisker. Whether that remains so over time, we look forward to finding out. Drink 2026-2051.

entry.g:title: 2023 Elderton Command Single Vineyard Shiraz
entry.g:description:
Gorgeously rich, seductive and plush yet refined and stylish.

Since the inaugural 1984 vintage Elderton Command Shiraz has established a formidable international reputation. Planted in 1894 the Command vineyard is located on the southern edge of the Nuriootpa township and planted on deep alluvial silt over red and brown earth and limestone. The majority of the rows are orientated east-west (as opposed to the more common orientation of north-south). This enables cooling breezes from the Barossa Ranges to flow through the rows of vines rather than against them. Maturation takes place in a combination of new French and American oak puncheons for 24 months, the wine is then given a further 12 months bottle age before being released.

entry.title: 2021 Principe Corsini Don Tommaso Chianti Classico Gran Selezione
entry.summary:
Tense and structured with energetic red fruits.

Certified organic. Deep dark red black core with a dark red hue. Elevated scents of red to black currant, rose petals and red to dark cherries are interwoven with spicy cedar, earthy tobacco, dried herb and leather notes. Medium bodied, generous red to black currant and red cherry fruits are framed by chalky tannins. Notions of red liquorice, earth, tobacco, cedar and spicy dried herbs form across the back half. Good tension and grip with vibrant acidity lending an energetic feel to the long, refined yet slightly rustic finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews..
A restrained wine with vanilla, plums, cherries and a balsamic note. Full-bodied with velvety tannins and flavors of graphite and fruit. Its very nuanced, supple and savory on the chalky finish. Sangiovese with 20% merlot. Drinkable now, but best from 2026.
94 Points
JamesSuckling.com

entry.title: 2026 Clonakilla Viognier Nouveau
entry.summary:
Vibrant and fresh yet gorgeously textured.

Brilliant water like core with green highlighted edges. Fragrant peach and fresh apricot scents sail out of the glass followed by whiffs of honeysuckle, musk and delicate ginger spice. Displaying excellent intensity and textural shape, the mouth is filled with delicious peach, pear and apricot fruits which are supported by subtle honeysuckle, musk and ginger spice elements. Supple in its flow, it has lively acidity and a long vibrantly refreshing yet gorgeously rounded finish.
Drink over the next 2-3 years.
Alc. 12.5%

Other Reviews..
This wine has stepped up in recent years and this is another very good release. It tastes of fennel, apricot kernels, tonic water, brine and aromatic citrus, the latter stepping into blossom-like territory. Theres also a smidgen of mandarin. Its effusive and its delicious, though its just a bit serious too. I like it very much. Drink 2026-2030.
93 Points
Campbell Mattinson The Wine Front

entry.title: 2023 Figli Luigi Oddero Langhe Nebbiolo
entry.summary:
Juicy red fruits backed by chiselled tannins and energetic acidity which impart a muscular feel.

This is 100% La Morra fruit from estate vineyards in the Santa Maria Cru, just in front of the winery. Organically grown mid-hillside at around 250300 metres in typical marl and sandy soils. 2023 was a tough vintage for winemakers, with yields down significantly. Grapes were hand harvested with strict selection. Crushed and destemmed, fermented with native yeasts. Ageing in steel and large-format oak.
Red to dark red colour with black shaded edges and a rusty red tinged hue. Fragrant scents of rose petals, red currant and red cherry intermingle with dusty earth, tobacco and spicy dried herbs. Juicy red cherry, red liquorice and red currant fruits are backed by chiselled tannins and energetic acidity which impart a muscular feel. Dusty earth, tobacco, dried herb and spice elements linger across the back half. Nervy and tense it has a bright, rustic red fruited finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14.5%

entry.title: 2025 Paralian Lacey Vineyard Fiano
entry.summary:
Zingy and mouth filling with a long scrumptious finish.

Brilliant pale straw colour with subtle flashes of green around the edges and a watery hue. Aromas of lime juice and green apple skin mix with fresh garden herb, wet slate and saline like notes. Intense lime, Granny Smith apple and green pear fruits engulf the palate with a mouth filling like effect. Zingy acidity with infusions of Mediterranean herbs and slatey mineral elements the undercard. Excellent textural volume and drive with a long scrumptious finish.
Drink over the next 1-2 years.
Alc. 12.5%

Other Reviews..
From the Lacey familys Tatachilla vineyard; mainly in steel, with a small parcel in an old barrel. Vintage '25 was warm thats been well reported and while that means a bit more fruit intensity for fiano, the best examples, such as this, show no lack of vibrancy. Crisp golden apple, Meyer lemon, pomelo, Tahitian lime on a very fragrant, though far from simple, nose. There are subtle hints of spice and a flintiness, and the palate flows with gentle texture, temperate pithiness and resolved yet tangy acidity. Very good indeed. Drink by 2029.
95 Points
Marcus Ellis - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2016 Stella di Campalto Brunello di Montalcino Rosa Amore
entry.summary:
Located outside Castelnuovo dellAbate in the southeastern corner of Montalcino, Podere San Giuseppe was an abandoned historic estate until Stella di Campalto took the helm in 1992 and transformed it into a pioneering beacon of biodynamic viticulture. Certified organic in 1996 and biodynamic in 2005, the property features a mosaic of distinct vineyard plots set across varied soilsincluding quartz, limestone, sand, and volcanic earth. Winemaking follows a strict minimal-intervention philosophy: each vineyard parcel is harvested and fermented separately with native yeasts, moved entirely by gravity in multi-level underground cellars, and aged with zero additive manipulations or vintage blending. Prized for their delicate, highly aromatic elegance rather than heavy extraction, Stellas 100% Sangiovese wines are held back and released only when she feels they have reached optimal harmony, establishing her estate as a true benchmark of artisanal Montalcino winemaking.

Named for its signature floral bouquet and its distinction as the crown jewel of an exceptional vintage, 'Rosa Amore' underwent nearly a decade of patient cellar aging, including 43 months in oak and 64 months in bottle, before Stella deemed it ready for release. The result is a 100% Sangiovese of remarkable poise, seamlessly balancing delicate rose-like perfume with striking structural depth and vitality.

entry.title: Red Mill Classic Gold Rum (700ml)
entry.summary: Red Mill's 'Classic' is matured in approximately 50% ex-whiskey casks (Bourbon, Scotch and mixed Quarter Casks) and 50% ex-wine casks (Australian Pinot Noir and Red Bordeaux), then settled in a custom 1000L Foudre cask for six weeks before bottling. The light body suggests a column still component is at the fore, the profile crisp and fresh with light cola and low-key fruitiness, finished by a touch of dry molasses cake, sprinklings of allspice and gingery warmth. Never quite sweet, despite its lightness, there's a sense of elegance and nuance that keeps you coming back. Better than a simple mixer, this welcome departure from mainstream sweetened rums could even work as a stand-in for a summer-time single malt. 40% Alc./Vol. No added sugar.

entry.title: 2024 Feudo Montoni Catarratto Masso
entry.summary:
A snappy dry white with a mineral infused finish.

Feudo Montoni enjoys a long history in the Valledolmo region of central western Sicily. Their cellars are housed in the baglio (typical Sicilian court square building) built by the noble Arogenese family in 1469. The property was purchased by current owner and winemaker Fabio Sirecis grandfather Rosario in the late 1800s.
This Catarratto comes from the Masso cru, which is one of the highest vineyards on the Feudo Montoni Estate at 700m and named because of its rocky-sandy soil. The vines are aged between 55 and 60 years old but have been grafted onto very old bush vines producing fruit thats dense and full flavoured. This iron rich soil contributes to a wine that is intensely fresh and mineral. After concrete fermentation, the wine is kept on lees for 6 months with some batonnage before being bottled. Brilliant pale straw to straw colour with green flecked edges and a watery hue. Elevated aromas of lime, guava, pear and green apple mix with fresh Mediterranean herb and wet slate notes. Spicy pear, guava and lime fruits overlay a slatey mineral and fresh herb infused back drop. Finishes dry with brisk acidity and a saline mineral like laced aftertaste.
Drink over the next 2-3 years.
Alc. 13%

entry.title: Willett Family Estate 124 Proof 13 Year Old Single Barrel No. 3718 Straight Bourbon Whiskey (750ml)
entry.summary:
Note: Product has come from a private collection and as such may have some minor scuffing/scratches/handling marks. Actual product pictured.

Established in 1935 and still a private family-owned and operated company, Willett Distillery (aka Kentucky Bourbon Distillers or KBD) have historically been rather like an American version of a Scottish-style independent bottler. They purchased barrels of young whiskey and aged them in their hill-top warehouses south of Bardstown. Older expressions have become blue chip investments with a 24 year old Willett selling for upwards of 10K. Single barrel 3718 is now very rare. 62% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2024 Oakridge 864 Block 1 Hazeldene Vineyard Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Light and vibrant yet intense and powerful finishing long, elegant and tense.

Matured for 10 months in French oak (10% new) with 25% whole bunch inclusion. Semi translucent bright red colour with black toned edges and a light crimson red tinged hue. Wonderfully complex and alluring, the nose offers up aromas of violet, red cherry, strawberry and red liquorice infused with clove followed by forest floor, brambly cedar, rhubarb and spice notes. Light and vibrant yet intense and powerful, the palate is detailed with delicious red cherry, red liquorice and winter strawberry fruits. Infusions of clove, forest floor, bramble and spicy cedar lend further nuance. Finely built tannin structure with energetic acidity. The long, elegant finish showing excellent tension.
Drink over the next 8-10 years.
Alc. 13.5%

Other Reviews
This vineyard is planted to the MV6 clone. 3/4s of the berries are destemmed into an open fermenter on top of the remaining quarter, which is whole bunches. Pressed into French oak barrels, 10% new, the wine spent ten months maturing before a further six months in tank on lees. The colour here is a very pale crimson. entry.title: 2023 Sons of Eden Remus Old Vine Shiraz
entry.summary:
A rich, sumptuous Eden Valley Shiraz that boasts superb power and a long sleek yet savoury finish.

Sourced from three different vineyards in the Eden Valley region with vines 80 plus years old. Included in the fermentation process were up to 15% whole bunch clusters with maturation taking place in French oak hogsheads (60% new) for a period of 18 months.
Dense inky black colour with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Potent spicy dark plum, liquorice and dark to black cherry scents are interwoven with fennel, smoky vanillin cedar, earth and peppered meat notes. Rich, sumptuous and plush the palate is draped with plum, liquorice and dark cherry fruits which meld into a smoky vanillin cedar, fennel and peppered earth back drop. Boasting superb power it has velvet smooth tannins and a long sleek yet savoury finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 14.5%

entry.title: 2023 Yalumba Sanctum Coonawarra Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
An elegant red fruited Cabernet of medium length.

Deep dark red black shaded colour with a dark red hue. Fragrant red currant and mulberry scents are complimented by cedary tobacco, earth and subtle bay leaf notes. Mid weighted the palate has an elegant flavour profile of red currant and mulberry fruits over a cedary tobacco, dusty earth and spicy tomato leaf infused back drop. Fine grained tannins with a finessed, red fruited finish of medium length.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13%

Other Reviews..
Hails from the Menzies Estate vineyard, smack bang in the middle of Coonawarra on those famous terra rossa over limestone soils. The aromas provide a slightly interesting departure from the fairly typical blackcurrant, which is still there but augmented with a subtle blueberry note. Typically elegant and poised, which is what youd expect from Coonawarra, but there is a deceptive structural integrity here that gives it purpose and definition to carry through to a sustained long finish. It will continue to improve with further cellaring. Drink 2026-2036.
94 Points
Ray Jordan WinePilot.com

entry.title: 2023 Domaine de Trevallon Alpilles Rouge
entry.summary:
Formed in the early 1970's, with the first vintage 1976, Domaine de Trevallon have become one of the most famous and respected properties in Southern France. After graduating his architecture degree, Eloi Durrbach set south aiming to make natural wines with a sense of place and ability to age with ease. Planting now comprises 15 hectares of red grapes, equal parts of Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah, plus 2 hectares of Marsanne and Roussanne. All grapes have been grown and treated organically since their planting.

Alpilles Rouge is a blend of 50% Cabernet Sauvignon and 50% Syrah, aged for 24 months in old foudre and barrels with a minimum amount of racking during this time. The grapes are not destemmed, and vinification occurs with natural yeasts and no sulphur. While this wine is generally opulent and indulgent in its youth, it famously rewards time in the cellar, beautifully evolving slowly over decades.

entry.title: Risky Business Prosecco - DAMAGED LABEL
entry.summary:
A buoyant fluffy white mousse subsides to reveal a pale straw coloured base that has a steady stream of bubbles coursing through it. Distinct pear and ripe apple scents jump out of the glass with some quince and sherbet like notes also evident. Risky Business has been sourcing prosecco from the King Valley for nearly 10 years. There's an enviable consistency to style. It's seen here from the bright, just-cut green apple and citrus summery scents through to the utterly delicious lemon sorbet crunch and bubbly zing on the palate. And dry ... prosecco looks so good when it's dry and clean-cut.
95 points

entry.title: Whipper Snapper Upshot Single Malt Australian Whiskey (700ml)
entry.summary: Other reviews... Whipper Snappers single malt whisky is far less oak-forward than its other expressions, because its been matured for a minimum of four years in refill barrels rather than virgin oak. The cool part here is that, while the lions share of single malt whisky produced globally is matured in ex-bourbon casks from the US, this one is matured in Whipper Snappers own ex-whisky casks. After all, it makes its own bourbon-style whiskies, so why bother getting its casks from anywhere else? The result is a whisky with lovely floral and citrus notes on the nose, light and pretty but still with plenty of nutty grain and oak to give it power. As with much of Whipper Snappers spirits, the careful distillation and cask selection is evident in the cleanliness and integration on display. A nicely textured palate and light finish make this an easy-drinking and approachable Australian single malt whisky. 92 points - Fred Siggins, winecompanion.com.au

entry.title: Grand Marnier Triple Sec Liqueur (3000ml) - DAMAGED LABEL AND WAX
entry.summary:
Note: As pictured. The cork seal is intact. Only the wax top and front label are damaged.

A special large format of the world famous liqueur. Very limited stocks.

Made with oranges and Cognac, Grand Marnier is a liqueur immortal and one of the world's best known curacaos. Aged in the cellars of Chateau de Bourg in Cognac and blended with fruit from the French West Indies, the company's entry level bottling has become a bar standard, combining the tantalizing fragrance of Seville oranges with the warm, intoxicating rush of extra-aged cognac in a 49/51 blend. Offering superb purity and definition with notes of mixed peel, orange cake and vanilla and a concentrate of citrus peel and mandarin flavours, what's also admirable about this timeless liqueur is its expert balance; the lively spirit backbone and the finish that winds up fresh, mildly tart and vibrant with lingering honeyed-citrus flavours.

If you want an even more indulgent experience, three super premium releases set the bar higher, introducing increasing proportions of (primarily) Grande Champagne Cognacs, sometimes boasting incredible age, adding further depth and complexity to an already remarkable liqueur. Whichever you choose, these expressions are best appreciated neat, on the rocks or in a snifter glass at room temperature. 40% Alc./Vol.

Other reviews... The aroma is a sweet/sour, tangerine/Mandarin orange perfume that never stops enchanting. At the palate entry the orange zests acidity mingles gracefully with the Cognacs alcohol, making for delicious drinking. Satiny finish. 90-95 - wineenthusiast.com

Seasoned Casanovas also recommend Grand Marnier for a Royal Romance:

In shaker; one-fourth each of Passionfruit juice and Grand Marnier, half gin, shake well and serve.
Or try the popular B52:

1/3 Grand Marnier
1/3 Coffee liqueur
1/3 Irish cream liqueur
Pour delicately on a bar spoon the coffee liqueur, the Irish Cream then the GRAND MARNIER liqueur into a shooter glass. Serve without mixing.

The Charleston
1 shot of Cherry Brandy Liqueur (e.g. Cherry Heering)
1 shot of Grand Marnier
top up with lemonade and ice
Method: Pour the cherry brandy and the orange liqueur into a highball. Stir well, then fill a highball glass with ice cubes and pour the cocktail directly over them . There is no need to use a strainer in this instance. Top up with the chilled lemonade to taste, then serve.

entry.title: Willett Family Estate 92.7 Proof 20 Year Old Single Barrel No. 1904 Straight Bourbon Whiskey (750ml)
entry.summary:
Note: Product has come from a private collection and as such may have some minor scuffing/scratches/handling marks. Actual product pictured.

Established in 1935 and still a private family-owned and operated company, Willett Distillery (aka Kentucky Bourbon Distillers or KBD) have historically been rather like an American version of a Scottish-style independent bottler. They purchased barrels of young whiskey and aged them in their hill-top warehouses south of Bardstown. Older expressions have become blue chip investments with a 24 year old Willett selling for upwards of 10K. Single barrel 1904 is now very rare. 46.35% Alc./Vol.

entry.title: 2021 West Cape Howe Book Ends Cabernet Sauvignon
entry.summary:
A rich, medium to full bodied Cabernet with robust tannins imparting a grippy feel across the finish.

Dense inky black heart with a deep dark red black hue. Pronounced spicy blackcurrant aromas infused with black olive intermingle with vanillin cedar, tobacco and bay leaf notes. Rich blackcurrant, liquorice and black cherry fruits show excellent concentration across the medium to full bodied palate. Cigar box, earth, black olive and spice elements underpin the fruit. Robust tannins impart a grippy feel across the medium to long finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 14.5%

Other Reviews
An excellent wine from the 2021 vintage, which in Mount Barker delivered beautiful cool climate fruit with richness, concentration and supreme balance. Classic varietal characters of blackcurrant and dark plum with a touch of black cherry open on the nose, followed by a supple palate with a structural core contributing to its long finish. It's the most stylish expression of Mount Barker cabernet.
94 Points

entry.title: 2024 Nicole Oatley Wines NOW Chenin Blanc
entry.summary:
A fleshy textured Chenin Blanc that shows impressive intensity.

Brilliant water like core with green highlighted surrounds. Aromas of green apple, lime and pear mix with some quince and flinty mineral notes. Fleshy textured pear, Jonathan apple and quince fruits are delivered with impressive intensity. Subtle musk and spice elements sit in the background. Fresh acidity with a long nicely shaped finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 13%

Other Reviews..
This new face in WA wine was one of my finds of the previous year, and once again it has come up trumps, displaying the remarkable qualities of chenin blanc to emerge triumphant even in challenging and very hot seasons. It is a testament to both vineyard management and winemaking. In this case, it leans more into stone fruit and citrus rather than the tropical notes you might normally expect with chenin. It has a beautiful texture, fine acidity, excellent length, and is yet another illustration of how good chenin blanc can be in the Swan Valley.
94 Points
RayJordanWine.com.au

entry.title: 2023 Mount Langi Ghiran Cliff Edge Shiraz
entry.summary:
A refined Grampians Shiraz with a plush mouth feel and finessed, pepper laced finish.

Midnight black in colour with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Pronounced aromas of blackberry, liquorice and dark plum are complimented by whiffs of clove, smoked meats and peppered earth. Refined and mid weighted, the palate is generously layered with blackberry, plum and red liquorice fruits. Some blueberry, faint clove, subtle smoked meat and peppered earth elements extend across the back half. Plush mouth feel with seamlessly integrated tannins lending polish across the finessed, pepper laced finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 13.5%

Other Reviews
Whole-berry ferments in open top fermenters; seven to 10 days on skins, matured 14 months in French barriques (25% new). Totally accessible young Grampians shiraz with classic fragrant dark berries to the fore, matched evenly, aromatically with lifted minty-aniseed-peppery spice. It is both generous and bright in personality. The palate is delivered finely textured with fruit and spice running long. Drink by 2032.
93 Points
Jeni Port - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

This comes from quite old vines on the granite soils of the Grampians. Its a bright, tremendously lively, fragrant, and thoroughly appealing medium-bodied red. Theres an essence of purity, freshness and vibrancy from the first sniff through to the final combination of medium-weight sweet fruit, spices, licorice, and fine chalky tannin that pushes it through to a sustained finish. Drink 2025-2037.
94 Points
Ray Jordan WinePilot.com

entry.title: 2024 Domaine Collotte Bourgogne Pinot Noir Cuvee de Noble Souche
entry.summary:
Light and fresh with an elegant red fruited finish.

Fruit is sourced mostly from vines planted in 1947 in Champ Forey (80%) to the east of the village with the other 20% coming from vines in Chambolle Musigny. The fruit is hand-picked and 100% de-stemmed and fermented in stainless steel with no pigeage to produce a fresh, vibrant style.
Semi translucent vibrant red colour with black toned edges and a crimson red tinged hue. Fragrant red cherry, winter strawberry and cranberry scents mix with whiffs of fresh herbs, earth and spice. Light and fresh, juicy red cherry and strawberry fruits overlay a rhubarb, dried herb, earth and spice back drop. Vibrant acidity and slightly chalky tannins with an elegant and energetic finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 13%

entry.title: 2023 Torbreck Les Amis Grenache
entry.summary:
A rich, opulent Grenache with liqueur like concentration and power.

Matured for 18 months French barrique (40% new). Very deep black dark red colour with a dark red hue. Heady scents of black raspberry, liquorice, black plum and black cherry waft through the olfactory senses. Also chiming in are earthy incense like notes, vanillin spice and peppered dried herbs. Rich and liqueur like in its concentration and power, the palate is saturated in a tidal wave of black raspberry, liquorice and black plum fruits. Vanillin spice, black cherry, scorched earth and subtle peppered dried herb elements form the back drop. Opulently textured it has ripe, slightly chewy tannins and a long, heat shaded finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 15.5%

Other Reviews..
Made from 1960s-planted Grenache, this is a serious, super-concentration wine with more than a touch of Gandalfs pipe on the nose! Only 100 cases were made, and it is the darkest and most cosmic wine I have tasted under this label. This is a fabulous, single-site, dry-grown vineyard with super-low yields. There is a deeply foresty wine with incredible DNA, and the palate is bloody, ferrous, complex and herbal. There is a deep, dark chocolate and cherry-red ganache rebound of flavour on the finish, making this sylvan creation decadent, too.
19+/20
Matthew Jukes

The 2023 Les Amis Grenache is the highest in elevation of the three single-vineyard Grenache vineyards. It is planted on bluestone and ironstone gravels in clay soils, and the vines were planted recentlysome time in the 1980s. The vineyard is exposed and the soils shallow, so the vines work hard here. In the mouth, this is spicy and medium-bodied, with an attractive freshness that has nothing to do with the ripeness nor, upon questioning, the pH or total acidity, as the numbers relate pretty similarly to the other Grenache wines on the bench. The cooler, wetter season may play a part. In short, this is a lovely wine! 15.5% alcohol, sealed under natural cork. Drink 2026-2038.
94 Points
Erin Larkin Robert Parkers The Wine Advocate

entry.title: 1967 The Last Drop Glen Garioch 47 Year Old Single Malt Scotch Whisky (700ml) - Plus 50ml bottle
entry.summary:
Note: Product comes from a private collection and as such has some minor scuffing/scratches/handling marks. Actual product pictured.

The Last Drop was founded by three industry veterans who set out to track down extraordinary old stocks in forgotten cellars in order to bring whiskies of both great age and exceptional quality to the market. What can only be described as an obsession, they've committed a significant amount of time and energy scouring Scotland for buried treasure.

This bottling represents The Last Drop's first-ever single malt. And they managed to pick a very old distillery with a detailed history of producing high-quality malt: Glen Garioch. From a time when they were making a sizable ratio of peated whisky, they were also floor malting, a practise mostly out of fashion. Another unusual trait was that this whisky spent 47 years in a reportedly bourbon-style remade hogshead cask., which was unusual for the time. The results seem to speak for themselves, with many reviewers describing a thick, oily mouthfeel with tannic but fresh, sweet fruit and an iodine-laden smoky overlay. The word complex is used with abandon. No real surprise considering how long and well this whisky has been sitting. Exceptionally rare. 45.4% Alc./Vol.

Tasting notes from one of the Last Drop trio, Andrew Rankin... This magnificent malt has matured with elegance. Heady notes of cognac-soaked fruitcake, marzipan and icing are balanced with ripe apricot and a hit of peaty smokiness, softening to a delicious vanilla and honey nectar.

entry.title: 2025 Williams Crossing By Curly Flat Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
A light, savoury Pinot with an elegant finish.

Dark red in colour with black tinged edges and a light red hue. Spicy red to dark cherry and strawberry aromas are trailed by hints of rhubarb, dried herbs and forest floor. Light and savoury, red to dark cherry, winter strawberry and rhubarb fruits are featured over some forest floor, dried herb and spicy cedar characters. Fine grained tannins with an elegant finish.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13%

Other Reviews
Youre getting a fair bang for your buck with this Macedon Pinot Noir. Shows a compelling mix of red fruits with a subtle truffle-oil nuance and a damp earthen-floor infusion. Medium-bodied but finely structured, with chalky tannins, lightly applied oak, and plenty of fruit generosity. Drinking beautifully now, though a little more time in the cellar will allow the fruit characters to develop even more. Drink 2025-2032.
93 Points
Ray Jordan WinePilot.com

Im not sure Ive tried a Williams Crossing Pinot Noir before. This is raised in oak thats all older then three years of age.
Its a savoury style of Pinot Noir with dark cherry, redcurrant, pastrami and dried twigs, only medium-bodied, with good density of flavour, cool balanced acidity, a tight sort of graphite and dusty feel to tannin, gentle sappiness, and fine length. It has complexity and it drinks well. Nice.
Drink 2026-2030+
92 Points
Gary Walsh The Wine Front

entry.title: 2025 Williams Crossing by Curly Flat Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Fleshy nectarine, peach, Jonathan apple and quince fruits with a slatey gun flint like back drop.

Brilliant pale straw colour with green tinged edges and a watery hue. Aromas of nectarine and peach skin mix with some quince and gun flint like notes. Fleshy nectarine, peach, Jonathan apple and quince fruits meld their way into a slatey gun flint like back drop. Fresh acidity with a generously fruited mid length conclusion.
Drink over the next 3-4 years.
Alc. 12.5%

Other Reviews
It opens with secondary aromas, those derived from winemaking, in this case from lees contact and oak maturation. Think of cinnamon and vanilla curd. These are followed by spicy nashi pear, peaches, preserved peach, pineapple, Granny Smith apple. Although the secondary characters initially take centre stage, they soon integrate with the fruit profile. The palate is textural yet crisp and vibrant, very much a medium-bodied style at 12.5% alcohol. The acidity is both inviting and essential, preventing the secondary characters from overwhelming the palate. Fortunately, that never happens. It ends with a discreet fruit profile alongside plenty of creaminess. Overall, this is an excellent everyday Chardonnay that ticks all the boxes.
94 Points
Lisa Cardelli WinePilot.com

entry.g:title: 2024 Red Feet Sangiovese Shiraz

entry.title: Black Maple Hill Single Barrel #2 21 Year Old Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey (750ml)
entry.summary:
Note: Product has come from a private collection and as such has some minor scuffing/scratches/handling marks. There's also some cellar bloom on the labels, however overall the condition is good. Actual product pictured.

Black Maple Hill is not a distillery, but rather an independent label first introduced in 2000 by a Californian wine and spirits distributor called CVI Brands. Importantly, this is said to be one of the original early era bottlings, as opposed to the newly re-marketed Black Maple Hill bottlings now supplied by a small craft-distillery in Oregon called 'Stein' and packaged in different shaped bottles.

The legend and hype behind Black Maple Hill stems from a belief that early releases were wheated bourbon from Stizel-Weller and bottled by Julian Van Winkle III himself. Later, bottlings were said to have been moved to Kentucky Bourbon Distillers (KBD aka Willett) and made using whiskeys sourced from Heaven Hill. Whatever the truth may be, "...the magical touch of the Van Winkle finger conferred an irresistible desirability, and Black Maple Hill bottlings began to sell for thousands of dollars on the secondary market."

It's not known precisely which whiskey(s) made it into this bottle. The contents are open to speculation, especially the later iterations which are equivalent to an independent whiskey purchased from another independent whiskey supplier. What is certain is that this is one uber rare and collectable Bourbon.

Whiskyauctioneer.com offer some further insight as to the history of these bottlings:
"The Kulsveens [KBD] oversaw a golden period for the brand, with well-aged bourbons filled into a number of now hugely collectable Black Maple Hill releases. Although KBD had acquired some Stitzel-Weller stock, the majority of their casks came from the neighbouring Heaven Hill distillery in Bardstown, a distillery sadly lost in a fire in 1996 and increasingly desirable ever since... By the late 2000s, a global Bourbon boom had catapulted Black Maple Hill into the spotlight. The irresistible prospect of old-aged liquid capsules of Stitzel-Weller and Heaven Hill swept the Bourbon community, and Black Maple Hill bottlings quickly became an absolute must-have. They developed a cult-following of fans fuelled by curiosity and connoisseurship. Black Maple Hill bottlings were increasingly becoming harder to find and soon were appearing on the secondary market for values far in excess of their original retail price tag. Sadly they were not the only benefactors, and KBDs own Willett Family Estate brand had surfed the same wave, and the company increasingly reserved its stock for this, limiting what they could make available to CVI Brands and their other contracts. Black Maple Hill was eventually reduced to a non-age statement product, before disappearing from shelves. As they struggled to find an alternative it appeared as though Black Maple Hill was at the end of their story."

entry.title: 2025 Holm Oak Chardonnay
entry.summary:
Rich and creamy textured with mid weight and a long, well rounded finish.

Barrel fermented with 20% new oak. Brilliant pale straw colour with green highlighted edges and a watery hue. Elevated white peach, pear and dried honey scents are trailed by some citrusy nougat, subtle crme brulee and spice notes. Rich, creamy textured flavours of peach, pear and dried honey unfold across the mid weighted palate. Notions of crme brulee, nougat and spice also chime in. Finishes long, fleshy and well rounded.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 13%

Other Reviews..
Light straw with characters of lemon, peach and nectarine, hints of meadow flowers, crme frache, citrus zest, shortbread, spiced oatmeal, sea spray and crushed stone. There's a swell of biscuity oak on the palate that meshes nicely with the peach and citrus fruits, an appealing tension and clarity to the interplay between fruit and acidity and a finish that flares and lingers nicely. Drink by 2031.
93+ Points
Dave Brookes - James Hallidays Australian Wine Companion

entry.title: 2025 3 Drops Riesling
entry.summary:
Zippy and taut with a long driving finish.

Brilliant water like colour with green tinted edges. Pronounced lemon and lime aromas are trailed by wet steel and chalky mineral like notes. Zippy lime, lemon and Granny Smith apple fruits cast a racy feel across the palate. Crisp laser like acidity with wet steel and chalky mineral elements lingering through the long, driving yet taut finish.
Drink over the next 6-8 years.
Alc. 13%

Other Reviews.
As I shoved my generously framed nose into this glass of 3 Drops Riesling, a smile arose from deep inside. It. Smells. Delicious. Lemon sorbet, grapefruit juice and musk sticks. The concentration of fruit and perfumed florals scream plump cheeks, cheekiness and reckless confidence. In the mouth, theres a great line of acid and vibrancy, cocooned in a pithy texture. The flavour is packed in: lime sherbet, pomelo and all the pith. Theres even a surprising pickled radish note to the finish. Germany comes to mind. It will put a spring in your step. Drink with a hot-girl dinner of carbs and laughs. Drink 2026-2034.
93 Points
Cyndal Petty WinePilot.com

The spicy lemon rind aromatics are immediately striking in this positively exquisite riesling from the Great Southern. Three Drops has emerged as one of the best producers of this variety, and in a good season like this, it has really excelled. Its fine and crisp, with a typically linear line carrying through to a very long finish. Crunchy, spicy minerality on the palate with a nice lick of acid to close. Super wine.
95 Points
RayJordanWine.com.au

entry.title: 2022 Paringa Estate The Paringa Pinot Noir
entry.summary:
Powerful and expansive with a gorgeous supple flow and a long, moreish conclusion.

Dark red in colour with black toned edges and a red to dark red tinged hue. Intense red to dark cherry, violet, strawberry and anise aromas flood the nostrils followed by some rhubarb, brambly cedar, dried herb, forest floor and spice notes. Powerful and expansive, cascading waves of rich dark cherry, strawberry and anise flavours engulf the mouth. Subtle rhubarb, brambly cedar, spicy dried herb and forest floor elements unfold across the back half to lend further complexity. Gorgeously supple in its flow, it has velvet like tannins and a long, moreish conclusion.
Drink over the next 5-6 years.
Alc. 13.5%

entry.title: 2024 Mollydooker The Boxer Shiraz
entry.summary:
Rich, dense and thick with a long decadent, liqueur like finish.

Sourced from McLaren Vale and Langhorne Creek the flamboyant Boxer Shiraz is famed for its massive fruit weight, voluptuous texture and decadent richness. Maturation took place in 100% American oak of which 40% was new and the rest one year old.
Impenetrable inky black colour with a deep dark red black tinged hue. Heady dark to black plum and ripe blackberry scents waft from the glass followed by some vanillin oak, dark chocolate and subtle mint notes. Rich, dense and thick, the voluptuous palate is doused in dark plum, liquorice and blackberry fruits. Toasty vanillin oak, subtle earthy dark chocolate and fennel elements lurk underneath. Concentrated and powerful it has velvet smooth tannins and a long decadent, liqueur like finish.
Drink over the next 4-5 years.
Alc. 15.5%

entry.title: Hellyers Road Distillery Richly Peated 9 Year Old Single Malt Australian Whisky (700ml)
entry.summary:
Crafted from barley peated to 45-55 ppm, then matured in first-fill American oak ex-bourbon barrels sourced from Heaven Hill. Initially more fruity than smoky on the nose (apple and elderflower), otherwise a very successful, Highland-inspired drier-styled peater. Cocoa and bitter dark chocolate abound, alongside wood smoke, hints of mezcal, a burst of sweet oak and citrus. The oily, well-tuned finish continues the theme with subtle barbecue char through the aftertaste. Very tasty. 48.3% Alc./Vol. Non-chill-filtered.

Notes from the producers... Nose: Meaty, smoky and satisfying. Speck, fresh herbs, lemon zest and honey. Palate: Sweet campfire smoke, coastal green lichen, and damp bark. Distinctly Tasmanian. A sweet mid palate, toffee apple and citrus zest before a classical peat crescendo. Finish: Medium length with persistent salinity.
